We find that the GaV$^-$, created through FIB implantation and high-pressure high-temperature annealing, exhibits a combination of the best properties of both the NV$^-$ and G4V's: optically-detectable spin coherence at room temperature ($T_2(293K) = 1.06 μ$s), a large Debye-Waller factor $\sim$0.4, a short radiative lifetime ($\sim$3.83 ns), strong temperature dependence of the zero-field splitting (16x that of the NV$^-$), and charge-noise-protected D$_{3d}$ symmetry. These features (along with improved performance at low temperature) position the newly discovered GaV$^-$ as a key resource for quantum sensing, networking, and computation.

papers.title: On the reduction of GAP Conjecture to certain classes of groups and around
papers.abstract: In this note we revise our approach from [Rostislav Grigorchuk. On the gap conjecture concerning group growth. Bull. Math. Sci., 4(1):113--128, 2014] to the reduction of the Gap Conjecture on Group Growth to the class of just-infinite groups. For this purpose we introduce the class of groups that we call \emph{(GAPSY)} as well as some other classes. The properties of these classes are discussed in the relation with growth, elementary amenability, and just-infiniteness. Additionally, we discuss the GAP type problems for cancellative semigroups. A number of (old and new) open problems and few historical remarks is included in the note as well.

papers.title: On Ignorability Beyond Missing at Random: Completion-Invariant Missingness for Nonmonotone Missing Data
papers.abstract: The missing-at-random assumption underlies most analyses of incomplete data. Under nonmonotone missingness, it is especially stringent, imposing pattern-specific restrictions with different conditioning sets. A strictly weaker normalization condition is known to justify maximizing the observed-data likelihood. We show that every law satisfying this condition has a unique missing-at-random counterpart sharing its observed-data and complete-data distributions. Observed-data procedures developed under missing at random for identified functionals, including doubly robust estimators, therefore remain valid, with the same semiparametric efficiency bound. We then prove that the condition holds if and only if filling in the missing values from their conditional distribution under the true full model preserves the complete-data distribution, hence the name completion-invariant missingness. We use a characteristic kernel to compare the completed distribution with the fitted model and assess the joint compatibility of the specified full model and completion-invariant missingness. We derive the asymptotic null distribution with estimated parameters and establish bootstrap and multiplier calibration. Since a parametric full model alone need not identify completion-invariant missingness, we give identification conditions for Gaussian, Student $t$ and finite mixture families. Simulations assess sensitivity to departures from each assumption, and applications to clinical laboratory measurements and childhood growth illustrate the diagnostic.

papers.title: Auslander-Reiten relations and local finiteness in extriangulated categories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Hom-finite Krull--Schmidt extriangulated category over a commutative artin ring. Write ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)$ for the subgroup of the split Grothendieck group generated by the relations of all $\mathbb E$-triangles, and ${\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$ for the subgroup generated by those coming from Auslander--Reiten $\mathbb E$-triangles. We first prove that either one-sided finiteness condition on Hom supports implies ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)={\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$. For incoming Hom supports, the proof uses a Jordan--Hölder filtration of the contravariant defect. The outgoing case follows by duality. This gives a new proof of the implication from local finiteness to generation by Auslander--Reiten relations. Our argument uses defects and induction on their composition length. In this way, it avoids the radical filtration argument used by Zhu and Zhuang. We then sssume that $\mathcal C$ has enough projectives and injectives, and prove that $\mathcal C$ is locally finite if and only if its projective and injective subcategories are locally finite, the Euler functions associated with Auslander--Reiten relations have finite support, stable and costable morphisms detect ordinary morphisms away from the projective and injective boundary, and ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)={\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$. Our results recover the classical module and triangulated cases. They also explain why the two one-sided support conditions are equivalent in the triangulated setting, but may differ in a general extriangulated category.

papers.title: Strong error estimates for finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with strong error estimates for fully discrete finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise. We use the implicit Euler--Maruyama scheme for time discretization and continuous piecewise linear finite elements for spatial discretization. Moment bounds and exponential integrability estimates are established and used with the discrete stochastic Gronwall inequality to derive error estimates in full expectation. Sub-second-moment error estimates are first obtained in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm and the discrete $L^2$-in-time $H^1$-norm. Second-moment error estimates in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm are then established using a higher-moment argument. The convergence rates are of order $k^{1/2}$ in time and $h$ in space, with the spatial rate being optimal in the $H^1$-norm. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to examine the convergence rates and the influence of multiplicative noise on the solution.

papers.title: A geometric characterization of weighted homogeneity for reduced complex analytic germs
papers.abstract: We prove that a reduced complex analytic germ is weighted homogeneous if and only if, in suitable local coordinates, it admits a holomorphic vector field vanishing at the origin and pointing strictly outward along a single sufficiently small link. On a connected link, transversality suffices. The criterion applies in arbitrary codimension, including to non-isolated singularities. The proof uses a compact composition operator to control the spectrum on the Zariski tangent space and obtains a positive grading from the resulting spectral condition.

papers.title: The graph $a$-Turán theorem
papers.abstract: We prove analogues of Turán's theorem and the Erdős--Stone theorem for graph $a$-numbers. The $i$th $a$-number $a_i(G)$ equals the $i$th rational Betti number of the real toric manifold associated with the graph associahedron of $G$. We show that the Turán graph $T_r(n)$ maximizes every $a$-number among $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices. We also show that for any fixed graph $H$ with at least one edge and each fixed $i\geq1$, the limiting extremal density of the $i$th $a$-number among $H$-free graphs depends only on the chromatic number of $H$. Since $a_1(G)$ is the number of edges of $G$, these results recover the two classical theorems in degree one and extend them to higher $a$-numbers.

papers.title: $(r,s)$-Designs in the Nonbinary Johnson Scheme: Constructions and Linear Codes
papers.abstract: Using factorizations of complete graphs, we determine the existence conditions for $(2,1)$-designs in the nonbinary Johnson scheme where each $3$-element subset appears exactly once as a support. Furthermore, by utilizing large sets of Steiner triple systems, we construct designs with index $1$ that cannot be obtained from the known construction combining block designs and orthogonal arrays. For linear codes, we express multiplicative character sums over specified nonzero coordinates as sums over the codewords of the dual code. Using this identity along with the rank of a matrix formed by Krawtchouk polynomials, we provide a sufficient condition for the set of all codewords of a given weight to form an $(r,s)$-design. In this matrix, we can utilize not only the rows corresponding to weights absent from the code, but also the rows corresponding to weights for which the set of codewords already forms a design. Moreover, let $q>2$ be a prime power, and let $0 \neq C \subsetneq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code with exactly two nonzero weights. For $t \geq 2$, the set of all codewords of weight $w \geq t$ forms a non-empty $(t,t)$-design if and only if the dual minimum distance is at least $t+2$. Consequently, this provides a negative answer to the Wu--Zhou problem concerning two-weight codes with a dual minimum distance of $3$.

papers.title: Stationary Phase along Rays and the Determinant of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
papers.abstract: We study the top-weight sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of linearly constrained Kloosterman sums over finite fields of odd characteristic, of rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$. A local Fourier-transform analysis describes wild monodromy at infinity along rays through nonescaping critical points and their quadratic characters, giving explicit Swan conductors and the escape locus. The resulting stationary-phase description yields a ray-theoretic proof of the geometric determinant. A reflection pairing and a Frobenius calculation at the tame endpoint recover the arithmetic determinant $\det\mathcal W_n\simeq\mathcal L_ψ(-2^{n-1}λ^{-1}\sum_i h_i)\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell(-(n+1)r(n)/2)$. We obtain reciprocity for exterior-power Frobenius traces, the exact distribution of normalized determinants, and spectral compression on symmetric loci. Assuming the ambient connected-monodromy theorem from companion work, we determine the monodromy of the geometric generic ray. Further results include bounds for complete exponential sums, conductor identities for selected parameter curves, and the Euler characteristic of the parameter torus. Rank-two boundary conormal calculations are separated from higher-codimension characteristic-cycle recursions, which remain conditional on explicit microlocal hypotheses.

papers.title: Antipodal paths: a short proof by counting intersections
papers.abstract: We give a short elementary proof of Norine's antipodal-coloring theorem: every red--blue edge coloring of a hypercube in which antipodal edges have opposite colors contains a monochromatic path joining antipodal vertices.

papers.title: A Lower-envelope Eikonal Neural Operator
papers.abstract: We propose the Lower-envelope Eikonal Neural Operator (LENO), a physics-informed neural operator for eikonal equations with heterogeneous velocity fields and general source sets. LENO encodes the variational minimum principle of viscosity solutions by constructing source-wise candidate fields and taking their pointwise minimum. This lower-envelope structure enforces the source condition exactly and represents nonsmooth multi-source solutions without a soft boundary penalty. The model is trained without precomputed solution data, using a Godunov upwind residual as the sole training signal. Experiments on point sources and curve sources, sample-dependent piecewise velocity fields, and OpenFWI CurveVel-A and Style-A media show accurate agreement with references of Fast Marching Method (FMM). Additional validation shows that the Godunov residual outperforms conventional finite difference residuals on a high-resolution test, that velocity conditioning and the lower-envelope transform are essential in realistic heterogeneous media, and that the trained operator supports efficient batched evaluation and resolution transfer.

papers.title: Fully Explicit Stabilized Runge--Kutta Methods for Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard Dynamics
papers.abstract: Stiff phase-field dynamics are typically solved by semi-implicit or fully implicit time discretizations, since the interfacial scales in the Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard equations impose severe step-size restrictions on standard explicit methods. In this paper, we investigate a different strategy based on stabilized Runge--Kutta solvers, in particular the Runge--Kutta--Legendre (RKL) and Runge--Kutta--Gegenbauer (RKG) families. These schemes possess enlarged stability regions and therefore provide a natural explicit framework for diffusion-dominated gradient flows without requiring implicit solves. For the Allen--Cahn equation, combined with Strang splitting, we establish a maximum principle in 1-dimensional case, and prove energy dissipation in all the dimensions. For the modified energy dissipation analysis, we further introduce two new first-order stabilized schemes of RKL and RKG type and derive a novel eigenvalue estimate for the second-order RKG method. We also conduct extensive numerical experiments with both constant and adaptive time stepping, on regular domains as well as on an L-shaped irregular domain. The numerical results show that stabilized explicit Runge--Kutta methods provide an effective and flexible approach for the numerical simulation of Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard dynamics while preserving key structural properties. The Python implementation is available at https://github.com/ZT220501/SRK-for-Gradient-Flows.

papers.title: Anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior driven by dichotomous Markov noise in a quantum Ising chain: Generalized stochastic resonance in the defect density
papers.abstract: The anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior may arise under noise, adding a noise-induced contribution to the defect density beyond the conventional Kibble-Zurek term. Most investigations of such behavior have so far been restricted to Gaussian noise. For Gaussian colored noise (GCN), the power spectrum dictates a monotonic variation of this term with the correlation time. Here, we focus on dichotomous Markov noise (DMN), a prototypical non-Gaussian colored noise, in the quantum Ising chain. We show that the noise-induced defect density, taken as the response function, exhibits generalized stochastic resonance: it is nonmonotonic in the correlation time, growing in the fast-noise regime and decreasing in the slow-noise regime. This resonance stems from the anomalous AKZ behavior in the slow-noise regime, where the DMN-induced trend is nonmonotonic, in contrast to the monotonic GCN case. The underlying mechanism lies in the sparse realizations of DMN in the slow-noise regime, a feature not captured by the power spectrum. Our work thereby reveals a fundamental distinction between Gaussian and non-Gaussian noises in the nonequilibrium critical quench dynamics of the quantum Ising chain.

papers.title: Beyond Curvature Bias: Higher-Order Manifold Fitting via Multiscale Cancellation
papers.abstract: Local manifold-fitting procedures smooth noisy observations over neighborhoods of scale $h$, inducing a systematic normal bias of order $h^2+σ^2$ that persists at the population level. We develop geometric bias cancellation (GBC), a multiscale framework for higher-order manifold recovery under ambient Gaussian noise. For procedures admitting a normal-bias expansion $c(h,σ)b(x)+O(h^4)$, we construct cross-scale correspondence using estimated normal fibers and show that second-order normal accuracy suffices for fourth-order correspondence accuracy. Canceling the leading geometric bias yields $O(h^4)$ population Hausdorff accuracy while preserving an embedded manifold diffeomorphic to the underlying manifold. We establish the required expansions and finite-sample recovery guarantees for successive tangent-space projection and Gaussian density ridges. For STSP, geometric bias cancellation also achieves an asymptotically vanishing Hausdorff error ratio relative to oracle bandwidth-tuned single-scale fitting. For the local contraction estimator of \citet{yao2023manifold}, we identify an obstruction to scalar bias cancellation and develop a directional cancellation achieving $O(σ^4)$ population Hausdorff accuracy with uniform positive reach, as well as fourth-order finite-sample accuracy when $n\gtrsimσ^{-(d+6)}\log(1/σ)$. Simulations confirm the predicted improvement from second- to fourth-order population bias.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Near-Maximizers of Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: For a centered Gaussian process $G$ with continuous sample paths on a compact metric space $T$, a continuous drift $f: T \mapsto \mathbb{R}$, a noise level $σ>0$, and $ε\ge 0$, let $A_ε$ be the set of points at which $f+σG$ is within $ε$ of its maximum. Writing $\mathbb{E}\sup_TG$ for the expected supremum of $G$, we prove that the expected squared diameter of $A_ε$ in the canonical pseudometric of $G$ is at most $8ε\mathbb{E}\sup_TG/σ$ and that the expected maximal squared distance from a point of $A_ε$ to an exact maximizer is at most $4ε\mathbb{E}\sup_TG/σ$. The constants cannot be improved uniformly over index sets, processes, and drifts, and no logarithmic factor in $ε$ appears, unlike in bounds integrated from tail estimates. At $ε=0$ the bounds give the almost sure uniqueness of the maximizer in the canonical pseudometric without nondegeneracy assumptions. Given this uniqueness, both bounds follow from a bound with constant $2$ on the mean square of the largest increment of an independent copy of $G$ from an exact maximizer to a point of $A_ε$. The proof rests on an identity for the mean squared support function of the $ε$-subdifferentials of a smooth convex function at a standard Gaussian vector, obtained from two Gaussian integrations by parts.

papers.title: A Polynomial Bound on Split Rank
papers.abstract: We prove that the split rank of a rational pure-integer polyhedron is polynomially bounded in its input length, resolving a conjecture of Basu, Conforti, Di Summa, and Jiang. If the defining system has dense binary encoding length $L$, then $O((L+1)^9)$ split rounds suffice to reach the integer hull in arbitrary dimension.

papers.title: On subgroup regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: A subset $D$ of the vertex set of a graph is called an $(a,b)$-regular set if each vertex in $D$ has exactly $a$ neighbors in $D$, and each vertex outside $D$ has exactly $b$ neighbors in $D$. A proper subgroup $H$ of $G$ is called an $(a,b)$-regular set of $(G,α)$ if it is an $(a,b)$-regular set of $GC(G,S,α)$ for some generalized Cayley subset $S$ of $G$ induced by the involutory automorphism $α$. This paper investigates subgroup $(0,b)$-regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs. We first obtain some necessary and sufficient conditions for a proper subgroup of a group $G$ to be a $(0,b)$-regular set of a generalized Cayley graph. In particular, we show that a proper normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ is a $(0,b)$-regular set of $(G,α)$ if and only if $H$ is a perfect code of $(G,α)$ for some odd integer $b,$ which generalizes the result in [F.S. Seiedali, Z. Akhlaghi, B. Khosravi. Generalized Cayley graphs and perfect code. Discrete Math. 2026]. Furthermore, for connected generalized Cayley graphs with $α$-normal generalized Cayley subsets, we characterize subgroup $(0,b)$-regular sets via equitable partitions.

papers.title: Fréchet Oblique Forest for Non-Euclidean Regression
papers.abstract: We propose Fréchet oblique forests (FOF) for non-Euclidean regression with predictors and responses in metric spaces. An Alexandrov inner-product score defines directional splits in metric predictor spaces and recovers ordinary oblique splits for Euclidean predictors. Candidate splits are evaluated through pairwise response distances, avoiding repeated Fréchet mean computations during split search. Forest predictions minimize a weighted Fréchet criterion obtained by averaging leaf weights across trees. For compatible tree rules, we establish integrated consistency and polynomial risk bounds under explicit approximation and entropy conditions. Simulations with matrices, distributions, spherical data and mixed predictors, together with an application to taxi-flow networks, demonstrate competitive predictive performance.

papers.title: A One-Sided Chord Trim of Wetzel's Sector Covers Unit Arcs
papers.abstract: Wetzel conjectured, and Panraksa and Wichiramala proved, that the circular sector of radius one and angle $30^\circ$ contains a congruent copy, reflections allowed, of every arc of length one. We show that half of its arc is not needed: replacing the arc between the angles $15^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ by its chord gives a convex cover of area $π/24+(\sqrt6-\sqrt2)/8=0.2603092\ldots$. As in the proof for the sector, we place an arc in two supporting wedges. A sum of support, cap and radial inequalities, with vector coefficients summing to zero, shows that an arc with no copy in the trimmed sector is longer than one. One two-parameter family of configurations is checked by rational interval arithmetic; programs and data are supplied. No chord that starts below $3.6^\circ$ gives a cover. We also reduce the inclusion-minimality of the trimmed sector to two families of cuts.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with squared Bessel arrival intensity
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a model for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with stochastic intensity given by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. The asymptotic properties of the model are also analysed. We establish laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, large deviation principles, and moderate deviation principles for several quantities of interest. More precisely, these results are obtained for three important settings: cumulative occupancy over a finite time interval, system occupancy under a diverging long-run mean arrival intensity, and the superposition of independent infinite-server queues with Cox-BESQ arrival intensities. Numerical experiments illustrate the associated rate functions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting rare-event approximations.

papers.title: Holomorphic Sectional Curvature of Flag Manifolds via Kähler Reduction
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of Li and Petersen's theorem that every invariant Kähler metric on a compact generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For a unitary partial flag manifold, we realize the given metric by Kähler reduction of a Hermitian vector space. The defining equations place the level set on a sphere of radius \varrho, where the radial component of its second fundamental form gives the explicit lower bound 4/\varrho2 through the quotient curvature formula. Finally, we use a holomorphic isometric totally geodesic embedding to transfer the bound to generalized flag manifolds of every Lie type.

papers.title: Null designs and switching in polynomial spaces
papers.abstract: Null designs are finite point configurations with real weights whose polynomial moments vanish up to a given degree. In Godsil's framework of polynomial spaces, we give elementary proofs of sharp lower bounds on the number of points in the Euclidean and spherical cases. We characterize the spherical null designs attaining the bound and give explicit formulas for their weights. We then study how null designs can be used to replace part of a weighted design while preserving its polynomial moments. We give conditions ensuring nonnegative weights and apply the minimum-size classification to switching on circles. Examples on spheres and in Hamming and Johnson spaces illustrate these results, including a replacement between noncongruent spherical $5$-designs that preserves equal weights and the number of points.

papers.title: Rational contractions in quasi-Banach spaces: convergence, multiplicity of fixed points and applications
papers.abstract: We study self-maps $f$ of a complete $b$-metric space $(U,d)$ (constant $b\ge1$) satisfying the rational contractive condition \[ d(fu,fv)\le\frac{d(u,fv)+d(v,fu)+κ}{b\,[d(u,fu)+d(v,fv)]+1}\,d(u,v)\qquad(u,v\in U), \] with $κ\in[0,1)$. We first observe that the two-parameter family of conditions studied in our earlier work reduces, after a rescaling of the $b$-metric, to this one-parameter form. We then prove: (A) every Picard sequence converges to a fixed point, with an explicit a~priori estimate whose geometric ratio depends only on $b$, $κ$ and $d(u_0,fu_0)$, an a~posteriori estimate, and asymptotic rate at most $κ$; (B) a structure theorem: such maps are automatically continuous, every fixed point attracts the whole ball of radius $(1-κ)/2$, distinct fixed points are at distance at least $(1-κ)/2$ (sharp), basins of attraction are clopen, and the number of fixed points does not exceed the number of connected components of $U$; in particular the fixed point is unique on connected spaces; (C) Ulam--Hyers stability of the fixed-point problem. The class of such maps is not invariant under passing from a quasi-norm to the equivalent $p$-norm metric, so the quasi-Banach results are not formal consequences of the metric ones. A gluing principle shows that the multiplicity permitted by (B) occurs. As applications we obtain existence, exact multiplicity and error estimates for infinite nonlinear systems with relay-type forcing in $\ell^p$, $0<p<1$, and for nonlinear perturbations of Volterra-type equations $f=\pm a+T_gf+ψ(f(z_0))k$ in the Hardy space $H^p$, $0<p<1$, where $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(ζ)g'(ζ)\,dζ$ and $g\in\BMOA$.

papers.title: Admissibility of unbounded complexes of smooth representations
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a $p$-adic Lie group and $k$ a field of characteristic $p$. We prove that a complex of smooth $k$-representations of $G$ has admissible cohomology if and only if it is globally admissible, i.e., its hypercohomology with respect to a torsion-free open compact pro-$p$ subgroup is finite dimensional in every degree. This extends the bounded-below and bounded-above comparison of Schneider--Sorensen to arbitrary unbounded complexes.

papers.title: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
papers.abstract: Gábor Czédli introduced congruence density and investigated how it changes under sublattice extensions. We prove that density cannot increase: if $S$ is a sublattice of a finite lattice $L$, then $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. We also determine when equality holds: $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ precisely when every element of $L\setminus S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of Czédli and Szabó relating quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding results for quasiorder density.

papers.title: Contiguity of unions of perfect matchings and random regular uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: For fixed integers $s\ge3$ and $r$ satisfying $\log(r!)>\frac{r(s-1)}s\log r$, the union of $r$ independent uniform perfect matchings of the complete $s$-uniform hypergraph is mutually contiguous to the uniform simple $r$-regular $s$-uniform hypergraph, as $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $s$. In particular, $r=\lceil e^s\rceil$ suffices. The main input is the sharp entropy inequality for random permutations of Bristiel and Caputo. It proves the global maximization needed for the second moment of the number of complete factorizations. The remaining calculation, including its lattice factor, matches the short-cycle contribution required by small-subgraph conditioning.\\ This is an expanded version of a proof provided by ChatGPT-Astra.

papers.title: the limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erdős problem 521
papers.abstract: We resolve Erdős Problem~521 by proving that the normalized real-root count $N_n/\log n$ of Rademacher polynomials almost surely has no limit. More generally, consider the Kac polynomials \[ P_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}ξ_jx^j \] with i.i.d.\ real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment. Let $N_n$ denote the number of distinct real roots of $P_n$. We prove that, almost surely, \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π+C_*, \] and the set of subsequential limits is exactly \[ \left[\frac1π,\;\frac1π+C_*\right]. \] Here $C_*>1/π$ is a constant uniquely determined by an equation. The lower-limit identity remains valid under the weaker assumption that $\mathbb{E}|ξ_0|^{2+δ}<\infty$ for some $δ>0$.

papers.title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
papers.abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $ζ(3), ζ(5), \dots, ζ(s)$, where $ζ$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.

papers.title: Conditional Gaussian Limits and Character Laws for Randomized Symmetric-Group Representations
papers.abstract: Let $ρ_n$ be a real orthogonal representation of the symmetric group $S_n$ of dimension $d_n\to\infty$, let $σ_n$ be a uniform random permutation, and let $O_n$ be an independent Haar-orthogonal matrix. We study the linear statistics $\operatorname{Tr}(A_nO_nρ_n(σ_n)O_n^T)$ for deterministic real test matrices $A_n$ normalized only in Frobenius norm, which allows tests that isolate individual entries. Conditionally on $σ_n$, the statistic has mean $s_nχ_n(σ_n)$, where $χ_n$ is the character of $ρ_n$ and $s_n=d_n^{-1}\operatorname{Tr} A_n\to s$. We show that the centered statistic has conditional Gaussian limit $N(0,1-s^2)$ for every such test if and only if the trivial and sign constituents of $ρ_n$ occupy $o(d_n)$ dimensions, and that this limit is asymptotically independent of every convergent $σ_n$-measurable observable. The key input is a tensor-square estimate, based on the Frobenius-Schur identity and the minimum degree of non-linear irreducible representations of $S_n$, which shows that this single condition controls both normalized traces needed in the Haar-conjugation argument. For the uncentered statistic, convergence in distribution of $χ_n(σ_n)$ to a law $Ξ$ is necessary and sufficient for every test statistic to converge to $sΞ+\sqrt{1-s^2}G$, with $G$ standard Gaussian and independent of $Ξ$. For every irreducible sequence with $d_n\to\infty$, finitely many entries scaled by $\sqrt{d_n}$ have independent standard Gaussian limits. Finally, we compute $Ξ$ explicitly for diagrams with a fixed first-row tail, their transposes, and diagrams with sublinear largest hook, answering in these cases a question of Tsou.

papers.title: Enumerating Pyranim Isomorphisms
papers.abstract: We study a Nim-adjacent poset game, where chips are arranged in a pyramid and two players take turns removing chips that do not currently support chips to the upper-left and upper-right; upon removing this chip, all supported chips above are also removed. Play continues until the final chip is removed. We use a bijection between the game states, Dyck paths, and unit interval graphs to count the number of possible game states up to isomorphism.

papers.title: Congruences Modulo 16, 32 and 64 for a Restricted Overpartition Function
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{t}^{(3)}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which consecutive parts differ by a multiple of $3$ unless the larger part is overlined, and the smallest part is overlined unless it is divisible by $3$. Using dissections of theta functions, we establish two infinite families of congruences modulo $32$ and $64$. We also obtain two residue formulas modulo $16$ and use them to derive four further infinite families of congruences modulo $16$. In particular, for every positive integer $M$ and nonnegative integer $n$, the residue of $\overline{t}^{(3)}(M^2(18n+12))$ modulo $16$ is $8$ if $6n+4$ is a square and $0$ otherwise.

papers.title: Fast circular convolution with periodic kernels
papers.abstract: We study the periodic circular convolution or PCC, where the convolution kernel depends periodically on the spatial location. We introduce two fast algorithms to compute the PCC that rely on the Discrete Fourier Transform. One of the algorithms reveals that the matrix representation of the PCC is unitarily equivalent to a block diagonal matrix, which facilitates the analysis of PCCs and operations such as their product and inversion. We present two sample applications. One to deconvolve the action of an optical system whose point spread function depends periodically in space. The second is to compute dispersion relations for a periodic chain of masses.

papers.title: Gradient Flows over Convex Bodies for Learning Optimal Regularizers
papers.abstract: We consider the question of describing gradient flows over the collection of convex bodies. This is motivated by foundational questions arising in inverse problems. Suppose we wish to solve an ill-posed inverse problem using regularization techniques. Can we learn an optimal choice of a convex regularizer directly from prior data? Given a numerical algorithm that computes such an optimal regularizer, is there a principled manner for describing the evolution of its iterates? The objective of this paper is to lay the foundation towards answering these questions. To this end, we consider a criterion of an optimal regularizer based on seeking a convex body that minimizes the expected gauge evaluation with respect to a prior data distribution subject to a volume constraint. The formulation is initially nonconvex, but admits hidden convexity by passing to its polar. We characterize the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions that certify global optimality. We also analyze the $L^2$-gradient flow as well as a minimizing movement scheme with the Hausdorff penalty. Our results show that the objective gap decays exponentially along the gradient flow and we obtain dimension-dependent rates for both the objective gap and distance to the optimal body for the Hausdorff scheme. Finally, we apply the KKT conditions to identify explicit optimal convex bodies. For data where the optimal nonconvex regularizer is the $\ell_p$-quasinorm, $p \in (0,1)$, the optimal convex regularizer is the volume-normalized $\ell_1$-ball. For data described by paired basis atoms, the optimal convex regularizer is the polar of a shifted zonotope.

papers.title: The lower boundary of the $\{K_2,K_{p},K_{q}\}$-profile
papers.abstract: We determine the asymptotically sharp minimum number of $q$-cliques that appear in any $n$-vertex graph with $γn^2$ edges and $δn^{p}$ $p$-cliques for $q>p>2$. The question of determining the minimum number of $r$-cliques that appear in any $n$-vertex graph with $γn^2$ edges was previously resolved by Razborov for $r=3$, Nikiforov for $r=4$ and Reiher for all $r\geq 5$. For all $r\geq 3$, the minimum is attained by a complete multipartite graph where all parts are equal except for one that can be smaller or by a limit of such graphs. Very recently, Ma, Wang and Zhu as well as Li, Liu and Zhang showed that the same construction is also a minimizer for the number of $r$-cliques when the number of $s$-cliques is fixed for any $2\leq s<r$. A minimizer in our setting is the disjoint union of the same complete multipartite graph with an independent set. This establishes the lower boundary of the three-dimensional $\{K_2, K_p, K_q\}$-profile.

papers.title: Quantization of Betti Mapping Stacks
papers.abstract: We describe a quantization procedure for Betti mapping stacks with shifted Poisson targets by combining factorization homology and formal geometry. We quantize derived stacks of local systems of low-dimensional manifolds.

papers.title: Almost unimodular quantum groups
papers.abstract: We define a locally compact quantum group $\mathbb{G}$ to be almost unimodular if its modular element is diagonalizable. This is shown to be equivalent to the almost periodicity of a novel weight on the dual von Neumann algebra, which we call the middle Haar weight. The point modular spectrum of this weight is related to the point spectrum of $δ$, and we prove that unimodularity of $\mathbb{G}$ is equivalent to traciality of this weight. When $δ$ is affiliated with the center of $L^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, we show that there is a canonical closed, normal, unimodular quantum subgroup $\mathbb{G}_1 \leq \mathbb{G}$ which assumes the role of the unimodular part of $\mathbb{G}$, and moreover the openness of this quantum subgroup is equivalent to the almost periodicity of $\mathbb{G}$. Additionally, we establish several permanence properties of almost unimodularity.

papers.title: A global rigidity criterion for Coxeter $3$-polytopes
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial condition ensuring global projective rigidity of simple hyperbolic Coxeter $3$-polytopes. As an application, we prove that every right-angled Löbell polytope is globally rigid.

papers.title: Maximum Principles and Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the validity of the maximum principle and the existence of a principal eigenvalue for a problem involving two regions, in one of them the main operator is the classical Laplacian (a local operator) while in the other region the operator is a nonlocal one (these regions are coupled via a transmission term that is also nonlocal). The main difficulty here comes from the lack of compactness of the nonlocal part that occurs since we are considering non-singular kernels.

papers.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the integers form a Diophantine subset of the rational numbers. More precisely, there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[T,W_1,\dots,W_n]$ of total degree at most four such that $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ is an integer if and only if $P(q,\mathbf w)=0$ for some $\mathbf w\in\mathbb{Q}^n$. Consequently, any recursively enumerable subset of $\mathbb{Q}^r$ is Diophantine, and Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points fails. The proof is inspired by OpenAI's work on Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$. It does not use the $2$-converse or the $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and employed by OpenAI. We define the rational numbers with square denominator using rational points on certain quadratic twists of the congruent number elliptic curve. The criterion of Tian, Yuan and Zhang, in Smith's formulation, implies that these quadratic twists have analytic rank one. A height estimate for rational points on a fixed quotient of a Shimura curve allows us to express multiplication of elliptic-curve indices. We obtain this estimate by bounding the modular levels of the associated quaternionic abelian surfaces. The level bound is based on a compatible system of Galois representations over $\mathbb{Q}$ with controlled ramification and on Khare--Wintenberger's proof of Serre's conjecture. Green--Tao--Ziegler's theorem on linear patterns of primes supplies the rational solutions needed for a Diophantine model of integer arithmetic.

papers.title: On classifying knotted surfaces
papers.abstract: These notes, which are based on four lectures delivered at the summer school "Knotted Surfaces in Four-Manifolds" at PCMI in 2026, discuss classifications of locally flat surfaces in simply-connected $4$-manifolds.

papers.title: Quantum Control
papers.abstract: Quantum Control is the art of steering the fragile dynamics of a quantum system in a precise way toward a desired final state or transformation. It is a cornerstone of many quantum technology applications and at the same time allows us to shed light on the fundamental connection between the energy structure and the time dynamics of quantum systems at the heart of some of the most interesting phenomena of quantum mechanics. In this chapter on quantum control, we introduce the control problem, go through basic error sources and methods to suppress these errors and then discuss state-of-the-art techniques to solve the control problem, like adiabatic methods, quantum optimal control and methods of machine learning.

papers.title: Phase Interference and Transverse Catalysts Govern the Noise Fragility of Long-Range Variational Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Long-range entangling gates shorten variational state preparation, but they also accelerate operator spreading across the register, linking nonlocality to a presumed noise fragility. Here we show that the single-fault fragility $F$ of a variational circuit is governed by how fault phases interfere on the target Hamiltonian, not by how far faults spread. For Heisenberg chains we prove that two faults with identical extensive support can incur either bounded or extensive energy damage, in the exact ratio $N/2$. A phase-matched longitudinal halo remains energetically dark until ignited by transverse catalysts that break a symmetry of the remote register, namely spatially nonuniform single-qubit rotations or the pair-flip component of two-qubit $XX/YY$ gates, whereas uniform rotations and magnetization-conserving exchange gates leave it strictly dark. In noisy training with full-width long-range $ZZ$ gates, suppressing either catalyst alone leaves circuits trapped on an ignited plateau sustained by remote $XY$ couplings, whereas suppressing both eliminates the plateau, achieves minimal fragility despite larger fault operators, and halves the dephasing error. Training is driven by a race between catalyst pruning and gradient force balance, as annealing the transverse catalysts out of trapped circuits rescues every trajectory while annealing the entire longitudinal sector does not. Combined with the gate-count exposure $λ=pK$, a single fragility measurement accurately predicts the noise-induced energy shift across circuit architectures and noise strengths, reducing ansatz design to a trade-off between coherent expressivity and gate count.

papers.title: Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends
papers.abstract: We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.

papers.title: Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $G=F\rtimes_φ\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $φ$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece. Otherwise, the distortion of $H$ is quadratic if all dilation homomorphisms are trivial, and exponential if one of them is nontrivial. Along the way, we show that the distortion of $H$ is determined, up to superadditive closure, by the distortions of the stabilizers of its horizontal components.

papers.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
papers.abstract: We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$. At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques. Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.

papers.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
papers.abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,α): x\in U, α\in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),α(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

papers.title: Convergence rates for truncated and discretised signature expansions
papers.abstract: Linear expansions in Brownian Stratonovich signatures, which originate in stochastic Taylor expansions, are increasingly used to represent and model processes with memory. Their numerical use requires truncating the signature at a level $M$ and discretising the driving path along $N$ steps. Under a simple growth condition on the coefficients of the linear expansion, we establish strong and weak convergence rates for both approximations, uniformly in time. The strong truncation error decays like $(B^M/(M!)^\varepsilon)^a$ for some constant $B$, uniformly in $N$, where $\varepsilon$ measures the growth of the coefficients and $a$ the regularity of the test function; the weak error does not improve on it. The discretisation error is of order $N^{-a/2}$ in $L^p$, and $N^{-1}$ weakly for polynomial test functions, uniformly in $M$. All these rates are sharp for polynomial test functions, and $M$, $N$ can be chosen independently. We extend the estimates to errors in probability, on distribution functions and on risk measures, and illustrate them on stochastic delay equations, Volterra processes and option pricing in signature volatility models.

papers.title: Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
papers.abstract: A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.

papers.title: An Optimized Expansion Auction Integrating Energy, Flexibility, and Network Constraints
papers.abstract: Auction mechanisms are widely used to support generation investments. In the US, capacity auctions serve as supply-adequacy instruments to address the missing-money problem, whereas in Latin America, energy and capacity auctions procure long-term contracts to support generation expansion. In both settings, accreditation metrics, such as Firm Energy (FE) and Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), are used to approximate the reliability contribution of selected units and winning projects are selected based on a financial offer. This approach fails to recognize the actual contribution of winners to the multiple services they provide to the system. This limitation becomes more significant with high shares of renewables, as the value of each resource increasingly depends on network and technological constraints, as well as on complementarities within the generation portfolio. Inspired by short-term auctions, such as day-ahead markets, this paper proposes a joint optimization-based auction for generation and transmission investments that internalizes these interactions, capturing the intrinsic value of generation candidates without requiring the computation of FE or ELCC metrics. The auctioneer determines the winning portfolio through an expansion-planning model that explicitly represents network constraints, operational interactions, reliability standards, and multiple scenarios. A case study of the Brazilian system indicates lower system costs, lower risk, and a more diverse portfolio relative to the stylized decoupled procurement approaches currently deployed in many systems.

papers.title: TGen-SQD: Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) avoids iterative variational circuit optimization, but its accuracy and cost depend on selecting a compact determinant subspace that captures the ground state. Existing machine-learning selectors use task-specific physical cues and typically retrain for each Hamiltonian. We introduce TGen-SQD, a physics-informed generator jointly trained across multiple Hamiltonians. It learns from configuration-interaction-weighted data and uses orbital- and system-level descriptors to guide generation. After training, its weights remain frozen for inference on seen and zero-shot geometries. On a 20-qubit H10 chain, TGen-SQD achieves mean energy errors of 40.18 +/- 1.52 and 43.97 +/- 1.20 mHa on seen and unseen geometries, respectively, 12.7% and 11.7% lower than the state-of-the-art PIGen-SQD baseline under matched shot and proposal budgets.

papers.title: Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted étale groupoid model
papers.abstract: We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal étale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
papers.abstract: We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=Γ(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{π^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $λ$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $λ$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT). We indicate several avenues for further investigation.

papers.title: Mapping the High-Field Response of Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors
papers.abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) are increasingly being integrated into cryogenic quantum-sensing platforms that operate in large magnetic fields. Here, the high-field limits of these measurements were probed by characterizing the dark count response of a NbTiN SNSPD at up to 14~T using in situ control of the detector orientation and benchmarking that performance against normal detector operation in smaller magnetic fields. The detector performance is strongly anisotropic: perpendicular magnetic fields rapidly reduce the usable bias-current range, whereas near-parallel alignment enables operation at substantially larger total fields, with a finite operating margin retained to 12~T and measurable dark-count response at the 14~T field limit. The angular dependence is governed predominantly by the perpendicular component of the magnetic field, consistent with vortex-mediated suppression of the superconducting current scale. The same field-dependent current scale also determines the electrical pulse amplitude, linking high-field detector operation directly to readout performance. These results establish a practical route for deploying SNSPDs in multi-tesla quantum-sensing and high-field cryogenic experiments.

papers.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
papers.abstract: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

papers.title: Rigid Theories
papers.abstract: A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.

papers.title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
papers.abstract: Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(α)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. Utilizing the higher order Fourier analysis machinery of Green and Sawhney in their breakthrough work on the Gaussian prime conjecture, we show that if there are no local obstructions, then there are infinitely many $(x,y)\in \mathbb Z$ such that $L_1(x,y),\dots,L_k(x,y),$ and $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(x+yα)$ are simultaneously prime. We further establish an asymptotic formula which matches the prediction by the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture. We present two arithmetic applications of this prime counting result. First, we show that the Brauer--Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to weak approximation on a new family of varieties, including diagonal conic bundles all of whose degenerate fibres are defined over $\mathbb Q$ except one fibre that may be defined over an imaginary quadratic field. Second, we construct elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with infinitely many quadratic twists of rank exactly two.

papers.title: Triply conservative schemes for degenerate convection-dispersion equations
papers.abstract: It is well known that for numerically solving hyperbolic conservation laws, even a convergent numerical scheme still may not always converge to a weak solution. The remedy is the famous Lax-Wendroff theorem. In a recent work on degenerate convection-diffusion equations, an analogous phenomenon was identified and doubly conservative schemes were introduced. In this paper, we address the same issue for solving the following nonlinear degenerate dispersive or convection-dispersion equations: \begin{equation*} u_t+f(u)_x+A(u)_{xxx}=0. \end{equation*} The resulting equation is regarded as degenerate if $A'(u)$ is allowed to vanish. An important example is the Rosenau-Hyman $K(m,n)$ equation. In contrast to classical KdV solitons possessing exponentially decaying tails, $K(m,n)$ equations can admit compactly supported solitary waves, known as compactons, whose regularity can deteriorate at the boundary of their support. We first give an example in which both a classical conservative and doubly conservative scheme converges to a limit that fails to satisfy the ultra-weak formulation. To address this issue, we introduce the notion of a triply conservative (TriC) scheme and prove a Lax-Wendroff type theorem for consistent TriC schemes. Under suitable assumptions, a convergent sequence generated by a consistent TriC scheme will converge to an ultra-weak solution. Several existing high-order schemes are shown to have a TriC structure. We further introduce a new high-order TriC finite volume scheme based on a connection between triple cell averages and quadratic B-splines. The theory and the scheme are also suited for two-dimensional anisotropic problems and non-uniform meshes. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions confirm the high-order accuracy on smooth solutions and illustrate the behavior of the schemes for compactons and traveling fronts.

papers.title: Counterexample to Flow-Transfer Conjectures
papers.abstract: An edge map $f:E(G)\to E(H)$ between graphs is called an $FT_M$ map if the pullback of every $M$-tension on $H$ is an $M$-flow on $G$; equivalently, the pullback of every $M$-valued 1-coboundary is an $M$-valued 1-cycle. The correspondence between restricted tensions and homomorphisms to Cayley graphs motivates two flow analogues. An $(M,B)$-flow (or tension), is an $M$-flow (resp. $M$-tension) taking values in $B$. For subsets $B=-B\subseteq M$ with $M$ an abelian group, Šámal conjectured that a graph admits an $(M,B)$-flow if and only if it admits an $FT_M$ map to the Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)$. DeVos conjectured that, whenever there is a graph homomorphism $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)\to\operatorname{Cay}(M',B')$, every graph admitting an $(M,B)$-flow also admits an $(M',B')$-flow. We prove that these conjectures are equivalent and give a counterexample using the Petersen graph.

papers.title: Floating Body Asymptotics via Fractal Strings
papers.abstract: Schütt and Werner associated an almost polygonal planar convex body with a decreasing convex sequence and obtained two-sided estimates for the area removed by its floating body. We reinterpret the gaps of the defining sequence as the lengths of a normalized fractal string. Our main result shows that the area deficit, that is, the difference between the area of the set and its floating body, is comparable to an integral transform of the inner tubular volume of this string. As a consequence, if the string has Minkowski dimension $D$, then the principal power exponent of the area deficit is $1-D/3$. We also derive refinements for regularly varying tube functions, establish a realization criterion extending the almost polygonal case of the theorem of Schütt and Werner, and discuss several examples. As an application, we obtain corresponding asymptotic rates for the expectations and variances of the missed area and the number of vertices of random polygons, including new intermediate behaviors between the classical polygonal and smooth cases.

papers.title: Your PID Is Already a Neural Network: Learning Its Gains with Only Three Weights and No Teacher
papers.abstract: A discrete PID controller is exactly a recurrent neural network, a classical state-space fact: a fixed linear memory of the running integral and the last error, read out by three trainable weights that map one-to-one to the PID gains. Networks with bounded hidden states, such as LSTMs of any width, only approximate it. Trained only on a one-step physical cost (the expected cost of one transition from a fixed state distribution), with no demonstrations, teacher controller, or known gains, the network solves a strongly convex least-squares problem, so gradient descent converges from any initialization to the unique one-step optimal PID gains; the limit network is that PID, with the same action on every error sequence. Partitioned regression then shows what extra capacity buys. Orthogonal residual features keep these gains and improve on the PID if and only if they correlate with the part of the optimal action outside the PID span. On a nonlinear second-order example the gap is 5.88% of the optimal PID cost, and 4.00% against PID with a bias; no controller can improve on PID by more on this objective. A residual started at a tuned PID begins exactly at that PID; at the one-step optimal PID, a fixed-feature residual's first gradient step lowers the cost if and only if its features can improve on the PID. Experiments confirm the realization, recovery, and gap results to numerical precision. On held-out plants of three families, under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, a residual warm-started at a heavily tuned PID and trained with it lowers the long-horizon cost by 3.5%, 3.5%, and 1.9%, with family-wise 95% bounds excluding zero, also under distribution shift; a post hoc comparison with the PID tuned alone suggests that most of it comes from the recurrent part in two families. The primary endpoint, a gain of at least 5% from a generic PID start, is not met in any family.

papers.title: Operator uncertainty and cross-domain information in quantum signals: Second-moment bounds for quantum waveform design
papers.abstract: We derive second-moment bounds for quantum waveform design by combining entropic uncertainty relations with the covariance description of continuous-variable systems. For any state with finite second moments and entropies, the mutual information between the arrival time and the transverse wave number, which are compatible observables from different canonical pairs, is bounded above by the logarithm of twice the smaller of the time-frequency and position-wave-number uncertainty products. We demonstrate that a Gaussian wave packet with a bilinear space-time phase saturates this bound for every admissible set of standard-deviation budgets, and that the bound therefore provides a necessary and sufficient condition for reaching a target information within the canonical model. For this state, the joint measurement of the arrival time and the transverse wave number is optimal among local Gaussian measurements, yields the Rényi-2 entropy of the reduced state, and attains the quantum Fisher information for the coupling at fixed input widths. We also show that, with additive detector noise, timing jitter limits the recorded information to a level set by the ratio of jitter to pulse duration. These results provide a framework for designing spatiotemporally coupled quantum signals, and we propose an optical realization based on pulse-front tilt and a lens.

papers.title: The Wasserstein cost of the Girsanov Theorem
papers.abstract: This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for Itô diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem. More precisely, let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the law of the solution of a stochastic differential equation with a bounded Lipschitz drift. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ be independent Brownian paths, and let $Z_i$ be their Girsanov weights for $\mathbb{Q}$. The reweighted empirical measure $$\widehatμ_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_iδ_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i}$$ approximates $\mathbb{Q}$ when $n$ is large. We prove that the Wasserstein cost $W_p^p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is of order $(\log n)^{-p/2}$, in expectation and almost surely, for every fixed $p\geqslant1$. In the Brownian case where $Z_i=1$ these results show that $\sqrt{\log n}W_p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is asymptotically sandwiched between $\sqrt{2λ_d}$ and $4\sqrt{2λ_d}$, where $λ_d$ is the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in the unit ball. We provide numerical experiments to estimate the (conjectured) limiting constant in dimension $d=1$.

papers.title: MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to stay positive in the expanding regime
papers.abstract: We study MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to remain positive for a long time when $|θ|>1$, where $θ$ denotes the coupling parameter. We show that, for a fixed starting point, the finite-dimensional distributions of the conditioned process converge and identify the limiting process as a Doob $h$-transform with explicit function $h$. We also obtain precise asymptotics for the corresponding persistence probabilities. The limiting process exhibits qualitatively different behaviour depending on $θ$ and on the support of the innovation distribution. We also determine stationary distributions of the limiting conditioned processes for all $θ\ne 1$.

papers.title: Tautological generation of preprojective BPS cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mathbf{d}$ be a dimension vector. We prove that the affinized BPS cohomology of the stack of $\mathbf{d}$-dimensional representations of the preprojective algebra $Π_Q$ is generated by its reduced virtual fundamental class under the action of tautological classes. This is a generalisation to singular quiver varieties of the Kirwan surjectivity statement of McGerty-Nevins for smooth framed quiver varieties. We prove that the statement holds for every King stability condition. To prove this, we attach legs to vertices of $Q$ and construct a correspondence with a smooth quiver variety for the extended quiver. This correspondence sends the reduced virtual fundamental class of the singular preprojective quiver stack to the Vandermonde determinant capped with the fundamental class of the smooth preprojective quiver stack for the leg-extended quiver. We construct the Weyl group action by the simultaneous Springer resolution of Dobrovolska-Ginzburg-Travkin, providing a comparison of the cohomology of fibres. This comparison preserves the tautological Chern classes. The sign-isotypic formula involving Kac polynomials of Hausel-Letellier-Rodriguez-Villegas, combined with Kirwan surjectivity for smooth framed quiver varieties of McGerty-Nevins, then implies the tautological generation theorem. We also describe the sign isotypic component of the cohomology of quiver varieties using the real-root subalgebras of the BPS Lie algebra. The tautological generation result can be extended via similar methods to deformed preprojective algebras of Crawley-Boevey-Holland at central parameters.

papers.title: Comparing grade restriction windows to Cox windows
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of toric varieties which admit an HKKN stratification compatible with the combinatorics of the GKZ fan. This class includes all smooth projective toric varieties of Picard ranks 1 and 2. We show that the grade restriction windows due to Halpern-Leistner and Ballard--Favero--Katzarkov arising from our HKKN stratifications agree with the intrinsic window categories appearing in work of Ballard--Berkesch--Brown--Cranton Heller--Erman--Favero--Ganatra--Hanlon--Huang. On the other hand, we provide an example of a smooth projective toric DM stack where this intrinsic window is never a grade restriction window despite the many possible choices. As an application, we demonstrate that reordering and/or taking a subset of an HKKN stratification sometimes changes the grade restriction window and sometimes does not.

papers.title: Formal completions and decompositions of matrix factorization categories of Fano mirrors
papers.abstract: We study the derived categories of matrix factorizations for certain toric Landau--Ginzburg models that are mirror dual to del Pezzo surfaces and Fano threefolds. Some of these models have non-isolated singularities: their critical loci may contain curves and surfaces, possibly with intersecting irreducible components. We handle these cases by studying the potential in the formal neighborhood of each irreducible component of the critical locus. Away from $\operatorname{Sing}(\operatorname{CritLoc}(W)_{\mathrm{red}})$, we construct global formal coordinates and determine the local normal form of the singularity. Near the singular or intersection strata, we analyze how the pieces of the whole connected formal neighborhood are related by localization. This gives explicit decompositions of the derived categories of matrix factorizations after idempotent completion. For the five rank-one pairs $(B_d,V_{4d+2})$, we also compare projective compactifications. The isolated sectors and central-component counts agree for $d=2,3,4,5$ and differ for $d=1$. Equivalence of the distinguished compactified contributions for the remaining matched pairs requires compatible global gluing data or compactified Homological Mirror Symmetry.

papers.title: Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras
papers.abstract: We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius. This settles a question of Hernandez--Walton--Yadav and unifies a wealth of results in the literature. We conclude with applications to topological quantum field theories and Poincaré duality algebras.

papers.title: On the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
papers.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

papers.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
papers.abstract: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.

papers.title: Generic unipotent representations of finite reductive groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a generic reductive group in the sense of Broué--Malle--Michel. We construct a category over $\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}]$ which interpolates between the various categories of unipotent representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ as we specialize $t$ to $q$. We use this category to show two properties of the unipotent decomposition matrix of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ mod $\ell$ (not dividing $q$): that, uniformly in $(q,\ell)$, there are finitely many such matrices and that for $\ell$ large enough, depending only on $\mathbb{G}$, this decomposition matrix depends only on the root of unity corresponding to $q$ mod $\ell$. We also prove that for $q$ and $q'$ two prime powers that are $\ell$-adically close enough, the categories of unipotent mod $\ell$ representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(q')$ are equivalent.

papers.title: Zero detection via Cox random measures
papers.abstract: Using point process theory we propose and investigate a probabilistic identification of zeros of a deterministic real valued function. We construct a random atomic driving measure for a Cox point process whose mass at a candidate location depends explicitly on the value of the function at that location. We study the properties of the constructed random measure, including its exact asymptotic properties, its Laplace functional and related random processes. We also give an important application involving zero detection for Riemann's ξ function.

papers.title: Invariant random compacts for $\times p, \times q$ on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove that for multiplicatively independent natural numbers $p,q \ge 2$, if $μ$ is a Borel probability measure on the space $\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{T})$ of nonempty compact subsets of the circle $\mathbb{T}$ which is invariant under the induced actions of both multiplication by $p$ and $q$, and $μ$-a.e. $Y$ has positive Hausdorff dimension, then $μ$-a.e. $Y$ is equal to $\mathbb{T}$.

papers.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
papers.abstract: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(σ)$ to $L^q(ω)$ for the operator $H_σg(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,dσ$, where $σ$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $ω$ is a $σ$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $κ_{p,q}$ in $C_*\leκ_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $ω$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Osękowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.

papers.title: Blow-up rate for 1-d semilinear wave equations without scaling invariance at characteristic points
