We give a unified proof of stability for every $p\ge2$ with the optimal dimension-free sub-Gaussian rate, linking the reweighting, trimming and truncation techniques of the outlier and heavy-tailed robust literatures through concentration of counting and truncation processes. Building on stability and spectral signatures, we quantify the optimization landscape over sample weights that remove at most a fraction $\varepsilon_{n,k}=k/n$ of the mass, where the trimming parameter $k$ slightly exceeds the number of outliers. An unobserved convex spectral loss has inexact quadratic growth, with curvature $\frac{1-\varepsilon_{n,k}}{\varepsilon_{n,k}}$, relative to a mean-induced Bregman divergence, and the observable spectral loss supplies a dimension-free, inexact, relatively weakly star-convex subgradient oracle for it. This yields a Lyapunov analysis of mirror descent reweighting for $\varepsilon_{n,k}<\frac13$ that covers Hedge, the projected subgradient method, a new mean-induced mirror descent, and a centered multiplicative weights update. Each method uses one top-eigenvector computation per step and attains the optimal sub-Gaussian rate without knowledge of $(p,ν_p)$. Mean-induced mirror descent further achieves faster optimization rates and last-iterate guarantees, at the cost of a more expensive projection step in higher dimensions.

papers.title: Remarks on the BKM criterion for both classical and variable Euler systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish new results on BKM-type criteria for the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ as well as the Euler equations with space-time variable coefficients in a bounded domain. Our first result shows that if a finite-energy solution to the Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ blows up at a time $T_\ast$, and $T_\ast$ is the first such time, then $\limsup_{t\to T_\ast^-}(T_\ast -t)^{1+2k/5}\|D^kω(t)\|_{L^\infty} = \infty$ for every $k \geq 1$, thereby excluding the endpoint rate allowed by previously established lower bounds. The proof assumes the endpoint rate as an upper bound near the blowup time and uses a result by Chae and Wolf to obtain a contradiction. The second result gives a BKM-type criterion for solutions to the incompressible Euler equations with variable coefficients in the minimal regularity class $H^r$, where $r \in (2.5,3)$.

papers.title: Diffusion phenomena for evolution equations
papers.abstract: We study the diffusion phenomenon for the abstract damped wave equation $u''+Bu'+Au=0$ on a Banach space and its possibly degenerate parabolic counterpart $Bv'+Av=0$. We assume that $B$ is bounded and the wave equation is well-posed, without requiring symmetry, injectivity, or commutativity of $A$ and $B$. Our aim is to identify initial data for which the parabolic solution is a genuine diffusive profile: $\|u(t)-v(t)\|=o(\|v(t)\|)$ as $t\to\infty$. Using Fourier analysis of resolvent expressions for the associated quadratic and linear operator pencils, we establish decay estimates for the difference of hyperbolic and parabolic solutions and their time derivatives. In particular, we characterize broad classes of initial data yielding the classical upper bounds of orders $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$. We also prove lower bounds for both solutions, of the form $\|u(t)\|,\|v(t)\|\gtrsim r(t)$, for large sets of initial data and arbitrary prescribed functions $r(t)\to0$ that decay sufficiently slowly. Combining these results with high- and low-frequency resolvent estimates and a condition on the ranges of $A$ and $B$, we obtain genuine diffusive profiles. The analysis uses spectral properties of a sectorially holomorphic parabolic solution semigroup, which need not be strongly continuous. We apply the theory to damped wave equations on $L^2(Ω)$ with the Dirichlet Laplacian and bounded nonnegative damping that may vanish on large sets. We establish criteria for the required resolvent and range conditions, treat the whole space and exterior domains, and construct diffusive initial data using Weyl sequences.

papers.title: Relative divisors and intersections of noncommutative rational localizations
papers.abstract: The simple constituents of monic pencils determine singularity support in a free skew field. For a pencil inverse algebra that is a free ideal ring, the multiplicities of the nonbase constituents compute the scalar-regular part of Cohn's matrix divisor theory. For independent generic invertible matrices of size at least two, every entry of a nonidentity free-group word is an atom with one relative singularity component. In rank two, opposite pivots give the exact identifications among these components. Intersections of word-entry localizations are then given by intersections of their label sets. An irreducible pencil of dimension six represents a commutator entry. For an algebra finitely generated over the free polynomial algebra at a common regular scalar point, the residual closure is a finite pencil inverse algebra determined by the generators' common domain. Every nonzero inverse-adjoining defect is infinite-dimensional. We compute how free-group quotients change intersections and give additive formulas for general quotient and tensor intersections. We prove Berenstein--Retakh's polygon conjecture using $n-2$ charts for $n\geq4$. For an unpunctured Möbius strip with $n\geq2$ boundary marks, the upper-algebra equality follows from $n+1$ charts. For the once-marked strip, the allowed algebra is strictly smaller than its residual hull, which equals the full chart.

papers.title: Stability of Hilbert--Samuel functions with linear bounds in homological degree
papers.abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I$ be generated by a filter regular sequence. Set $A=R/I$, $s=\dim A>0$, and $D= \operatorname{hdeg}(A)$. If $A$ is equicharacteristic, we prove that perturbations of order $(2s+1)D$ preserve the Hilbert--Samuel function in every dimension. In arbitrary characteristic, we obtain the order $[s+(s+1)(k!)^{k-1}]D^k$, where $k$ is the maximum of $1$ and the dimensions of the lower deficiency modules of $\widehat A$. Both bounds depend only on the final quotient. The proof constructs monic annihilating equations for the deficiency modules and uses them to choose a parameter $d$-sequence with an explicit relation to a reduction of the maximal ideal. In the equicharacteristic case, a dimension filtration and characteristic polynomials over regular subrings give equations of degree at most the arithmetic degree, with coefficients in the required powers of the reduction.

papers.title: Understanding the Asymptotic Transience of Q-Learning via Distributional Expansion
papers.abstract: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the maximization transient is of order $n^{-1}$ and converges almost surely, after rescaling by $n$, to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.

papers.title: Quantum CSS codes: Decoder-aware multiobjective design and bound-certified selection
papers.abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes trade decoding reliability against the resources needed to measure their checks. We formulate Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code design at fixed encoding resources as a decoder-aware multiobjective problem. The objectives are failure probability under sector-wise degenerate maximum-likelihood decoding and check weight, the minimum total weight of an independent pure-type generator basis. For independent bit- and phase-flip noise with perfect syndrome extraction, deterministic truncation bounds support selection under a failure-rate constraint. At a per-sector error probability of 0.01, the bounds certify that a code encoding two logical qubits into 40 physical qubits meets a failure-rate target of 0.001 at check weight 139. The lower bound of every cheaper candidate in the corresponding (40,2) main menu exceeds this target. In paired searches sharing one annealing kernel and equal query budgets, decoder-aware guidance gives significantly higher mean final hypervolume than distance guidance in all eight tested configurations under the reported Holm correction. Against distance-multiplicity guidance, five configurations show significant gains and three do not, including one with a negative mean difference. All arms are scored in common truncated-reliability and normalized-check-weight coordinates. The framework connects reliability-check-weight trade-offs to bound-certified selection within evaluated CSS pools.

papers.title: Evaluating Quantum Circuit Protection Methods After Compilation: An Empirical Comparison
papers.abstract: Quantum cloud providers can read the circuits they receive and their outputs, yet methods for hiding a circuit are usually evaluated on the circuit as written, before compilation optimises it. We compare three ObfusQate schemes (inverse, composite and delayed gates), ECQCO and Q-MaskCut under one protocol that compiles every protected circuit at optimisation level 3 before measuring it; the goal is to keep the provider from learning the user's algorithm and answer. Q-MaskCut is one example combination of existing techniques: a one-time-pad key, decoy wires, circuit cutting with a random rotation pair across each cut, and Pauli twirling with dynamical-decoupling masking after compilation. We simulate 11 circuits of 3 to 19 qubits without noise and on two noise models, measure the compiled structure and execution time of 23 circuits of 3 to 127 qubits, and test whether the structural disguise survives a second compilation by the provider. Composite and delayed gates lose most of their structural disguise in compilation and leave the output readable; inverse gates keep a high normalised graph edit distance (normGED) only by making execution 7 to 112 times longer; ECQCO's output could not be decoded with the implementation provided by its authors. Q-MaskCut hides the output (mean total variation distance without the key 0.94), and without noise, with exact fragment probabilities, it decodes exactly. Its compiled normGED of 0.88 comes mostly from the masking, which a second compilation removes, leaving 0.42 from the key, decoys and padlocks. With noise, its fidelity is comparable to the original's; it needs 7 to 91 fragment variants per circuit in the simulations (7 to 61 in a run on ibm_marrakesh) and a classical reconstruction. Protection should therefore be evaluated on the compiled circuit and again after the provider recompiles it.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotics and stability for a two-power affine Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality
papers.abstract: We study the affine Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality under the constraint $\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}(f^{q-\varepsilon}+f^{q+\varepsilon}) dx=1$ for $f\ge0$, where $q=\frac{2n}{n+α}$, $n\ge2$, $0<α<n$, and $0<\varepsilon<q-1$. We determine the second-order expansion of its sharp constant and the scale selected by all normalized radial extremals as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0^+$. For sufficiently small fixed $\varepsilon$, we prove stability estimates with power $2$ in $L^{q-\varepsilon}\cap L^{q+\varepsilon}$ for the Euclidean and affine energies. The power $2$ is sharp, and the sharp stability constants admit $O(\varepsilon^2)$ upper bounds as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0^+$. The proof combines identities for the two power integrals with Euclidean spectral estimates, affine compactness and a nonlinear directional expansion. No uniqueness or additional regularity of the radial extremals is assumed.

papers.title: Sharp partition function bound for the attractive logarithmic gas
papers.abstract: For the attractive logarithmic potential, we prove that the partition function is bounded uniformly in the number of particles on every compact inverse-temperature interval $[0,\be_0]$ with $\be_0<B$, where $B\in(0,2\d]$ is the sharp constant in the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. The proof separates a smooth bulk, which inherits the entropy inequality, from a short-range singular interaction. The singular contribution is controlled on the event that each box of a fixed grid contains few particles. The complementary overcrowding event has exponentially small probability, which compensates a crude linear-in-$N$ bound on the log partition function. The resulting estimate supplies the partition bound that can be used recycled in a few different results. A separate Lean formalization verifies the conditional partition-bound theorem under the log-HLS assumption.

papers.title: Exact Values and Bounds for Four Color Quadratic Polynomial van der Waerden Numbers
papers.abstract: For a nonzero polynomial $P(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $P(0)=0$, let $W(P(x);4)$ denote the least integer $N$ such that every four coloring of $[N]$ contains distinct integers $u,v$ of the same color with $v-u=P(d)$ for some integer $d$. The best known general upper bounds for polynomial van der Waerden numbers are primitive recursive but remain enormous compared with the few known exact values. In this paper we determine the exact four color polynomial van der Waerden numbers for \[ \begin{gathered} x^2+x,\quad 2x^2+x,\quad 3x^2+x,\\ x^2+7x,\quad 2x^2+7x,\quad 3x^2+7x,\\ x^2+9x,\quad 2x^2+9x,\quad 3x^2+11x. \end{gathered} \] We derive upper bounds using combinatorial proofs and lower bounds using constructions of explicit colorings of $[N]$ found using the alternative computing inspired method of simulated annealing. More generally, we also prove that the four color polynomial van der Waerden numbers for the entire family of nonzero polynomials $ex^2+fx$ grow only linearly in the magnitude of their coefficients \[ W(ex^2+fx;4)=Θ(|e|+|f|). \]

papers.title: Explicit Subspace Evasive Sets via Subspace Designs
papers.abstract: Given a finite field $\mathbb F_q$, we say that a set $A\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ is an $(r,c)$ subspace evasive set if and only if for any affine subspace $U\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ with bounded dimension $\dim(U)\leq r$, the intersection size $|A\cap U|$ is at most $c$. The probabilistic method shows the existence of $(r,c)$ subspace evasive sets with $|A| = q^{(1-ε) n}$ with $c = O(r/ε)$. However, the best explicit constructions by Dvir--Lovett (STOC 2012) and Ben-Aroya--Shinkar (CJTCS 2013) have $c$ growing as an exponential function of $r$. Here, we give an explicit construction of such subspace evasive set that achieves the intersection bound $c=O(\min(r\log(r/ε)/ε, r^2/ε))$ when both $r$ and $1/ε$ are constants. Our approach is simple and the key idea is to compose subspace design codes (Guruswami-Xing, STOC 2013) with a suitably chosen ``local'' subspace evasive set. As a corollary, we give the first construction of an explicit (strongly) capacity-achieving list-recoverable code with nearly optimal list size, circumventing all previously-known barriers to construction.

papers.title: The frustration index of fully frustrated hypercubes
papers.abstract: The frustration index of a signed graph is the minimum number of edges meeting every negative cycle. Let $F_n$ be the frustration index of the signed $n$-cube $Q_n$ in which every square is negative. Using signings constructed from weighted cubes, we prove that for every positive integer $r$, \[ F_{r^2+1}=(r^2-r+1)2^{r^2-1}. \] When $4\mid r$, our construction also gives the exact value $F_n=(n-r-p/4)2^{n-2}$ in the six dimensions $n=r^2+1+pr/2$, $p\in\{\pm1,\pm2,\pm3\}$. In dimension nine an argument with integral eigenvectors gives $F_9=772$. By varying one weight in the construction for $r^2+1$, we obtain $F_n=(n-\sqrt n+O(n^{-1/2}))2^{n-2}$ for arbitrary $n$. The values at $n=r^2+1$ show that the error term has the best possible order. Taking the positive edges of an optimal signing gives a square-free subgraph of $Q_n$ with at least $(n+\sqrt n-O(n^{-1/2}))2^{n-2}$ edges whose complement is also square-free.

papers.title: Existence, relative Morse index and the number of positive multi-peak solutions to subcritical Hamiltonian systems
papers.abstract: We construct positive multi-peak solutions of a singularly perturbed Hamiltonian elliptic system with a common uniformly positive potential $a$ and powers $p,q>1$ below the Sobolev critical hyperbola. The peaks concentrate at any prescribed set of $k$ distinct nondegenerate critical points $P_i$ of $a$. The Hessian of the action is strongly indefinite. A Schur complement gives exactly $kN$ eigenvalues near zero and their leading terms, which have order $\varepsilon^2$ and are determined by $D^2a(P_i)$. The solutions are nondegenerate. A scalar Schur reduction and localization of its inverse term give the relative Morse index $k+\sum_{i=1}^k\ind D^2a(P_i)$. Local Pohozaev identities give local uniqueness. A compactness argument then shows that, for $m$ prescribed nondegenerate critical points, the union of the fixed profile neighborhoods associated with their nonempty subsets contains exactly $2^m-1$ positive solutions. Using uniqueness of positive solutions of the limiting system up to translations, we obtain the same count in classes defined by nonvanishing in fixed balls and a scaled nonlinear mass bound that excludes an additional peak. We also give second-order expansions of the peak locations and rescaled profiles.

papers.title: Machine Learning Moment Closure for the Boltzmann Transport Equation: Enforcing Hyperbolicity
papers.abstract: The Boltzmann transport equation describes particle transport across collisional regimes, but resolving its velocity dependence is expensive. Moment methods reduce this cost by evolving finitely many velocity moments, requiring a closure for unresolved higher-order moments. Data-driven closures can represent these moments accurately, yet without structural constraints they may produce complex characteristic speeds and unstable simulations. Learned Boltzmann closures with guaranteed hyperbolicity have so far been formulated in one spatial dimension; in multiple dimensions, hyperbolicity must hold in every direction simultaneously. We develop, to the best of our knowledge, the first data-driven closure for multidimensional Hermite moment systems of the linear Boltzmann equation that is hyperbolic by construction. The network learns a symmetric positive-definite symmetrizer shared by all spatial directions and restricted to a subspace that preserves the known lower-order transport equations; the unresolved rows follow from a symmetric completion. Every directional Jacobian thus has real eigenvalues and a complete set of eigenvectors for every network output and at any truncation order. The closure is trained only on spatial derivatives of unresolved moments from kinetic reference solutions, with no solver in the training loop, and evolved by a partially conservative discontinuous Galerkin method. In two-dimensional experiments in the transition and scattering-dominated regimes, a single learned third-order system with ten moments remains stable in all cases. Averaged over time, it is more accurate than the classical P7 and P15 truncations with 36 and 136 moments in every experiment, and its density error is about two orders of magnitude smaller than that of the P3 truncation with the same moments.

papers.title: Strongly quasidiagonal C*-algebras with nuclear dimension one and infinite decomposition rank
papers.abstract: We construct the first, to our knowledge, examples of strongly quasidiagonal C*-algebras with finite nuclear dimension and infinite decomposition rank. The examples are extensions of the form $0\to I \to E\to C(\mathbb{T})\to 0$ where $I$ is a simple AF-algebra. These examples are in some sense the easiest `natural' choices in light of Spielberg's work on AF-embedding extensions and the behavior of each dimension theory with respect to extensions. The standard extension bound provides $\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}} E \leq 2$ which is improved to 1 by recent work of Evington, Faurot and Schafhauser. Nuclear dimension 1 is the lowest possible for such an example because decomposition rank and nuclear dimension agree at 0. Finally, failure of the comparison property used to show infinite decomposition rank was inspired by local operator space techniques of Junge, Ozawa and Ruan.

papers.title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method for Semidefinite Complementarity Optimization
papers.abstract: Semidefinite complementarity constraints arise in applications such as inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization. We develop a structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian method (SPALM) for mathematical programs with these constraints. The method augments the smooth constraints and retains matrix complementarity in its subproblems. We handle these subproblems by an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions. With vanishing absolute subproblem errors, feasible accumulation points of infinite outer sequences are asymptotically M-stationary. Under AM-regularity, these points are M-stationary. We prove that active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ is sufficient for this regularity. For each AL subproblem, the full stationarity residual converges to zero along infinite accepted inner sequences if the initial sublevel set is bounded, the proximal parameters are bounded above and away from zero, and the block errors vanish. If the block errors are also square-summable, an $O(T^{-1/2})$ best-residual bound holds over $T$ accepted iterations. Huber-Stiefel and fixed-basis procedures generate feasible matrix candidates, whose acceptance is verified by descent tests and computable limiting-normal certificates. For rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation, we construct a lifting that preserves the projected feasible set and global optimal value and satisfies active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ at every feasible point. The stationarity guarantees apply to this lifted model. Finite-budget experiments on this lifting and a single-equality observation-fitting inverse SDP meet the prescribed numerical feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.

papers.title: Random feature policy iteration for inverse mean field games with complex geometry and high dimensions
papers.abstract: We propose a random feature policy iteration method for reconstructing the obstacle function in a mean-field game (MFG) from observations of its value function, leveraging the method's mesh-free nature and flexibility to handle complex geometries and high-dimensional problems. The method builds on a policy iteration framework for inverse MFGs, which decouples the coupled nonlinear forward-backward PDE system into a sequence of linear PDE and inverse problem solves. The fixed random feature representations preserve this linear structure, allowing the resulting subproblems to be solved by minimizing residuals at sampled collocation points through linear least-squares problems. The mesh-free nature of the method further extends the applicability of the policy iteration framework to inverse MFGs with complex geometry and in high dimensions. Another key advantage is its flexibility in using different spatial approximations for different variables: the obstacle function, value function, and population density can be represented in separate feature spaces, accommodating obstacles that are substantially less regular than the corresponding PDE solutions. Moreover, boundary conditions can be enforced through collocation on irregular domains without constructing boundary-fitted meshes. Numerical experiments involving smooth and discontinuous obstacles, a domain with holes, and higher-dimensional problems demonstrate the accuracy and flexibility of the proposed method.

papers.title: Golod thresholds of ideals and products of ideals in dimension 3
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be a proper ideal in a standard graded polynomial ring $P$ with homogeneous maximal ideal $\m$. We show that there exists $k_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\m^kI$ is Golod for all $k\geq k_0$. The smallest such $k_0$ is denoted $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$. We give an explicit formula for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ in the case when $I$ is a monomial complete intersection and bounds for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ for other classes of ideals. We show that under a certain degree condition, the product of a Golod ideal with a maximal homogeneous ideal is Golod. In the last section, we show that in a regular local ring of dimension 3, the product of any two proper ideals is Golod; this solves a question posed by Dao-Stefani \cite[Question 4.5]{dao2022monomial} and VandeBogert \cite[Question 4.11]{vandebogert2022products}.

papers.title: Quantum Fluctuations of the Stress-Energy Tensor via Noether's Theorem and the Connection to the Cosmological Constant
papers.abstract: When deriving the expression for the conserved Noether's current one obtains a term that is an integral over the Euler-Lagrange equation. This term vanishes vanishes if the system evolves along the classical path. However, quantum particles do not necessarily follow the classical path and, hence, for a quantum system, the Euler-Lagrange term does not vanish. This extra term corresponds to a quantum fluctuation of the Noether's current owing to the system deviating from the classical path. Here, we compute the fluctuation of a quantum field directly from Noether's Theorem and, by considering a spacetime translational symmetry of a complex scalar field, we find the specific fluctuations of the Stress-Energy tensor. As the Stress-Energy tensor is the source term for Einstein's equations of General Relativity, these fluctuations can be seen to be a contribution to the Cosmological Constant. The final expression for this contribution is proportional to the mass of the field to the fourth power which is consistent with previously derived expressions for the Cosmological Constant.

papers.title: A Master Identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-Type Series for $1/π$
papers.abstract: We derive a novel three-parameter master identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-type series for $1/π$. By unifying disparate results from the literature into a single overarching framework, we demonstrate that Glaisher's original series and numerous known variations emerge naturally as special cases through systematic choices of the parameters. This master identity simplifies the derivation of existing formulas, provides a mechanism for generating an infinite number of new series for $1/π$, and is further utilized to derive associated series involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers.

papers.title: Rational isogenies of of rank-two Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.

papers.title: Talagrand's Convolution Bound for Tensor Powers of Finite-State Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: Talagrand's convolution conjecture, recently proven by J. Lu, S. Guo, and E. Fang, concerns the smoothing properties of the heat semigroup on $\{-1,1\}^N$. We follow their perturbed coupled reverse-heat approach to generalize the theorem to tensor powers of irreducible continuous-time Markov semigroups on finite state spaces. Specifically, let $(S_t)_{t\geq0}$ be the semigroup of an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space $G_0$ with stationary distribution $π$. Then, for every $τ>0$, there exists a finite constant $C_{τ,S,π}<\infty$ such that, for every $N\geq1$, every nonnegative function $f:G_0^N\to[0,\infty)$, and every $η>1$, \begin{align*} π^{\otimes N}\left(S_τ^{\otimes N}f>η\int_{G_0^N}f\,dπ^{\otimes N}\right)\leq\frac{C_{τ,S,π}}{η\sqrt{\logη}}, \end{align*} where the constant is independent of $N$, $f$, and $η$. Most of the machinery developed by Lu, Guo, and Fang transfers cleanly, but since probability distributions on $|G_0|$ elements are not determined by their mean for $|G_0|>2$, we must use explicit terminal bridge laws to find a dimension-independent bound for the terminal-discrepancy estimate. We have formalized our result in Lean 4. The formalization is publicly available.

papers.title: Falconer's conjecture through descent and chaining
papers.abstract: OpenAI proved that a compact set $E\subset{\mathbb R}^d$ of Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d}{2}$ determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive length. We give a complete proof of this theorem which follows the overall architecture of the OpenAI argument, from the construction of the initial pair measures to the final Fourier estimate, but which modifies that argument substantially at the points where the geometric costs are paid and where the estimates are reassembled. The reductions are organized by the descent and chaining viewpoint of Burstein, Iosevich, and Krause: one potential, built from two separated depths together with a penalty for insufficient separation, pays for every reduction on every interval of scales, the terminal intervals included, and a finite-record chaining lemma keeps the fixed power losses attached to the few reductions which incur them. In odd dimensions the radial improvement is obtained directly at each finite scale from a quantitative contact interval, chosen by minimizing a mass curve against lines of two slopes, with explicit margins in place of a compactness argument, and the conditional estimates on the three parts of that interval are multiplied by a lemma on full source fibers. A random sign identity represents the coarse pair filter by products of endpoint multipliers and reduces the cost of reassembling the spatial pieces inside the shell estimate. The argument gives more than positive length. Since the mass first excluded near heavy hyperplanes at each late scale is summable with a power rate, all the Fourier estimates compare with one fixed measure, and the distance set supports a probability measure with an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$ and with power Fourier decay, so that $Δ(E)$ has positive Fourier dimension.

papers.title: A Novel Iterative Algorithm Incorporating Machine Learning for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck Equations in Three-Dimensional Ion Channel Simulation
papers.abstract: The Poisson Nernst Planck (PNP) equation is widely used to simulate ion channel transport, but its strong nonlinearity and coupling characteristics make numerical solutions extremely challenging, and decoupling methods are usually required. The Gummel iteration method is widely adopted as a common decoupling algorithm owing to its simplicity, ease of implementation, and applicability even under complex conditions. But its convergence efficiency highly depends on the selection of the relaxation parameter, unsuitable parameters will lead to slow convergence or even divergence. At present, parameter selection relies heavily on manual experience, which is inefficient and unstable, significantly hindering the solving efficiency for practical problems such as ion channel simulations. To address this, we propose a machine learning-based parameter selection method, which can select near-optimal relaxation parameters for the Gummel iteration of PNP equations for ion channels. Based on the machine learning-based parameter selection algorithm, we develop a coupled finite element and Gummel iteration solver, and more stable convergence and higher computational efficiency have been achieved in ion channel simulations. To validate the method, we conduct tests on two real channels with complex geometries that differ significantly from the training samples. Numerical results demonstrate that this method has a significant effect on improving the convergence efficiency and stability of Gummel iteration, confirming its applicability in practical ion channel simulations.

papers.title: Random Diophantine inequalities in few variables
papers.abstract: We prove that for almost all additive Diophantine inequalities of degree $k$ in at least $k+1$ variables the expected asymptotic formula for the density of solutions holds true. This improves the result of Brüdern and Dietmann \cite{BD}.

papers.title: Entropy-degree rigidity for non-collapsed $RCD$ spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the entropy-degree theorem for continuous maps from a closed orientable non-collapsed $RCD(K,N)$ space $X$ to a closed negatively curved locally symmetric $N$-manifold $Y$, with $N \geq 3$. In the equality case, under a fundamental group index condition, we show the space is isometric to a smooth locally symmetric Riemannian manifold, and the map is homotopic to a Riemannian covering.

papers.title: Perimeter-Regularized Critical Shapes in the Class $\mathcal{O}_C$: Core-Normal Transfer and First-Order Return-Map Response
papers.abstract: Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a compact strictly convex core and $\mathcal{O}_C$ denote the class of domains whose outer boundary is a global outward normal graph over $\partial C$ and whose inward boundary normals return to the interior of $C$. We study volume-constrained critical domains of the Dirichlet-perimeter functional: \[ \mathcal{E}_μ(Ω) = -\frac{1}{2}\int_Ω|\nabla u_Ω|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x + μP(Ω), \qquad -Δu_Ω = f, \quad u_Ω|_{\partialΩ}=0, \] in the large-perimeter regime $μ\to\infty$. We give an adapted Lyapunov--Schmidt construction near translated spheres to extract the first physical shape coefficient of scale $μ^{-1}$. We then prove that $\mathcal{O}_C$ is open under small $C^1$ thickness perturbations and establish a quantitative coordinate-transfer theorem to a unique core-normal thickness. Finally, we prove that the forward return-map operator $d \mapsto F_d$ is Fréchet $C^1$ between Hölder spaces and provide its explicit derivative. This yields a shape-to-dynamics sensitivity theorem for $\mathcal{O}_C$: a perimeter-regularized PDE-constrained critical deformation produces an explicitly controlled first-order deformation of the return dynamics. A nonradial example confirms that the response coefficient is generically nonzero.

papers.title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
papers.abstract: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.

papers.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
papers.abstract: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$

papers.title: Equilateral simplices over general fields
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Schoenberg (1937) characterizes the dimensions $d$ for which $\mathbb{Q}^d$ contains the vertex set of a regular simplex with $d+1$ vertices. We generalize Schoenberg's result to all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$, using elementary Witt theory and Lagrange's four-square theorem. Our generalization also sharpens Schoenberg's theorem and complements more recent work of Lorenz and Zimmermann (2026) by characterizing the admissible edge lengths. In the case of finite characteristic, equilateral simplices with $d+2$ vertices can sometimes exist (F.~Radó 1986), and we characterize this situation as well, again for all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$. We also briefly consider the edge lengths of equilateral simplices of $d$ vertices.

papers.title: Regularization Independence in the One-Dimensional Schrödinger Equation with Delta Potential
papers.abstract: We consider a class of regularizations $\{δ_\varepsilon\}$ of the Dirac delta defined by a uniform $L^1$ bound, the normalization $\intδ_\varepsilon\to1$, and a truncated first-moment condition, with no restriction on sign, shape, support, or scaling. For this class we prove that the transmission and reflection coefficients for the Hamiltonian operator $H_\varepsilon=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-λδ_\varepsilon$ at fixed energy converge to those of the delta interaction. Under the additional assumption that each $δ_\varepsilon$ is bounded, we show that any family of negative eigenvalues of $H_\varepsilon$ bounded away from zero converges to $-λ^2/4$ when $λ>0$, and that no such family exists when $λ<0$. Both convergences are obtained with an explicit rate, expressed through two integrals of $δ_\varepsilon$, directly computable for a given regularization. The bound-state convergence follows from the work of Brasche, Figari, and Teta; here, our contribution is an elementary proof with an explicit rate. Their norm resolvent convergence, however, does not by itself imply convergence of the scattering matrix, which was previously known for families obtained by scaling a single fixed profile; we prove it for a strictly larger class.

papers.title: Geometric Combinatorics of Polynomials with Rotationally Symmetric Roots
papers.abstract: In a recent paper by Dougherty and McCammond, the authors introduced a piecewise Euclidean cell structure for the space of monic centered polynomials. This was achieved by studying the relationship between the polynomials and their critical values, using the Lyashko-Looijenga (LL) map, as well as the noncrossing combinatorics of the polynomials. In this paper, we extend their results to the space of polynomials with rotationally symmetric roots by studying an appropriate generalisation of the LL map, which relates the polynomials and their reduced critical values. The combinatorics of the polynomials are noncrossing partitions of type $B_d$. This give us a piecewise Euclidean cell structure built using the order complex of the noncrossing partition of type $B_d$. Along the way, we also give a compactification of this space of polynomials.

papers.title: Two-Stage Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming in Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: Lenstra showed that mixed-integer linear programming can be solved in polynomial time when the number of integer variables is fixed and the number of continuous variables is arbitrary. Mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) can be solved in polynomial time when the total number of variables is fixed. However, since MIQP is NP-hard already without integer variables, the analog of Lenstra's result fails unless P = NP. Hence, polynomial-time algorithms for MIQP with an arbitrary number of continuous variables must exploit additional structure. We study MIQPs with two-stage structure, which underlies Benders decomposition and two-stage stochastic programming. A few linking variables, including all integer variables, are coupled with many blocks of continuous variables that interact only through them, both in the constraints and in the objective. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for MIQP with an arbitrary quadratic objective when the number of linking variables and the block size are fixed, while the number of blocks, and hence the number of variables, is arbitrary. The case with no blocks is MIQP in fixed dimension. None of our assumptions can be dropped. Unless P = NP, the number of linking variables and the block size must both be fixed, the blocks cannot interact or contain integer variables, and large blocks cannot be allowed even if their objective is linear. Unless FPT = W[1], the exponent of the running time must depend on both the number of linking variables and the block size.

papers.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
papers.abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov (2025), the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

papers.title: Automating the Derivation of Advanced Algorithms in Numerical Linear Algebra using Associative Algebras with Involution
papers.abstract: Standard algorithms of numerical linear algebra use their scalars through seven operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the adjoint, the $*$-square root and $(i,j)$ indexing. This thesis overloads these operations, as automatic differentiation overloads arithmetic, allowing scalars in associative algebras with involution. Many of the resulting decompositions and algorithms reduce to Hermitian eigendecomposition over these $*$-algebras. The decompositions are organised by doubly-signed quivers, whose vertices record real, complex or quaternionic scalars and the action of the involution. We prove an analogue of Gabriel's theorem: every finite-dimensional real $*$-algebra is a matrix algebra, with sizes and signs, over a quotient of its quiver's path $*$-algebra. Spectral theorems, the singular value decomposition, Takagi factorisation, Sylvester's law of inertia and the real Jordan form arise as unitary similarity problems for Hermitian matrices. Division and square roots take place in a completed localisation which inverts the arrows. For the singular value decomposition, Householder tridiagonalisation becomes Golub--Kahan bidiagonalisation. Over split-complex numbers, the QR algorithm becomes Rutishauser's LR algorithm, two steps at a time, and Cholesky factorisation becomes Doolittle's LU factorisation. These identifications require suitable $*$-square roots and hold whenever the steps are defined. Infinitesimals make limits of algorithms exact computations: Gram--Schmidt yields the Bruhat decomposition, and Gaussian elimination with pivots chosen by orders of magnitude yields Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm in leading terms. A Python library implements the seven operations and algorithms. An appendix visualises the QR algorithm on $2\times2$ real matrices.

papers.title: A family of alternating projection examples whose Cesàro means fail to converge strongly
papers.abstract: In 1965, Bregman proved that the sequence of iterates of the method of alternating projections applied to two closed convex sets with nonempty intersection in a Hilbert space converges weakly to a point in the intersection. The question whether this convergence may actually fail to be strong was settled in a seminal paper by Hundal in 2004. He provided a counterexample featuring a halfspace and a closed convex cone generated by a certain curve. While largely elementary, the details of Hundal's construction and analysis are quite involved. We revisit this seminal example and present a family of such examples that allows for simpler proofs. Our generating curve combines unit vectors with Gaussian inner products and a height determined by a scalar function. The orbits converge weakly --- but not strongly --- to the origin, while their norms have a positive limit for which we give explicit lower bounds. We also prove that the associated Cesàro means behave likewise; in fact, this is generalized to alternating proximal mappings whose composition has a fixed point. Finally, these orbits allow interpretations in the context of projected-gradient, proximal-point, and gradient-descent algorithms.

papers.title: Randomly growing uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We investigate growing uniform random hypergraphs whose hyperedges are $(k-1)$-simplices. At each step, one of two processes occurs: (i) a new vertex is added with probability $p$; (ii) a simplex $\langle v_1,\ldots,v_k\rangle$ with randomly chosen distinct vertices is added with probability $1-p$. Emerging random uniform hypergraphs exhibit a percolation transition. A giant component is formed when $p<p_c=1-(2k-1)^{-2}$. The fraction of vertices in the giant component scales as $\exp[-C/\sqrt{p_c-p}]$, a signature of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase transition. In the non-percolating phase, the cluster size distribution has an algebraic tail with a continuously varying exponent, while at $p=p_c$, it acquires a logarithmic correction. We analyze triadic hypergraphs ($k=3$) in detail and then generalize to higher $k$. We show that the Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component scale linearly with system size. Higher Betti numbers fluctuate between realizations but remain finite, and hence the normalized Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component are asymptotically equal, up to a sign.

papers.title: Quantum Telatar formula: fading quantum capacity of Haar-random multimode attenuators
papers.abstract: Cellular communication is done over an imperfectly predictable multimode environment, where the sender only knows about the distribution of possible intermode coupling and scattering a signal faces. It may thus seem surprising that such communication is efficient. Telatar proved that the sender's lack of exact knowledge about the channel, on average, does not significantly hinder multimode communication. As the number $N$ of modes increases at fixed signal-to-noise ratio, the average capacity of a classical multimode fading channel grows linearly in $N$, like that of $N$ decoupled single-mode channels. We study the quantum analogue in a Haar-random passive bosonic network and prove a similar scaling for unassisted quantum information transmission. Suppose that the sender drives a fixed fraction of the input modes and the receiver collects more than half of the output modes. Then the quantum capacity of such channels at zero temperature grows linearly with the number of modes at fixed photon number per mode, just like the classical capacity grows with the number of antennas. At nonzero temperature, the Haar-averaged coherent information of the isotropic thermal input bounds the capacity from below, and its value per mode converges to an integral against Wachter's law. We numerically identify positive achievable rates in models motivated by cryogenic microwave networks and room-temperature multimode fibers.

papers.title: Permutation codes via spectral graph theory
papers.abstract: We use the Eigenvalue Method to obtain upper spectral bounds on the size of permutation codes in the Hamming, Ulam, Cayley and Kendall metrics. For the Kendall metric, we improve the double-ball upper bound of Buzaglo and Etzion [IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 2015] at minimum distance four and lengths seven and eight. For the Cayley metric, we improve the sphere packing bound, and determine when these spectral improvements occur. We derive theoretical spectral criteria for improvements from the ratio-type bounds of low degree, and show that the quadratic ratio-type bound for the Kendall metric always equals sphere packing. Furthermore, we prove sharp spectral bounds and recover known optimal code sizes for the Hamming and Ulam metrics.

papers.title: Tripod Reordering: A 33-Queue Layout of Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: A queue layout of a graph consists of a linear order of the vertices and a partition of the edges into queues so that no two edges in a single queue are nested. The minimum number of queues needed in a queue layout of a graph is called its queue number. A planar product structure theorem of Dujmović, Joret, Micek, Morin, Ueckerdt, and Wood (JACM, 2020) states that every planar graph is a subgraph of the strong product of a graph of simple treewidth at most $3$, a clique $K_3$, and a path. The result has been used to show that the queue number of planar graphs is at most $49$. Recently, Bekos, Gronemann, and Raftopoulou (Algorithmica, 2023) investigated how the general approach based on the product structure can be optimized for planar graphs. They claim that an appropriate reordering of the three vertices associated with each bag in the product structure decomposition, called a tripod, reduces the queue number of planar graphs to $42$. We first highlight a gap in their queue layout algorithm: one of the choices required by the algorithm is not guaranteed to exist. Then we show how to address the limitation and provide an alternative tripod reordering mechanism that reduces the upper bound on the queue number of planar graphs to $33$. As a corollary, bipartite planar graphs have queue number at most $22$.

papers.title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
papers.abstract: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. Moreover, for a complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of any knot of the family coincides (up to a factor) with the generating series of the semigroup. Let $(X,0)$ be a splice quotient singularity with $\mathbb{Z}HS^3$ link $Σ$ and let $(C,0)$ be a reduced curve-germ embedded in $(X,0)$ defined as the zero locus of the product of end curve functions. We prove, thorugh our topological characterization of complete intersection semigroups, the coincidence between the Alexander polynomial of the knot cut out by $C$ in $Σ$ and the Poincaré series of the embedded curve. Hence providing a generalization of the result due to Campillo, Delgado and Gusein-Zade for plane curve singularities. Furthermore, for any good resolution of $(X,0)$ compatible with the splice quotient analytic structure, we provide an explicit description of the semigroup of integer multiplicities of functions along any divisor of the resolution.

papers.title: Hopf algebras of leaf-graded forests
papers.abstract: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Improved last-iterate bounds for SGD with and without replacement
papers.abstract: In this work, we study last-iterate convergence bounds for stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on convex and $β$-smooth loss functions and improve the bound from $\cO((\log T)^3/T)$ to $\cO((\log T)^3/(T\log\log T))$ in the interpolation regime. The improvement comes from applying a horizon-dependent multiscale estimate of gradients to the comparison of trajectories. The bound applies to both sampling with replacement and sampling without replacement within one pass.

papers.title: Maximal nilpotence for higher Verlinde categories
papers.abstract: We show that all higher Verlinde categories are maximally nilpotent, as conjectured by Coulembier (2023). By previous results, it suffices to show that non-trivial simple objects have only finitely many non-zero symmetric powers in odd characteristic. We compute the maximal degrees of these non-zero symmetric and exterior powers explicitly, hence confirming their finiteness. We discuss some of the far-reaching consequences.

papers.title: Controlling the Vacuum: Tunable Magnonic Casimir Effect in Magnetic Moiré Systems
papers.abstract: We prove that the quantum fluctuations of the magnetic degrees of freedom of moiré structures can be tuned by adjusting the moiré lattice. Using the Bistritzer-MacDonald approach, we explore the consequences of this fact for the magnonic vacuum energy and the magnonic Casimir force, which become functions of the moiré pattern parameters. This allows a prototypical engine to be run with the vacuum fluctuations as a working agent and, in that way, to furnish a novel type of magneto-mechanical effect. Our calculations focus on the moiré Ladder as an example but can be generalized to any moiré structure in a straightforward fashion. We anticipate that our results belong to a generic property of moiré structures, regardless of the physical nature of the excitations at hand.

papers.title: The bounded approximation property in Banach function lattices, interpolation of the essential norm, and applications
papers.abstract: We prove the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded. This allows us to develop a general framework for the quantitative interpolation of compact operators, understood in terms of the essential norm, encompassing a large class of function spaces including weighted Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. Combined with extrapolation techniques, we show how to transfer compactness (or, more generally, control of the essential norm) from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to the three aforementioned classes of function spaces. Finally, we present several applications in analysis and partial differential equations.

papers.title: Real monopole Floer homology and the Alexander polynomial
papers.abstract: We prove that the Euler characteristic of the framed real monopole Floer homology of the double branched cover of a link is given by the Alexander polynomial evaluated at $\sqrt{-1}$. For knots $K$ with determinant one, this formula shows that Miyazawa's degree invariant of $K$ can be computed in terms of the Alexander polynomial of $K$. The proof involves a new connected-sum formula and oriented skein exact triangles for some new variants of real monopole Floer homology, called the diagonal and cone real monopole Floer homology, which admit mod-two gradings. This is the monopole counterpart of Srivastava's Euler characteristic formula in real Heegaard Floer homology.

papers.title: Encoding rational $Δ$-triples on elliptic curves
papers.abstract: A $Δ$-triple for a natural number $n$ is a triple $(x,y,z)$ of divisors of $n$ with $1<x<y\leq z<\sqrt n$ and $n/x-x=(n/y-y)+(n/z-z)$. The numbers that admit such a triple are those with the $Δ$ property, which governs the existence of certain $n$-simple triangles in factor graphs of split graphs. We allow the three components to be rational numbers, and show that, once the quotient $z/y=a/b$ is fixed, the rational $Δ$-triples for $n$ are exactly the rational points of the elliptic curve $Y^2=n\,ab\,w(w+ab)\bigl(w+(a+b)^2\bigr)$ lying over the interval $-b(a+b)<w<-ab$. Since a rational $Δ$-triple for $n$ amounts to $Δ$-triples for infinitely many of the numbers $κ^2n$, the chord--tangent construction becomes a way of producing new $Δ$-triples from old ones. For perfect squares, the curve always carries a rational point coming from a degenerate triple. This point has order $4$ if $a=b$, and infinite order if $a>b$. As a consequence, for every quotient $a/b>1$ there are infinitely many pairwise non-proportional $Δ$-triples of perfect squares with $z/y=a/b$, in contrast with the fact that perfect squares have no $Δ$-triple with $y=z$. For arbitrary $n$, there are infinitely many rational $Δ$-triples for $n$ with a given quotient if and only if the corresponding curve has positive rank.

papers.title: Bipartite Matchings, Matrix Permanents, and Zeon Power Series
papers.abstract: Perfect matchings of a bipartite graph are counted by the permanent of the graph's biadjacency matrix, and permanents of sequences of structured biadjacency matrices lead to integer sequences. We consider a number of such sequences and illustrate how zeon-algebraic representations of bipartite graphs lead to recursively defined zeon sequences. Then, using formal power series methods, we show that the ``$Ω$-exponentials'' of these zeon sequences reveal numbers of perfect matchings in the graphs.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust BEST-RQ For Speech Representation Learning
papers.abstract: BEST-RQ, based on random projection and quantization, has been a well-established self-supervised learning approach to learn speech representations from large-scale unlabeled audio due to its high performance and efficiency. However, in BEST-RQ representations learned by random quantization can be sensitive to the choice of quantization targets. To address this issue, we propose a distributionally robust extension of BEST-RQ that seeks representations robust across multiple quantization configurations. Specifically, we define groups by codebooks and formulate the training as a group Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) problem. Rather than optimizing solely for the average loss across groups, our approach adaptively reweights groups to emphasize those performing poorly. Additionally, we regularize DRO with a Kullback-Leibler divergence to prevent excessive distribution deviation. We evaluate our approach on the Multilingual LibriSpeech dataset and show that the distributionally robust BEST-RQ achieves superior performance over the conventional uniform average across multiple codebooks.

papers.title: Zeroth persistent homology of ground-state correlations at clean and disordered quantum transitions
papers.abstract: The antiferromagnetic Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields exhibits a continuous critical point, a mixed-order transition line and, with quenched disorder, an infinite-disorder fixed point and reentrant order. Using exact free-fermion solutions and the density-matrix renormalization group, we examine what the zeroth persistent homology of staggered ground-state correlations adds to conventional responses. Its barcode records the merge scales of the single-linkage hierarchy, and the maximum of its persistence-landscape velocity defines a threshold-free pseudocritical point. This point locates the clean critical point and the mixed-order line with an accuracy comparable to conventional responses. In the reentrant regime, the global velocity misplaces the entry, which is recovered only by restricting the filtration to the ordering scale, and none of the tested estimators locates the exit. A domain wall forced by the boundary conditions suppresses the disorder-averaged reentrant lobe. For individual disordered realizations, the labelled merge tree recovers most strong-disorder renormalization-group clusters, including noncontiguous ones missed by lattice-restricted hierarchies, with increasing agreement at stronger disorder. This information resides in the full correlation matrix, while zeroth homology provides a stable, threshold-free hierarchy.

papers.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
papers.abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $Δ$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $Δ=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.

papers.title: On Koebe theorem for Sobolev mappings on Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: We consider mappings between domains of two Riemannian surfaces. The main subject of the investigation are families of homeomorphisms with moduli inequalities. For such families, we obtain the uniform openness (uniform lightness). As a consequence, we obtain similar results for homeomorphisms of Sobolev classes with finite distortion whenever its maximal dilatations have a majorant integrable on almost all concentric circles. In particular, we obtain the Koebe-type theorem for both direct and inverse Sobolev mappings.

papers.title: Bounding Freedom of Choice via Causal Network Embeddings
papers.abstract: Standard Bell inequalities rely on measurement independence, the assumption that measurement settings are perfectly decoupled from the source of correlations. We demonstrate that embedding Bell scenarios into larger causal networks naturally overcomes this limitation. This embedding yields experimentally accessible lower and upper bounds on measurement dependence, the incompatibility of which certifies nonclassicality directly from data, without assuming a priori freedom of choice. We formulate a general linear-programming framework to systematically derive these measurement-dependence consistency (MDC) Bell inequalities. By bypassing standard non-convexity hurdles, this approach significantly outperforms existing techniques in computational simplicity and noise robustness. Finally, we reveal that genuine quantum nonlocality can be certified even for correlations exceeding the Tsirelson bound, and demonstrate our method's broad applicability to multi-outcome and multipartite Bell tests.

papers.title: Compactness-uniqueness method for null controllability
papers.abstract: We develop the compactness--uniqueness method for the null controllability of abstract linear control systems on Banach spaces. Our first main result characterizes the null controllable states for systems that are null controllable up to finite dimensional spaces, and shows that null controllability is then equivalent to the Fattorini--Hautus test. Our second main result gives a dual counterpart of this assumption, an observability inequality with a suitable compact remainder. These results unify and extend several known results, such as those on heat equations with nonlocal terms and on the simultaneous controllability of systems. Finally, for a transport equation with nonlocal terms from population dynamics, we characterize the null controllable states after a sharp time, including in the non-reflexive space $L^1$.

papers.title: The higher order regularity problem for elliptic systems with data in Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize the well-posedness of the higher order regularity problem in the upper half-space with data in Sobolev Banach function spaces by proving its equivalence to natural weighted estimates for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. The generality of our framework allows for applications to Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement-invariant spaces such as Orlicz spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces, as well as their weighted counterparts, among others. This is established for the family of second-order, homogeneous, elliptic, constant complex coefficient systems in ${\mathbb{R}}^n$ that admit a distinguished coefficient tensor, a natural condition that always holds in the scalar case and for the Lamé system of elasticity.

papers.title: Making Poisson σ again - an étude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
papers.abstract: The Poisson $σ$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $Σ$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = Σ\times G \to Σ$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,ω)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,Π)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = Σ\times M \to Σ$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $Σ$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,Π)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $ω$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

papers.title: Sign components for general bosonic-fermionic coinvariant rings
papers.abstract: We prove that the sign-isotypic components of the symmetric group coinvariant rings $R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(a,b)}$ and $R_n^{(k+a,\ell+b)}$ are isomorphic if and only if $n \leq 2$ or at least one of $(k,\ell)$ or $(a,b)$ is $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$. Moreover, for $k \geq 1$ the $ν$-isotypic components $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(0,1)}\right)^ν$ and $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell+1)}\right)^ν$ are isomorphic if and only if $ν$ corresponds to the sign representation. We also show that the socle of $R_n^{(k,\ell)}$ always contains the sign component, extending one direction of a result of Haiman for $R_n^{(2,0)}$. We settle the hook components conjecture of Bergeron (2024) for coinvariant rings, and a conjecture of Bergeron (2020) that the multiplicity of the sign character of $R_n^{(1,2)}$ is $3^{n-1}$. Our results also recover several existing results in the literature. Lastly, we extend our results to the hyperoctahedral group ${\mathfrak{B}_n}$ and prove that the determinant-isotypic components of $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(0,1)}$ and $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell+1)}$ are isomorphic.

papers.title: Sliding 2-handles over 3-handles and the barbell diffeomorphism
papers.abstract: We give three fundamental examples highlighting the relationship between loops of spheres in $\#^k S^2\times S^2$, pseudo-isotopies, and diffeomorphisms of the 4-sphere. First, we describe an explicit pseudo-isotopy and Hatcher-Wagoner family that realizes the barbell diffeomorphism $β$ of the 4-sphere by constructing a finger-Whitney system for the family. From the Hatcher-Wagoner family, we are able to conclude that the example in §7 of ``Pseudo-isotopies of simply connected 4-manifolds'' generates $β$. Next, it is known that the square of $β$ is isotopic to id. We reprove this by building an explicit 2-parameter family of Morse functions that trivializes the Hatcher-Wagoner family for $β^2$. We do this by utilizing exchange points and families of handle slides. In the final example, we show that another Hatcher-Wagoner family, affectionately called the double cross, also generates $β$.

papers.title: A Characterization of Completely Integrally Closed Prüfer $v$-Multiplication Domains
papers.abstract: We generalize a result known for Prüfer domains to show that a PVMD $R$ is completely integrally closed if and only if $\text{Inv}^t(R)$ is an archimedean $\ell$-group. It has been conjectured that a PVMD is completely integrally closed if and only if it is an Archimedean domain. It is known that a completely integrally closed PVMD is an Archimedean domain. We provide an example to illustrate that an Archimedean PVMD need not be completely integrally closed.

papers.title: Orthogonal Splines Associated to Root Systems and Applications to Function Approximation From Generalized Derivative Samples
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}(X)$ be the principal shift invariant space generated by a box spline $B_X$ with $d$-dimensional direction set $X$ and associated differential operator $D_X$. Assuming that each direction in $X$ appears with even multiplicity i.e $X = [X_0|X_0]$, we may endow $\mathcal{S}(X)$ with a special inner product $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$ which is similar to a homogeneous Sobolev-like inner product of order $|X_0|$. Then, for the special case when the directions in $X$ are selected from a root system, we introduce bi-orthogonal systems for $\mathcal{S}(X)$. Within any fixed bi-orthogonal system, each basis function is compactly supported albeit the diameter of the supports of the basis functions is not uniformly bounded. On the other hand, the image of any bi-orthogonal system under $D_X$ (which is necessarily finite and discrete) is uniformly finite. In other words, the basis elements, while having non-sparse box-spline representation, are uniformly sparse in their truncated-power representation. Using the Sobolev-like inner product and an aforementioned biorthogonal system for $\mathcal{S}(X)$, the analysis-synthesis operator from smooth compactly supported continuous functions into $\mathcal{S}(X)$ is well-defined. Using integration by parts and the orthogonality satisfied by the bases under $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$, this operator is a local discrete quasi-interpolation operator. When $X$ comes from an irreducible root system, we can slightly modify these quasi-interpolants to ensure they have optimal approximation order. In other words, if $f$ is sufficiently smooth and compactly supported, we can optimally approximate $f$ from a collection of generalized derivative samples induced by one of our bases.

papers.title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
papers.abstract:
The multivariate breeder's equation $Δ ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\inftyλ_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$. We show that the literal discrete analog of this result is false: with constant positive definite $P$ the iterates can oscillate or diverge. The result is restored by a single additional hypothesis, a uniform bound on the largest eigenvalue of $P_k$, $λ_n$, such that $λ_n(P_k)\le 2/L$ where $L$ is a local Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$. Under this bound the maximum is uniformly stable; under a stricter version together with $\sum_kλ_1(P_k)=\infty$, the maximum is uniformly asymptotically stable. Given these hypotheses, a level-set estimate of the basin of attraction carries over. Both bounds are sharp, and each remaining hypothesis is shown to be necessary. Biologically, the bound says that genetic variance in every direction must be small relative to the curvature of log mean fitness; outside this regime the mean phenotype can overshoot a fitness peak as hypothesized by Fisher's geometric model. As further application of our results, the same conditions apply to the mean update of Gaussian evolutionary optimization algorithms, in which the covariance of the search population plays the role of $G$.

papers.title: Modular $n$-queens in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: A chess queen in $d$-dimensions can move any distance in the direction of any edge or diagonal of the $d$-dimensional hypercube. (That is, a queen can move from a position $x$ to $x+cv$ for any $c$ and any nonzero $v\in\{-1,0,1\}^d$.) We prove that one can place $n^{d-1}$ non-attacking queens on the $d$-dimensional modular board $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ if and only if all prime factors of $n$ exceed $2^d$. The $d=3$ case of this result is a conjecture of van Rees from 1981. Our proof involves both human ideas and substantial AI assistance.

papers.title: Damped wave equation with a dynamic boundary condition: sharp resolvent estimate
papers.abstract: This work investigates the stabilization of a wave equation with a localized damping and dynamic boundary conditions. This model traces back to the classical treatment of torsion and impact problems. Consider a second-order hyperbolic equation posed with a dynamic boundary condition on a smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(\M,g)$ with boundary, in which the damping acts either in the interior or on $\d \M$. Under the assumption that the damping is positive on an open subset of its domain of action, a resolvent estimate is established. A logarithmic decay rate is then deduced for the energy of strong solutions. We provide examples that establish the sharpness of the resolvent estimate.

papers.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
papers.abstract: We study how many polarized anti-invariant factors of the intermediate Jacobians of smooth Eckardt hyperplane sections determine a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. In rank three, the equation is determined by its fixed cubic surface and a conic in the dual projective space. The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin--Zhang recovers the surface together with one plane section from each factor. When the surface has no automorphisms, these planes can be compared in a common dual space, and reconstruction reduces to classical conic interpolation. Five factors suffice without parameter data, and four suffice with their ordered parameter configuration; both bounds are sharp. In rank two, we construct two-dimensional families of pairwise nonisomorphic equivariant fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. For a fixed fourfold, we also show that the closure of the anti-invariant factor family in an associated OG10 compactification is an integral projective Lagrangian subvariety.

papers.title: schubmult: Symbolic algorithms and input-sensitive bounds for Schubert multiplication
papers.abstract: We present schubmult, a GPL-licensed Python system for exact multiplication of ordinary, double, quantum, and quantum double Schubert polynomials, as well as independent-alphabet triple and quantum triple products.
