Its central algorithm expands one factor into filtered column paths and couples them to Pieri computations on the other factor. Dynamic programming shares intermediate states, and the algorithm returns every Schubert-basis coefficient as an exact arithmetic circuit. We prove input-sensitive operation bounds for the entire product, not just a selected coefficient: for inputs of minimal rank $n$, the classical algorithms have complexity $2^{O(n\log n)}$ and polynomial complexity in $n$ for fixed Lehmer-code lengths. The quantum algorithms have the same general bound and polynomial complexity when, in addition, the number of nonzero entries in the Lehmer code of $v^{-1}$ is fixed. We describe the implementation and distinguish it from the algorithms analyzed, verify computations against independent routines and exact identities, and report reproducible timings for flag and Grassmannian workloads. Parabolic quantum products are treated separately via the Peterson-Woodward comparison.

papers.title: Exploring 3-CNF Formulas Generated From Partial Steiner Triple Systems
papers.abstract: Steiner triple systems (STS) and subsets of these known as partial STS (PSTS) are combinatorial objects that have received substantial interest from mathematicians since their introduction in 1847. Over the last three decades, (P)STS have found applications in diverse fields ranging from digital circuit testing to wireless transmission. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the triple in (P)STS allows for a mapping to 3-conjunctive normal form (3-CNF) formulas, the Boolean formula used as input to 3-SAT. Prompted by this ready conversion of (P)STS to 3-CNF formulas and numerous real-world applications of (P)STS, we explore the intersection of (P)STS with 3-SAT and its counting version \#3-SAT. We explain the properties of (P)STS-generated 3-CNF formulas in terms familiar to the SAT community and experimentally compare them against randomly-generated 3-CNF formulas. We find that PSTS-3-CNF formulas are statistically distinct from randomly generated 3-CNF formulas, in both probability of satisfiability and expected solution count.

papers.title: Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
papers.abstract: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

papers.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 5: cyclic total variation
papers.abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses \emph{exactly} to \(β_c(n)=β_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(γ_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the \emph{linear} statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\sqrt{K_0N}\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/β_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.

papers.title: On open weakly 2-semiconvex sets with nonempty 2-nonsemiconvexity-point sets in three-dimensional Euclidean space
papers.abstract: We study general topological properties of open weakly $2$-semiconvex sets in real three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$. An open set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is called weakly $2$-semiconvex if through every boundary point of the set there passes a closed half-plane that does not intersect the set. The largest subset of the complement of a given set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every closed half-plane intersecting this subset also intersects the given set is called the $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set corresponding to the given one. We prove that the nonempty $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set corresponding to an open weakly $2$-semiconvex set is open and weakly $2$-semiconvex. We also construct a weakly $2$-semiconvex domain whose $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set is an unbounded domain that can be either convex or nonconvex.

papers.title: Stochastic Dominance in Discrete Parking Processes on Graphs
papers.abstract: In a recent study on the one-dimensional discrete parking process, it was conjectured that the number of occupied sites in the sequential model first-order stochastically dominates its static counterpart on any path graph. In this paper, we first prove this conjecture for all path graphs and then explore whether stochastic dominance holds for general graph topologies. We show that the property extends naturally to all cycle graphs, and an exhaustive computational analysis confirms that it holds for all 31 connected simple graphs with fewer than 6 vertices. For graphs with 6 or more vertices, we demonstrate that this dominance does not hold universally by constructing explicit counterexamples in which the static model dominates the sequential one; moreover, while one model always dominates the other for all connected graphs with up to 7 vertices, we show that stochastic comparability fails starting at 8 vertices. We also prove that stochastic dominance is inherited by disjoint unions when all connected components share the same dominance direction, and we exhibit mixed unions in which stochastic comparability is either preserved or lost. Finally, supported by algorithmic computations, we formulate a conjecture proposing that the dominance of the sequential model over the static one holds for all graphs with maximum degree at most 3.

papers.title: Robust Decoupled Input Filtering for Internal Model Principle-Based Output Regulation of Polynomial Exogenous Signals
papers.abstract: Internal model principle-based controllers regulate polynomial references and disturbances exactly, but only asymptotically, and their transient input can peak and oscillate, increasingly so as the degree of the exogenous signals grows. A filter placed in series with the plant smooths the command but alters the closed-loop spectrum and can destroy stability. We propose an architecture that keeps the filter outside the loop the regulator stabilizes: the internal model is driven by the error of an ideal, unfiltered copy of the plant, the physical plant receives the filtered command, and an auxiliary plant copy absorbs the mismatch between the two inputs. If the filter satisfies blocking conditions at the origin, any gains that stabilize the unfiltered loop can be combined with any such filter without losing regulation of the true error. Under additive plant uncertainty, we derive a small-gain condition that guarantees robust stability and regulation. On a scalar plant, the proposed controller produces a smoother input and a larger input-delay margin than the unfiltered one, and it maintains regulation under a large loss of actuator effectiveness. On a three-mass chain, its tolerance to unmodeled actuator dynamics and delay stays essentially constant as the regulator is made more aggressive.

papers.title: Chaotic-Periodic Alternation in a Financial System with Double Delays
papers.abstract: In this paper we present the chaotic-periodic alternation phenomenon within a three-dimensional nonlinear financial system subjected to Pyragas-type time-delayed feedback, as well as the lag effect of the interest rate in the price index dynamics. Through numerical analysis, transitions to chaos, including period-doubling cascades, period-halving routes, and incommensurable-period dynamics are characterized. The emergence of chaotic-periodic alternation are found and described. Results suggest that minor timing misalignments in the inner dynamics of a financial system, as well as those considered in the feedback loop can induce systemic volatility.

papers.title: Conformal Risk Certificates for Portfolio Optimization Under Uncertainty: A Gated Reinforcement-Learning Approach
papers.abstract: Reinforcement-learning portfolio policies can optimize allocations from prices, covariances, and prior positions, yet they lack a calibrated, replayable mechanism for certifying that a proposed allocation respects a bounded risk envelope before execution. Regulators increasingly expect automated portfolio systems to provide exactly this kind of pre-trade audit trail, interpretable risk limit, and human-oversight mechanism. Gated Conformal Semantic Risk Control addresses this gap by separating return-seeking allocation from text-conditioned downside-risk verification. An instruction-tuned language model maps timestamped disclosures into schema-validated semantic risk states over macro, liquidity, earnings, and sector channels. These states induce correlated ellipsoidal factor-shock uncertainty sets whose conformal radii are calibrated by rolling finite-sample prediction over localized semantic nonconformity buckets. An asymmetric second-order cone gate then checks each raw PPO proposal against a certified worst-case semantic loss budget. The gate stays inactive for compliant proposals and intervenes only when that budget is exceeded. In walk-forward out-of-sample tests on nine liquid U.S. Select Sector SPDR ETFs, Raw PPO earns a 12.7% annual return while incurring a 4.05% semantic violation rate. Gated-CSRC removes all observed out-of-sample semantic limit breaches while retaining an 11.7% annual return. This 100-basis-point auditable safety premium is smaller than the yield loss imposed by unconditional hard projection, and exact McNemar testing confirms the compliance gain at $p < 10^{-15}$. Loughran-McDonald lexicon controls and time-shuffled text controls fail to reproduce this certificate.

papers.title: Faithful filtering of constrained quantum records: Local limits and collective advantage from loops
papers.abstract: Weak probes can record whether neighboring spins are aligned without revealing their common orientation. Reading the probes can then herald a projection of an unknown spin state onto the aligned subspace that preserves every coherence within it. We ask how often this projection succeeds when the probes are read separately or jointly. For binary pure product records and zero false positives, we derive the exact optimum over all separable measurements, and hence over all local operations and classical communication. It is the probability that one-sided local witnesses exclude every alternative, and simultaneous local measurements attain it. Joint readout can do better by accepting coherent combinations of ambiguous outcomes in which the alternatives cancel. For pairwise parity records on a connected simple graph, it beats every local strategy exactly when the graph has a loop, at all record overlaps strictly between zero and one. For general binary linear records, the condition is an irreducible dependency among at least three records. The advantage lowers the leading power of the efficiency at weak recording. On a triangle the efficiency becomes linear rather than quadratic in the witness probability, and a three-pulse coherent-light receiver captures this gain with a single click. Extensions treat targets spanning several patterns and a noisy comparison at a common output fidelity.

papers.title: Real positive definite counterexamples to a monotonicity conjecture for the $q$-permanent
papers.abstract: The $q$-permanent $P_q$ of an $n\times n$ matrix weights the term of each permutation $σ$ by $q^{\inv(σ)}$, where $\inv(σ)$ is the number of inversions of $σ$. It interpolates between the determinant ($q=-1$) and the permanent ($q=1$). Extending a conjecture of Bapat on $[-1,1]$, it was conjectured in 2010 that the $q$-permanent of every non-diagonal real symmetric positive definite matrix is strictly increasing on an interval $(\varepsilon,+\infty)$ with $\varepsilon<-1$. In this note, we disprove this conjecture. An explicit real symmetric positive definite integer matrix of order five, whose $q$-permanent has only nine nonzero terms, satisfies $P_{14}(A)>P_{15}(A)$. A sparse family shows that for every real $r>1$ some real symmetric positive definite matrix has a $q$-permanent with negative derivative at $q=r$. The counterexamples can be chosen to be correlation matrices without zero entries or, separately, to have integer entries. We also show that the smallest order of a counterexample is four, and that matrices supported on three coordinates separated by identity blocks fail much closer to $q=1$: in order five already near $q=1.7$, and in order $O(1/(r-1))$ at any prescribed $q=r>1$.

papers.title: Steady-state of Lévy process with general resetting: unreflected and reflected cases
papers.abstract: We study (unreflected and reflected) Lévy processes that are modified at independent Poisson review epochs by a random state-dependent reset map. The first model is unreflected: between resettings the level evolves as a Lévy process, and at a resetting epoch the new level is $F$ of the level seen just before the resetting. The second model is the reflected Lévy process at $0$, but with reset maps chosen from a wider transform-solvable class. In this work, we give contraction-type ergodicity criteria for the existence of the steady-state. We identify this steady-state of the system as the solution of certain stochastic fixed-point equation. This allows to find the Laplace-transform, moments recursions, and regularly-varying-tail formulae. For non-reflected case, the examples include affine deterministic resets $F(x)=cx+b$, random-coefficient resets $F(x)=Cx+b$ with two-point $C$ for the finite-activity Lévy process, spectrally positive Lévy flight, reflected Brownian process. For the reflected cased we analyse affine resetting mechanism $F(x)=cx$, the alternating resetting $F(x)=(B-x)^+$, and uniform proportional resetting $F(x)=Cx$ with $C$ having uniform distribution.

papers.title: Symplectic capacities of 4-dimensional monotone toric domains
papers.abstract: We compute the cylindrical contact homology chain complex associated with a monotone toric domain in $\mathbb{R}^4$. The chain complexes allow us to compute the cylindrical contact homology capacities associated with monotone toric domains with one or two inflection points. These capacities are conjecturally equal to the Gutt-Hutchings capacities defined using $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. Using our results, we find embedding obstructions between toric domains.

papers.title: Foliations, free cores, and Terao's conjecture for seventeen lines
papers.abstract: We prove that freeness is determined by the intersection lattice for arrangements of seventeen lines in the complex projective plane. The proof reduces a possible counterexample to smaller arrangements whose realisation spaces can be computed. A minimal logarithmic derivation defines a foliation; its inflection divisor and a local singularity count imply that the non-free member of a counterexample is nearly free with exponents $(7,10)$. Deleting four lines then produces a thirteen-line arrangement whose second Chern class is controlled by a combinatorial deficit. When the deficit is four, the remaining arrangement is free with exponents $(6,6)$. An exact covering argument places the necessary thirteen-line cores in four finite classes, containing $3{,}829{,}691$ lattices. We compute their realisation spaces and reconstruct all relevant seventeen-line extensions, including specialisations of positive-dimensional families. Among the candidate lattices, exactly sixteen admit a non-free realisation; they are rigid and have no free realisation. Together with the known cases, this establishes Terao's conjecture for central arrangements of at most seventeen planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Honest Inference with Heterogeneous Transfer Sources
papers.abstract: Transfer learning can improve precision by borrowing information from external sources, but how much improvement is possible while maintaining valid inference? We address this by studying honest confidence intervals for a target parameter using multiple sources with heterogeneous prespecified discrepancy bounds. Under local information and admissibility conditions, we establish a universal lower bound on interval length for procedures maintaining uniform coverage. A scalar information equation characterizes the bound, revealing how precision depends jointly on source sample sizes and discrepancies. Large source samples need not yield greater precision gains when their discrepancies are large. When discrepancies are unrestricted, honest intervals cannot improve upon the target-only rate, even when all sources are unbiased. For the Gaussian location model, we calculate optimal source weights and construct honest intervals attaining the lower bound order, establishing sharpness. We extend the lower bound theory to semiparametric models through parametric submodels. For the Cox proportional hazards model, we verify the information conditions under which the lower bound applies, including under right censoring.

papers.title: Lagrangian cobordisms and morphisms of persistence modules
papers.abstract: We consider a version of Legendrian contact homology filtered by the action of Reeb chords. In this version, a union of two disjoint exact Lagrangian cobordisms with Legendrian boundary conditions gives rise to a morphism between persistence modules. We discuss a certain algebraic invariant of such morphisms and use it to obtain obstructions to Lagrangian isotopies of the cobordisms, as well as applications to symplectic and contact dynamics.

papers.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with ten vertices
papers.abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with ten vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{25}{384}(10 + 2\sqrt{5})$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of two regular pentagons inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. As for six to nine vertices, the optimum is thus the convex hull of two regular polygons in orthogonal planes. On the combinatorial type of the pair, whose boundary complex is the join of two $5$-cycles, the sharp bound follows from our work on nine vertices. Since an optimal polytope is simplicial, by a result of Horváth and Lángi, it remains to exclude the other $162003$ simplicial types. We do this by sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic, extended by nonnegative multiples of facet polynomials, which are positive on every positively oriented realisation of

papers.title: Twisted algebras of invariant formal power series over monoids
papers.abstract: We develop a general monoid-theoretic framework to construct and study graded and color Hopf algebras of formal power series of bounded degree invariant under group actions. Rather than working with external alphabets of commuting, noncommuting, or anti-commuting variables, we start from an abstract monoid $M$ equipped with a $2$-cocycle twisting $τ:M\times M\to \mathbb{K}$, which is allowed to vanish, a bigrading over a commutative monoid $\mathcal{G}\times\mathbb{N}$ endowed with a bicharacter $φ$, and a group $G$ acting on $M$ via a bigraded action $ρ$ that is quasi-multiplicative with respect to $τ$, coupled with a $1$-cocycle weight function $ω:G\times M\to\mathbb{K}^\times$. By formulating local finiteness, gradings, quasi-multiplicativity, and ideals relative to the non-vanishing of $τ$, we prove that the invariant space $\mathbb{K}\langle\kern-0.2em\langle M\rangle\kern-0.2em\rangle^G$ forms a well-defined bigraded subalgebra of bounded-degree formal power series with a canonical monomial basis indexed by $ω$-admissible orbits. Furthermore, we establish four functorial constructions: embeddings into larger invariant algebras via restricted actions, color tensor product decompositions for direct products and diagonal actions, connected color Hopf algebra structures induced by internal monoid duplication, and quotient color Hopf algebras governed by invariant-retraction pairs with an explicit description of their kernel bi-ideals. As applications, we uniformly recover and extend the classical and twisted Hopf algebras of symmetric and quasisymmetric functions in commuting and noncommuting variables, MacMahon symmetric functions, the full square of symmetric and quasisymmetric Hopf algebras in superspace, symmetric and quasisymmetric functions in partially commutative variables, and signed-symmetric functions associated with the hyperoctahedral group.

papers.title: A convergent Lagrangian scheme for the Navier Stokes equations on the normed Wasserstein space
papers.abstract: We extend the differential structure on Wasserstein spaces of Schichl (arXiv:2508.15140) to the normed Wasserstein space $\mathbb{W}_1$ of finite signed measures, the natural setting for measure differential equations with source terms. We generalize the averaged flow dispersion and expectational flow operators to $\mathbb{W}_1$ and show that along divergence--free tangent vectors they act by measure--preserving flows, and further define source operators. As an application, we construct a purely Lagrangian splitting scheme for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^N$, inspired by the Averaged Flow Approximation Series (AFAS) in \cite{Schichl2025}. We recover, with explicit constants, the classical lifespan bound, a blow--up rate and the inviscid limit with rate $O(η^2)$, and a linearised scheme yields $L^{\infty}$, Hölder, $L^1$ and moment estimates for classical solutions.

papers.title: Quantum synchronization in XX chains under relaxation
papers.abstract: We study stable synchronization in qubit XX chains with site-dependent frequencies and exchange couplings under multi-local amplitude damping noise, extending the uniform-chain results of B. Çakmak et al., [Phys. Rev. A 114, L030202 2026] in several directions. We establish that the dark-mode energies are precisely the eigenvalues shared by all undamped segments separated by the damped sites. Generic stable synchronization of the edge qubits occurs if and only if these segments share exactly one eigenvalue and this eigenvalue is nonzero, in which case every qubit on the support of the corresponding dark mode is synchronized with locking constants independent of the initial preparation. This spectral matching condition identifies the Hamiltonian parameters that support synchronization, while the couplings to the damped sites control the relative oscillation amplitudes. We present analytical examples which show how inhomogeneity can create synchronization absent in uniform chains and turn preparation-dependent locking into generic synchronization. We also calculate the asymptotic pairwise concurrence and prove that, in the single-dark-mode regime, every pair participating in synchronized oscillations remains entangled with a nonzero, constant concurrence.

papers.title: A simple proof of the Bourgade-Sodin-Zeitouni theorem on the excess of the sine-$β$ process for non-integer $\sqrt{2/β}>1$
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of the Bourgade-Sodin-Zeitouni theorem on the excess of the sine-$β$ process for the Paley-Wiener space when $\sqrt{2/β}\in (1,+\infty)$ is not an integer. Let $k(β)=\lfloor\sqrt{2/β}\rfloor$. For almost every configuration, removing any $k(β)$ points leaves a minimal uniqueness set for the Paley-Wiener space. The same conclusion holds for each Bernstein space $\mathcal{B}^p$ of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$-integrable functions with $m(β)<p<\infty$, where $m(β)=β(k(β)+1)-\sqrt{β^2(k(β)+1)^2-2β}$.

papers.title: The memory cost of sequential quantum state preparation
papers.abstract: How much memory does a quantum device need to prepare systems one at a time? We address this question through the lens of quantum resource theories, which formalize physical restrictions on how the memory may interact with the stream of systems it processes. By comparing sequential with collective preparation, we show that under general assumptions both have the same asymptotic memory cost per output. Still, sequential preparation can require an unboundedly larger memory than collective one, and we investigate how this gap depends on the physical restrictions on the allowed interactions. For energy-conserving unitaries, we determine both optimal memory dimensions needed for preparing pure states from an energy eigenstate, and find that the extra memory required sequentially either remains bounded or grows logarithmically with the number of outputs. Under noisy operations, we reveal transformations for which one auxiliary qubit suffices for preparing arbitrarily many independent outputs collectively, while no memory of fixed dimension can deliver them sequentially. Finally, for sequential protocols that repeat a fixed interaction, we show that a $d$-dimensional memory that succeeds for $d^2$ rounds will succeed forever, and that such a sequential preparation is equivalent to quantum catalysis.

papers.title: The exact region of the Average Rectangular Volume and Spearman's rho, with an application to arachnitude
papers.abstract: The average rectangular volume ($\ARV$) of a bivariate aggregation function is the average of its volumes over all axis-parallel rectangles of the unit square; for a copula, it is the expected copula volume of the rectangle spanned by two independent uniform points. We determine the exact region of the pairs $(\ARV(C),ρ(C))$, where $C$ ranges over all bivariate copulas and $ρ$ is Spearman's rho. The region is compact, convex and symmetric, and its upper boundary consists of three analytically parametrized arcs. A previously proposed family of shuffles of Min generates one arc, but only on part of its range; the other two arcs are generated by singular copulas whose supports contain hyperbolic branches. The boundary is continuously differentiable away from its left endpoint $\ARV=\frac{11}{120}$, where it has a vertical tangent. The proof uses a folding transformation and explicit Kantorovich potentials for a family of optimal transport problems. Finally, we show that the arachnitude, a rank correlation used in actuarial practice, is an affine transformation of $\ARV$, so that the result also describes the joint region of Spearman's rho and arachnitude.

papers.title: A Grover-Accelerated Search for Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We show that Grover's algorithm can be used to parametrically accelerate wave-like dark matter searches. Despite having a finite coherence time $τ$, wavelike dark matter can imprint a coherent $O(1)$ phase onto a sensor through a dispersive coupling over an integration time which significantly exceeds $τ$. As such, we show that dark matter can be used as a repeatable quantum phase gate in a quantum device. If the sensor is prepared in a superposition of frequencies, we show that this phase can be transferred to a qubit register and digitized. The qubits are thus available for quantum computational processing in which dark matter can take part as a coherent gate. We show that Grover's algorithm can be used to speed up a search for dark matter in $N_{\rm bins}$ frequency bins by a factor of $\sqrt{N_{\rm bins}}$. Although the technological challenges to implementing such a search remain substantial, this demonstrates that there is no fundamental obstruction to accelerating wave-like dark matter searches with quantum computational techniques over many coherence times.

papers.title: Quantum Computing Enhanced Search for Wavelike Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Identifying a weak, stochastic signal hidden within a broad frequency band is a central challenge in the search for wavelike dark matter. We explore quantum computing enhanced sensing based on the Grover search algorithm to address this problem and find that a long integration time stabilizes the accumulated sensing phase, reducing quantum signal processing (QSP) errors induced by dark matter fluctuations. We further propose alternating the signs of the QSP angles between oracle calls to suppress the coherent accumulation of the intrinsic QSP approximation errors during the search. Combining these strategies in a transmon-based benchmark, we obtain a projected sensitivity to axion dark matter beyond existing astrophysical limits. This opens access to substantial unexplored parameter space across the $10$-$100\,μ\mathrm{eV}$ mass range and offers an accelerated discovery channel for wavelike dark matter. With $10^6$ entangled sensing qubits, the projected sensitivity reaches the QCD axion band. Although illustrated with transmons, the protocol can be adapted to other experimental platforms for wavelike dark matter detection.

papers.title: Critical schemes, jet syzygies, and twisted periods
papers.abstract: We study nonreduced critical schemes with prescribed support on nilpotent orbit closures and on the Kleinian singularity $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, and show that one specified minimal invariant syzygy among the first jet equations fixes their scheme structure. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N$ or $\mathfrak{so}_{2N}$ with Coxeter number $h$ and $p\ge2$ coprime to $h$, the selected polynomial is the coefficient of $s^{p+1}$ in $\det(1-sM)^{p/h}$, with reduced critical locus $\{M^p=0\}$, and the selecting syzygy is equivalent to the twisted period equation of Dubrovin and Feigin-Silantyev. The minimal invariant syzygies of that degree correspond to the lowest nonquadratic twisted periods, which, for $\mathfrak{so}_8$, form the standard representation of triality; in type D the Betti number alone does not determine the scheme. On $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, the selected polynomial is given by a terminating hypergeometric series. Restriction to Slodowy slices commutes with forming critical schemes and their nilradicals. These results determine, uniformly in rank and degree, the rings and nilradical filtrations through which the Schur and Macdonald indices of the corresponding Argyres-Douglas theories are proposed to arise as Hilbert series of arc spaces.

papers.title: Squeezed Light Generation by Cooper Pair Recombination in a Superconductor-Semiconductor Structure
papers.abstract: We theoretically demonstrate squeezed light generation in a compact, electrically driven device utilizing the nonlinear light-matter interaction of Cooper-pair recombination in a hybrid superconductorsemiconductor structure. On the basis of second-order perturbation theory, we developed an effective Hamiltonian which incorporates the electronic component of the interaction as a photon coupling strength coefficient, enabling a model to describe the quadrature squeezing effect of Cooper-pair recombination on the photonic state. We find the squeezing strength to be proportional to the superconducting energy gap squared and device length, as well as increasing with applied voltage. For practical device length, materials and voltage bias, we calculated squeezing values comparable to those of existing squeezed light generation methods when operating below the critical temperature. This theoretically developed concept shows viability for electrically pumped squeezed light generation and can pave the way towards realization of squeezing in compact integrated structures.

papers.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
papers.abstract: Let C_h be the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients of modulus at most h. With the nonzero real roots included, the closure is connected at every height; without them, connectedness becomes arithmetic. We prove that C_h is connected exactly when h=q(q-1) is a pronic number 2, 6, 12, 20, ..., and has at least five components otherwise. At height two this confirms a twenty-year-old numerical observation of Shmerkin and Solomyak on double zeros of power series: apart from 1/2 they form the interval $[1/ρ,1)=C_2\cap(0,1)$, with $ρ$ the tribonacci constant. Disconnection is almost always infinite. For (p-1)^2<h<=p^2-3, $h\neq p(p-1)$, infinitely many components with nonempty interior accumulate at $\pm p$ and $\pm 1/p$, and when h<p(p-1) these four points are themselves components. Next to each square q^2>=16, at least two of the three heights q^2-2, q^2-1, q^2 have infinitely many components accumulating at a common point of (1/(q+1),1/q). Explicit series give infinitely many components at every nonpronic height below 167 other than 1, 3, 4, 9, 25, 63 and 81, and in general at most sqrt(X)+1 nonpronic heights h<=X can have finitely many components, although C_h is a Peano compactum at every height. The proofs compare values and derivatives of all admissible power series near a real double zero; the comparison sets are open and closed in the whole core, so components separated near the axis cannot reconnect elsewhere. On the real axis, the double zeros at heights 1, 3, 4, 7 form sets with infinitely many components; at height one this proves a conjecture of Shmerkin and Solomyak and one of Solomyak on the connectedness locus for pairs of affine maps.

papers.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study online coloring, focusing on the competitive ratio. The best previously known results were (1) a lower bound of $Ω(n / \log^2 n)$ for both deterministic and randomized algorithms by Halldórsson and Szegedy (1994), (2) an upper bound of $O(n / \log n)$ for randomized algorithms by Halldórsson (1997), and (3) an upper bound of $O(n / \log \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms by Kawarabayashi, Yoneda, and Yoneda (2025). In this paper, we improve these results as follows: 1. A new lower bound of $Ω(n / \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms. 2. A new upper bound of $O(n (\log \log n)^2 / \log^2 n)$ for randomized algorithms. 3. A new upper bound of $O(n / (\log \log n)^{2-\varepsilon})$ for deterministic algorithms for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. For randomized algorithms, we nearly close the gap between the lower and upper bounds; the remaining gap is only $O((\log \log n)^2)$. We establish the asymptotic separation between randomized and deterministic online graph coloring. Against an oblivious adversary, a polynomial-time randomized algorithm achieves a competitive ratio asymptotically smaller than any deterministic algorithm can guarantee, even with unlimited computation.

papers.title: Gradient Estimates for Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations with Solution-Dependent Coefficients
papers.abstract: We study a conormal boundary value problem for a class of singular-degenerate quasilinear elliptic equations in divergence form in bounded domains. The leading terms are measurable in the spatial variable and depend nonlinearly on both the solution and its gradient. The singularity or degeneracy is governed by a power of the distance to the domain boundary, with exponent greater than negative one. In particular, the corresponding weights need not belong to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class. Assuming that the weighted mean oscillations of the leading terms in the spatial variable are sufficiently small on small balls and that the domains have Lipschitz boundaries with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish global weighted $W^{1,p}$-estimates for weak solutions with bounded weighted mean oscillation. Our results extend recent estimates for equations whose leading terms are independent of the solution itself.

papers.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szegő logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).

papers.title: Annular Obstructions and Skew-Shape Block Identities
papers.abstract: We give three principal results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, in the rank-two annular exchange model, the frozen row $(2,-3)$ yields the specialized polynomial $1+q^2$, which is not unimodal. Its interpretation as a single-lamination counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026) depends on identifying this row with the shear coordinates of a bridging curve in the same triangulation. We discuss this geometric correspondence using published annular examples; it is not established by the algebraic calculation or formalized in Lean. Second, the same polynomial fails log-concavity, and the frozen row $(1,-2)$ gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, likewise violating log-concavity. These calculations provide obstructions relevant to their Conjecture 1, subject to the same geometric identification. Third, for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, we prove the block-statistic identity of Kahane's Conjecture 4.7 (arXiv:2607.11225v2), using an explicit correction of the root convention. The proof uses commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations, with companion Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. As a consequence, we obtain a bivariate block refinement that is coefficientwise nonnegative in $t-1$ after a common monomial shift in $q$.

papers.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
papers.abstract: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$α$-bundles} and \emph{$β$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold ${\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow G_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic.

papers.title: Zeros of Katz's p-adic Eisenstein series E2
papers.abstract: For every prime $p\geq5$, the zeros of Katz's $p$-adic Eisenstein series $E_2$ on elliptic curves with good ordinary reduction have exactly $\lfloor p/12\rfloor+1$ distinct $j$-invariants. We prove that all these invariants lie in finite unramified extensions of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Their reductions are given by a classical formula involving the supersingular polynomial, and each nonelliptic residue class contains a unique simple zero. For the Legendre family, hypergeometric congruences determine the polynomial of the lifted invariants modulo every power of $p$. We also study isogenies between the zeros. Each $p$-power isogeny class contains at most one zero $j$-invariant, and any two distinct isogenous zero invariants are algebraic over $\mathbf{Q}$. At a fixed cyclic degree, the nonelliptic isogenies give points in a finite divisor over $\mathbf{Q}$ on the corresponding modular curve. Its degree bounds their number and their fields of definition, and excludes several small degrees. The only zeros with complex multiplication have $j=0$ or $1728$. Whether a non-CM zero can have an algebraic $j$-invariant remains open.

papers.title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
papers.abstract: ```text Let $β_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[β_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+θ_0})$ for an absolute $θ_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```

papers.title: Dynamic linear equations in the presence of small perturbations of an interface
papers.abstract: We consider solutions to the initial boundary value problems for both heat and wave equations in two dimensions. In this paper, we aim to advance the development of high-order terms in the asymptotic expansions of current boundary perturbations caused by small perturbations of the shape of a $C^2$-boundary inhomogeneity. Our derivations are rigorously derived by the field expansion (FE) method (formal derivation) and proved by layer potential techniques. It extends those already derived for small-volume inhomogeneities to develop efficient algorithms for determining certain properties of the shape of an inhomogeneity based on boundary measurements.

papers.title: Automatic Continuity for projective clone homomorphisms
papers.abstract: We show that every projective clone homomorphism from a closed function clone containing the automorphism group of a countable homogeneous Ramsey structure $Δ$ in a finite relational language is uniformly continuous. This answers, for such structures, open questions previously raised by Barto, Bodirsky, Marimon, Pongrácz, and the second author in several papers (Bodirsky, Pinsker, Pongrácz, J. Symb. Log. 2021; Barto, Pinsker, SIAM J. Comput. 2020; Marimon, Pinsker, arXiv:2512.01086). Consequently, the polymorphism clone of a first-order reduct $Γ$ of $Δ$ admits a projective clone homomorphism if and only if $Γ$ primitively positively interprets all finite structures; in other words, this ability of $Γ$ is characterised by the absence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, a purely algebraic condition.

papers.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
papers.abstract: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros $ρ_n$ of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity. Selberg proved unconditionally that there exists $λ_0<1$ such that a positive proportion of the zeros $ρ_n$ satisfy $γ_{n+1}-γ_n\leq 2πλ_0/\log γ_n$. Simonič, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh were the first to obtain an explicit value in Selberg's theorem, showing that $λ_0=1- 10^{-3\cdot 10^{13}}$ is admissible. This was considerably improved by Zhao who showed that $λ_0= 1-2.36\cdot 10^{-6}$ is admissible. In this paper, we use a different approach, based on an unconditional variant of Montgomery's pair correlation method, to obtain a substantial improvement of these results, showing unconditionally that $λ_0=0.7892<4/5$ is admissible.

papers.title: A fourth-order dimensionally split exponential time differencing scheme with real and distinct pole rational approximation for non-linear reaction-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel fourth-order, L-stable exponential time differencing (ETD) Runge-Kutta type scheme incorporating a dimensional splitting integrating factor method for the numerical solution of nonlinear reaction-diffusion systems. The method, ETDRK4RDP-IF, is obtained by approximating the matrix exponential operators in the classical dimensionally split ETDRK-IF scheme with an accurate fourth-order, L-acceptable rational function with real and distinct poles. The L-acceptability of the rational approximation guarantees effective damping of spurious oscillations arising from nonsmooth initial and/or boundary data and further eliminates complex arithmetic in the solution of the associated linear systems, thereby enhancing computational efficiency and making the scheme well-suited for parallel implementation in low-level programming languages such as Fortran and C++. Numerical experiments confirm the fourth-order accuracy for a range of reaction-diffusion problems with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, and demonstrate that it outperforms existing standard ETD methods in serial and parallel implementations, yielding CPU time reductions of up to a factor of 20.

papers.title: Divisor Folding and Finite-Group Trace Obstructions
papers.abstract: For a symmetric integer frequency set of size $n$ with Fourier floor $K$, we study a positive trace weighted by the reciprocal of the regularized Fourier multiplier. If restriction to frequencies divisible by $p$ leaves $n/p+O(K^2)$ frequencies, then for $n\ge K^4$ and $p\ll n/K^3$ the original trace differs by $O(n)$ from $p$ times the core trace at the inherited regularization. The transfer reaches cores of size $\asymp K^3$ and preserves vanishing triple density with diverging normalized triple count. We construct exactly regular finite abelian spectra at these scales for which the linear core trace bound fails by a power. The examples use unions of classical semiprimitive cyclotomic classes and also give obstructions in both reflection parities in odd characteristic. Finally, we bound the overlap of lifts of a core by its smallest positive Fourier height and the symmetry of the lifts. These bounds exclude balanced lifts of the binary examples in a range of cyclic extensions and quantify the asymmetry required in odd prime split extensions.

papers.title: Non-local phase transition models for partial singularities
papers.abstract: We study $Γ$-convergence, under appropriate scalings, of the energy functionals \[ F_\varepsilon(u) := [u]_{H^s(Q)}^2 + \int_{Q} W_\varepsilon(u)\,dx, \] where $s \in (0,1)$, $[\cdot]_{H^s(Q)}$ denotes the $H^s$-seminorm in $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$, and $W_\varepsilon$ is a multi-well potential featuring infinitely many equally spaced wells together with additional intermediate wells whose height vanishes at a prescribed rate. Depending on this rate, different limiting behaviors emerge, ranging from classical models to new intermediate regimes.

papers.title: Optical trapping of neutral atoms via magnetic-dipole transitions
papers.abstract: Optical trapping of neutral atoms is almost universally described as an electric-dipole (E1) effect. We show that the magnetic field of light, acting on a magnetic-dipole (M1) transition, can induce an ac Zeeman shift significantly larger than the ac Stark shift, thereby enabling magnetic trapping. We construct the M1 polarizability tensor and identify a critical detuning $δ_c$, independent of optical power, below which the magnetic interaction dominates. We analyze suitable trapping parameters and possible loss mechanisms, particularly for the intraconfigurational transitions $^3H_6\rightarrow{}^3H_5$ of erbium at $1437.13$~nm and $^5I_8\rightarrow{}^5I_7$ of dysprosium at $2418.84$~nm. We propose two trapping configurations: a hybrid magnetic/electric optical tweezer and an optical lattice with separated magnetic and electric antinodes, producing state-dependent purely magnetic and purely electric trapping wells. Our results present optical magnetic fields as a suitable resource to expand the toolbox for atomic manipulation.

papers.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $δ_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.

papers.title: A note on the intractability of enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression
papers.abstract: We show that, given a Horn expression and a family of inclusion-wise maximal satisfiable subsets of its clauses, deciding whether there exists another maximal satisfiable subset is NP-complete. As a consequence, unless P=NP, there is no output-polynomial time algorithm enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression.

papers.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
papers.abstract: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.

papers.title: Newton non-degenerate holomorphic foliations and their separatrices
papers.abstract: In this paper we study germs of holomorphic foliations in the complex plane that are Newton non-degenerate. This is an algebraic condition attached to the Newton polygon of the foliation, analogous to the one defined by Kouchnirenko for analytic curves and, more generally, hypersurfaces. As in this case, the condition of Newton non-degeneracy for foliations can be identified through the comparison of two numerical invariants: the Newton number - a computation involving simple geometric data of the Newton polygon - and the Milnor number. The Newton number is never greater than the Milnor number, and the foliation is Newton non-degenerate if and only if they are equal. The assumption that a foliation is Newton non-degenerate imposes conditions on its set of separatrices. We prove that, under this hypothesis, the foliation has no weak separatrices and, hence, all its separatrices are analytic. We also give a description of the set of separatrices of a Newton non-degenerate foliation, which is sufficient to characterize the foliation as Newton non-degenerate when it is of generalized curve type. This allows us to prove that the property of being Newton non-degenerate is topologically invariant for foliations of generalized curve type.

papers.title: Progression-free sets in class $2$ and arbitrary finite groups
papers.abstract: We study progression-free sets in arbitrary finite groups. We transfer sharp upper bounds from abelian groups to nilpotent groups of class $2$, and from nilpotent groups to arbitrary groups. Combining a recent result of Raghavan with the author's theorem on large subgroups of class $2$ gives \[ r_3(G) \, \leq \, C \, |G|\exp\left( -c\frac{(\log|G|)^{1/6}}{(\log\log|G|)^{1/3}}\right) \] for every finite group as $|G|\to\infty$. This improves the estimates obtained by using the abelian subgroup supplied by Pyber's theorem.

papers.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
papers.abstract: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. The random splits determine its weight in each role. From this representation, we prove an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of the cross-validated estimate. For a given splitting scheme with a common training set size, the variance is a function of these weights, with constants of the model, the metric, and the population. It covers metrics averaged over observations, such as mean squared error, and over case--control pairs, such as the AUC. The identity shows which schemes to use. The variance decomposes into sampling variance, which depends only on the training size, and variance due to the random fold splitting, which arises when the weights change from one draw of the splits to the next. K-fold cross-validation, whose weights are equal across observations by design, is therefore variance optimal at first order; Monte Carlo and bootstrap cross-validation are not. The first-order variance of K-fold does not depend on K, and under reasonable conditions on the model leave-one-out has the smallest variance of any K-fold scheme. For the AUC the same holds for leave-pair-out, which evaluates every case--control pair. Finally, we show the cross-validated estimate is asymptotically normal with the identity's full variance. Together, these results provide a general theoretical foundation for inference on cross-validated performance and establish principles for selecting variance-optimal cross-validation designs.

papers.title: Finite-Key Readiness and Authentication-Key Replenishment in QKD-Assisted UAV Edge Computing
papers.abstract: A service that needs fresh quantum keys must wait for key release, and may be denied it, before protected computation starts. We quantify this cost for a trusted stationary UAV serving two ground gateways, each obtaining its keys from one finite-key decoy-state BB84 attempt with parameters fixed in advance. A count-level Monte Carlo model, reproduced by a semi-analytic model, links key acceptance to protected upload, computation, and download, including failed attempts and hover energy. At 26~dB effective optical loss, with authentication hashing at its proxy-benchmarked, near-zero cost, fresh keys raise the 95th-percentile completion time of both tasks from 10.37 to 28.65~s; hover energy grows in proportion. The scalar rate models evaluated here miss the deadline limit on the block size. The pulse budget lies in a window bounded below by authentication-key replenishment and above by the deadline; for a fixed source, channel, and acceptance model, the authentication debit shifts the floor, whereas hashing cost does not. At a 35-s deadline the largest tested loss with a non-empty window is 27~dB at 1\% misalignment and 22~dB at 2\%; at 3\% no tested setting has one. Conditional on the assumed acquisition probability, the selected configurations meet this deadline with simultaneous lower confidence bounds of 96.9--97.3\% on held-out trials, at 26~dB and at 18--20~dB with 2\% misalignment. A high-cost stress reference that charges hashing in full narrows the window and lowers these loss limits to 26 and 20~dB at the reference processing capacity. A small rise in error rate or loss pushes the deadline probability well below its target and drains authentication keys, while the protocol's security parameter is unchanged.

papers.title: Structure of correlations for the single-$j$ model using quantum information theory
papers.abstract: We say that a system undergoes a quantum phase transition when the mean-field ground state of a given Hamiltonian spontaneously breaks its symmetries depending on the Hamiltonian parameters. It is a widely accepted view that this phenomenon enables the mean-field state to absorb the maximum amount of correlations without losing its mean-field structure. However, it is still uncertain how those correlations are incorporated within the mean-field state and how the correlation structure changes when we get closer to the exact ground state by restoring the symmetries. In this work, we answer these questions by studying the single-$j$ model, which is a realistic fermionic nuclear model with abelian and non-abelian broken symmetries. We find that both types of symmetries have very different effects for the correlations within the mean-field state. This makes unclear the concept of the symmetry breaking process as a mechanism to absorb the maximum amount of correlations. Moreover, the symmetry restoration redistributes existing `fake' correlations between paired orbitals to more complex subsystems.

papers.title: Quantum Thermal Transistor via Nonlinear Environmental Coupling
papers.abstract: Thermal amplification enables sensitive control of heat currents, providing a basis for heat management and thermal signal processing in quantum devices. For a harmonic oscillator coupled to emitter, collector, and base thermal reservoirs, we recover the absence of thermal amplification when system-reservoir interactions permit only single-quantum exchange. A controlled weak-nonlinearity expansion, supported by numerical stationary solutions, shows that two-quantum exchange at the emitter enables amplification and predicts its onset. When two-quantum exchange dominates at the emitter and collector, varying the base temperature redistributes populations between even and odd oscillator sectors. This changes the emitter and collector heat currents far more than the base current, enabling large thermal amplification. We propose a realization using a longitudinally coupled auxiliary two-level system and bath spectral filtering, specifying conditions for its elimination to yield the required oscillator dynamics. These results establish nonlinear system-reservoir coupling as a resource for controlling heat flow and enabling thermal amplification.

papers.title: Measuring Kaplan--Meier Overestimation Under Competing Risks: Event Ordering, Quantification, and Exact Inference
papers.abstract: Competing risks arise when individuals may experience multiple mutually exclusive event types. Competing events are frequently treated as censoring and analysed using Kaplan--Meier (KM) methods, which overestimate real-world event risks. While the existence of KM overestimation is well known, its determinants, magnitude, and inferential properties remain poorly characterised. We develop a nonparametric framework that treats competing risks overestimation as a statistical quantity in its own right. We show that competing event frequency alone is insufficient to characterise KM overestimation and develop an event ordering theory describing how temporal event allocation influences overestimation. Based on these results, we derive a closed-form Total Overestimation Diagnostic (TOD) that quantifies total KM overestimation directly from routine survival analysis output. We establish exact error equivalence results for both cause-specific and total overestimation. In particular, Product Limit Error Equivalence shows that inference for TOD reduces exactly to ordinary overall survival estimation. Simulation experiments validate the theoretical results and show that independent censoring primarily affects precision rather than overestimation magnitude. Across six benchmark competing risks datasets, cause-specific overestimation is characterised by both total overestimation and temporal event allocation. These results provide a practical framework for assessing competing risks relevance and determining when cumulative incidence methods should be preferred to naïve KM risks. The proposed framework transforms competing risks overestimation from a qualitative warning into a measurable quantity that can be routinely quantified, interpreted, and incorporated into reporting practice.

papers.title: Shifted Lagrangian structures and syzygies on Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.abstract: In \cite{FMR25}, Fantechi--Miró-Roig show how to construct new Lagrangian subspaces of the moduli of simple perfect sheaves on a K3 surface from a given one. We reinterpret their construction using the tools and flexibility of derived algebraic geometry. This allows us to generalize from K3 surfaces to (possibly singular) Calabi--Yau schemes of arbitrary dimensions.

papers.title: Regularity of minimisers for the $p$-distance functional
papers.abstract: We consider regularity of minimisers of the $p$-distance functional $\mathcal{F}[u]=\int_Ω\mathrm{dist}(Du,K)^p \mathrm{d}x$ where $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{N \times n}$ is a compact set. We distinguish the scalar and vectorial cases, and consider geometric conditions on $K$ where regularity can be improved.

papers.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
papers.abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a computation of the transverse Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple computation of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even cohomology. This is then applied to the classification of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we study the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,1}$ as well as complements of star-shaped configurations of rational curves in K3 surfaces, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.

papers.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
papers.abstract: We study the probability that the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge3$, stays above a level $-h_N$ throughout the lattice $N$-blow-up of a bounded Lipschitz domain, when $h_N$ is close to the entropic-repulsion height $\sqrt{4g_0\log N}$. Two mechanisms compete: a collective upward displacement of the field, whose cost is governed by capacity, and the suppression of the remaining local violations, whose cost is their expected number, both of which are of order $N^{d-2}/\log N$ exactly in the window $h_N(β)^2=g_0(4\log N+\log\log N+2β)$. We obtain a sharp asymptotic rate expressed through a variational problem combining a Dirichlet energy with an exponential potential inside this critical window. Outside this window we obtain the asymptotics at the appropriate moving speeds: capacity alone governs the cost as $β\to-\infty$, and the expected number of violations as $β\to+\infty$. As an application, we derive lower-deviation bounds for the cover level of a macroscopic body by random interlacements, which determine the order of decay at the transition.

papers.title: Nonparametric Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Mixtures of Logistic Regressions
papers.abstract: Mixtures of logistic regressions provide a flexible framework for modeling binary responses, extending standard logistic regression to accommodate unobserved heterogeneity while retaining an interpretable regression structure. In this paper, we study such models with an unspecified mixing distribution. We analyze a sieve nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) and derive nonasymptotic bounds on the estimation error of the resulting mixture regression function under both fixed and random designs. Our results reveal an explicit tradeoff between statistical estimation error and the approximation error induced by the sieve radius, from which we derive convergence rates under several tail conditions on the mixing distribution. For computation, we propose a finite-particle algorithm that approximates the sieve NPMLE by optimizing the locations and weights of a finitely supported mixing distribution. The method offers numerical advantages over existing algorithms and comes with rigorous convergence guarantees. For any fixed dataset, we establish global convergence of the likelihood to the restricted NPMLE value when the number of particles exceeds a finite threshold. When the true mixing distribution is finitely supported, we further establish uniform global convergence guarantees and derive error bounds that separate algorithmic and statistical errors. Our analysis also yields a denoising bound for the mixing distribution and an identifiability result that complements existing results in the literature.

papers.title: Sharp regularity results for variational integrals asymptotic to the $p$-Dirichlet integral
papers.abstract: We consider the regularity for minimisers of $\int_ΩF(Du) \mathrm{d}x$ where $F(z) \approx |z|^p$ in suitable senses at infinity. Depending on the strength of this asymptotic condition, we discuss various regularity results, and by means of counterexamples we show they are sharp. An effort is made to obtain results without assuming unnecessary regularity of $F$ while covering the full range $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
papers.abstract: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.

papers.title: Analytic and optimized approximations to the median of the gamma distribution
papers.abstract: The median $ν_Γ(α)$ of the gamma distribution has no closed form, but its behavior at both ends is known: it is asymptotic to $2^{-1/α}e^{-γ}$ (with $γ$ being the Euler-Mascheroni constant) as the shape parameter $α\to 0$, and approaches $α- 1/3$ as $α\to \infty$. We write approximations as interpolations $(1 - g)ν_0 + gν_\infty$ between two elementary-function bounds or approximations, each exact in one limit, with an interpolator $g(α)$ going from 0 to 1, and compare three such forms: a first one between previously proven bounds, a second ending in an approximation from the beta median that is exact at $α= 1$ but does not quite approach $α- 1/3$ as $α\to \infty$, and a third one, between bounds proved here, that corrects the large-$α$ end of the second. For each form, the ideal interpolator's slope at 0, approach to 1, and value at $α= 1$ are derived in closed form. Rational interpolators with every coefficient set in closed form from these properties, with no numerical fitting, reach a worst relative error of 0.0011 over all $α> 0$, with absolute error below 0.0002. Fitting some of these or other coefficients numerically to minimize the worst absolute-or-relative error then trades accuracy against complexity: the Pareto frontier reaches 0.000087 with two fitted constants and 0.000041 with five, and from two on uses degree-4 rationals of the second form with no $α^2$ term in the numerator. The proofs that the end functions of the first and third forms are bounds are machine-checked in Lean 4.

papers.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
papers.abstract: Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. We investigate these differences using the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) as an exemplary problem setting. We first establish the relationships between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. Since B&B and $A^*$ admit numerous algorithmic enhancements, we focus on relatively basic implementations. This allows us to examine the fundamental differences between the methods rather than compare the performance of state-of-the-art solvers. By using the same lower bound and best-first node selection, we isolate the effects of the search mechanisms, particularly the identification of equivalent states reached through different scheduling decision sequences. Experiments on 480 benchmark RCPSP instances show that graph-based $A^*$ substantially outperforms the B&B variants considered. With additional pruning rules, $A^*$ proves optimality for all 480 instances, compared with 445 for best-first B&B under the same time and memory limits. Depth-first B&B uses less memory and can find feasible solutions even when the search does not finish within the time limit. Stronger linear programming relaxations reduce the search space but introduce considerable computational overhead. Our findings highlight the importance of duplicate-state detection and clarify the computational trade-offs between the search approaches. These insights can help researchers select an appropriate method and identify opportunities to incorporate effective mechanisms from one approach into the other.

papers.title: Cotangent-lift inference of stochastic microbial dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the parameter estimation for the stochastic logistic and Lotka--Volterra diffusions from discrete, irregularly spaced observations corrupted by measurement noise, a setting typical of microbiome time series. For the logistic equation, the growth rate acts as a time change and does not enter the stationary law, so it can be identified only from the temporal structure of the data. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimator of the Euler scheme, with the observations taken as the states, coincides with the regression of log-increments on abundances used in the literature, and we characterise what this estimator cannot see under measurement noise: for the linearised dynamics, the law of consecutive pairs of observations is invariant along an explicit one-parameter family of relaxation rates and noise levels, and the regression converges to a limit set by the noise. Treating the true abundances as latent, we compute the likelihood with a Gaussian moment filter and show that measurement noise is precisely what couples the filter states across samples. The exact gradient is then the backward recursion of the discrete cotangent lift, whose cost, two to three likelihood evaluations, does not depend on the number of parameters, and we give the covector map of each filter step in closed form. In simulations, the latent estimator recovers the relaxation times, noise levels and interaction strengths that the regression biases, while larger communities require prior information on the interactions. In gut microbiome time series it attributes most of the variability of a dominant genus to measurement noise and estimates its relaxation time at about $64$ hours, with a large standard error.

papers.title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms for machine learning, chemistry, and cryptanalysis often assume coherent access to classical data at negligible physical cost. We instead treat data loading as a hardware process and quantify the dynamic energetic cost of a quantum random access memory (QRAM) query on a superconducting processor. Using the metric-noise-resource framework, we relate query fidelity and power to gate duration, relative two-qubit drive strength, and the distribution of attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, while accounting for thermal photons and gate errors. We analyze the linear-depth multiplexer and the noise-resilient bucket-brigade architectures, adapting the latter to a native superconducting gate set and refining its fidelity analysis using the fully decomposed gate schedule. For a representative bucket-brigade QRAM query with a $12$-qubit address register we obtain a query fidelity of $0.969$. The query consumes $3.51\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{J}$ of dynamic energy, corresponding to an average dynamic power of $4.38\,\mathrm{W}$ and a peak of $64.4\,\mathrm{W}$. Our optimization shows that, at fixed target fidelity, the operating point and attenuation profile can change the average power by a factor of two or more.

papers.title: $\mathbb Z$ is Diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 28 unknowns
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with deg $F=4$ and $n=393$. In this paper, we prove the existence of such a polynomial $F$ with $n=28$.

papers.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We show that, given a very general cubic threefold $X$, any smooth cubic threefold stably birational to $X$ must be isomorphic to $X$. The method applies as well to other Fano 3-folds, like the sextic double solid, and the quartic threefold. We also discuss the higher-dimensional case.

papers.title: Scott spectra of distributive continuous lattices
papers.abstract: Let \(L\) be a distributive continuous lattice. We prove that the hull--kernel topology on \(\Spec(L)\) is the Scott topology of the inclusion order if and only if \(σ(L^{\op})=\upsilon(L^{\op})\). The necessary implication and the algebraic case are known. We prove sufficiency for arbitrary distributive continuous lattices, thereby obtaining the spectrum characterization requested by Lawson and Mislove. The proof embeds \(L\) into a continuous lattice that is both a frame and a coframe, and transfers the Scott topology of the spectrum along the induced map of spectra.

papers.title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of transverse oriented $n$-planes at infinity
papers.abstract: Let $P, Q$ be two oriented transverse $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, $n\geq 2$, which satisfy the equality in the Lawlor--Nance angle criterion.
