We prove that any stationary integral $n$-cycle in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with $[P]+[Q]$ being the tangent cone at infinity, in both the current and varifold senses, is a translation of $[P]+[Q]$ or of a Lawlor neck.

papers.title: Regularity of $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic functions with applications to stable minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We show that the derivative of a $Q$-valued $C^1$ function on an $n$-dimensional domain that is locally harmonic on its regular set is locally Dirichlet minimising, and that its branch set coincides with that of its derivative. As a consequence, we get that a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is $C^{1,α}$ and that its branch set is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable when $n\geq 3$ and discrete when $n=2$. Our methods are directly applicable to the regularity theory of stable minimal hypersurfaces. We show that a multi-valued Lipschitz function whose graph is a two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal $n$-dimensional hypersurface with locally $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-finite singular set, and whose Lipschitz constant is sufficiently small is in fact multi-valued $C^{1,α}$. As a consequence, we obtain optimal regularity conclusions for a branched sheeting theorem of Bellettini for singular immersions. When $n=2$, we obtain stronger conclusions and show that locally about a branch point, a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is the real part of a Dirichlet minimiser which is itself obtained from a finite number of holomorphic functions via classical branching, thus giving a full series expansion for the function near the branch point. Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.

papers.title: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes
papers.abstract: The theory of turbo iterative decoding was brought into the quantum coding framework through the development of quantum serial turbo codes and quantum block turbo codes. In this paper, we present a theory for multidimensional quantum block turbo codes, a turbo decoding technique for multi layer product codes. We describe its algorithm and simulate the performance for the 3D case on a depolarizing channel.
authors: Jean-Louis de Bougrenet de la Tocnaye

papers.title: Bi-Hamiltonian structure and conserved quantities of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell system
papers.abstract:
We study the Hamiltonian and bi-Hamiltonian structure of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell (YON) system, an integrable model of long wave-short wave interaction depending on two real parameters $α$ and $β$, which reduces to the Yajima-Oikawa system for $α=0$ and to the Newell system for $β=0$. For $α
eq0$, a constant shift of the long wave maps the YON system into the Newell system, for which two nonlocal Hamiltonian operators are known. We show that, for $α
eq0$, the system admits no local Hamiltonian operator homogeneous in its natural grading and polynomial in $β$. A nonlocal gauge transformation built on the potential of the long wave makes the first of the known operators local for a single value of its parameter: the transformed system is Hamiltonian, for every $α
eq0$ and every $β$, with respect to a local, non-degenerate Poisson operator, which is the Lie-Poisson structure of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ current algebra. From a recursion operator advancing the hierarchy by two steps, given in explicit weakly nonlocal form, we construct a second, weakly nonlocal Hamiltonian structure, whose nonlocal tail is generated by the three autonomous Lie point symmetries of the system, and prove that both structures are compatible. Since the recursion operator admits no square root and the first structure has no Casimirs, the Lenard-Magri chain splits into two families, seeded by the two simplest conserved quantities. Every flow of both families is local, and all the corresponding Hamiltonians are in involution. As by-products, we relate the Lie point symmetries of the system to its conserved quantities via Noether's theorem, and obtain the conserved densities in closed form by asymptotic diagonalisation of the Lax pair.

papers.title: Scattering thresholds for the NLS equation with polynomially decaying damping
papers.abstract: We study the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a linear damping of strength $a(1+t)^{-θ}$, where $a>0$ and $θ\ge0$, in the whole energy-subcritical range. For $θ>0$, the time-averaged damping vanishes, so that the scattering theory developed in our previous work does not apply. We show that the long-time dynamics is governed by the time integrability of an effective coupling, which decays faster than any power when $θ<1$, polynomially when $θ=1$, and not at all when $θ>1$. In the mass-subcritical case, all solutions are global. They scatter when $θ<1$ and, for $θ=1$, above an explicit exponent depending on $a$. On the other hand, no non-trivial solution is asymptotically free below a second explicit exponent when $θ=1$, and below the short-range exponent $1+2/N$ when $θ>1$. In the mass-critical case, solutions are global below the ground state. Moreover, for $θ\le1$, every solution which survives until its decaying mass becomes subcritical is global and scatters. In the intercritical case, we prove small data scattering and, for $θ\le1$, a dichotomy between scattering and grow-up of the gradient. Finally, in the scale-invariant case $θ=1$, we analyze the range between the two thresholds. We reduce the equation exactly to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a decaying repulsive harmonic potential, and we construct approximate solitary waves with an integrable error. This leads to a conjecture, supported by numerical simulations, on the sharpness of the scattering threshold.

papers.title: Canonical Volumes of Threefolds with Positive Geometric Genus
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus has canonical volume at least $1/30$, with strict inequality when its Euler characteristic is positive. We describe the equality cases as canonical hypersurfaces of degree $28$ in $\mathbb P(1,3,4,5,14)$. These canonical models and their smooth projective resolutions are simply connected. Their coarse moduli space is irreducible and rational of dimension $103$, with finite quotient singularities; all admissible $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein deformations are unobstructed and arise by varying the equation.

papers.title: The strongly local part of nonlinear Dirichlet structures and its energy measures
papers.abstract: This paper substantially extends the results of Sasaya (2026, JFA): we propose a framework for nonlinear generalizations of regular Dirichlet forms and prove that each energy in this framework has a largest strongly local part. We also prove the existence and uniqueness of canonical energy measures of this part, which satisfy convexity and locality properties and, under additional assumptions, certain chain rules in one variable. In particular, our framework requires neither $p$-homogeneity nor strong locality. Moreover, under a Ball--Carlen--Lieb-type upper bound, we prove more detailed chain rules for the directional derivatives of these energy measures. Our framework is applicable both to $p$-energy forms on fractals and to a class of symmetric nonlinear Dirichlet forms in the sense of Cipriani and Grillo~\cite{CG2003}, including those of Orlicz--Sobolev and variable-exponent Sobolev type.

papers.title: On operators with infinitely many spectral components
papers.abstract: For a unital complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$. We prove that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing$ if and only if $\mathscr A$ contains a sequence of non-zero pairwise orthogonal idempotents, and that the number of components of a spectrum is always finite, $\aleph_0$ or $\mathfrak c$. This allows us to extend the spectral depth $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ to a cardinal-valued invariant with values in $\mathbb N\cup\{\aleph_0,\mathfrak c\}$. We show that $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ precisely when $\mathscr A$ contains a dyadic family of idempotents indexed by the full binary tree. In that case, some element has spectrum homeomorphic to the Cantor space $\mathbf 2^{\mathbb N}$. The supremum defining $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ is attained when the spectral classes of $\mathscr A$ are dense and when $\mathscr A$ is commutative, but not in general. We construct a unital complex Banach algebra with $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ and $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\varnothing$. If $Δ$ is the character space of a commutative $\mathscr A$ and $π_0(Δ)$ is the space of all components of $Δ$, then $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\card\bigl(π_0(Δ)\bigr)$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is finite, $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is infinite and scattered, and $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is not scattered. We also prove that the spectral depth is additive with respect to finite direct sums and that the spectral classes are invariant under injective holomorphic functions.

papers.title: Cost controllability and predictive control of input-constrained monotone systems on Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: Cost controllability, relating controllability and a performance measure like the stage cost in model predictive control (MPC), is a key tool in the stability and suboptimality analysis of closed-loop systems. We establish cost controllability for maximal monotone control systems subject to input constraints, a class encompassing finite- and infinite-dimensional port-Hamiltonian systems with colocated input and output. To this end, we employ a recently proposed saturated feedback to derive state-dependent bounds on the closed-loop cost. Our main result is that cost controllability holds globally with semiglobal exponential rate. We first establish this result in continuous time and then extend it to sampled-data systems. Whereas a qualitative detectability-like property is sufficient for asymptotic convergence of the controller, cost controllability requires quantitative rates. We provide two verifiable conditions ensuring cost controllability with explicit exponential rates: coercivity of the sum of system operator and output injection, and exponential detectability of the linear part. Moreover, under the coercivity condition, the resulting MPC scheme without terminal conditions renders the equilibrium globally asymptotically stable with semiglobal exponential rate already for prediction horizon two. We illustrate our results by a nonlinear finite-dimensional system, a semilinear heat equation and a nonlinearly damped wave equation.

papers.title: Phragmén-Lindelöf theorems for parabolic equations of p-laplacian-type
papers.abstract: We consider rigidity properties of ancient solutions to parabolic equations of $p$-Laplacian-type. We start with the degenerate range $p>2$. First, a solution which is bounded above in an intrinsic backward paraboloid is either bounded in an entire half-space, or grows in space at least like a power with a sharp, explicit exponent. This relies on the expansion of positivity and on the Comparison Principle. Then, we turn to the growth in time. Positivity in the paraboloid alone yields no upper rate: we present explicit self-similar solutions, positive in the paraboloid, with $u(0,-T)\simeq T^β$ for every $β\le0$ and every $β\ge1$. For solutions bounded below in the paraboloid, we prove a dichotomy for the infimum of $u(\cdot,-T)$ on a ball whose radius is a fixed fraction of that of the paraboloid at time $-T$: either it is of order $T$ along a sequence of times, or it grows sublinearly, like $T^ζ$ with $ζ<1$ explicit. In the second case, a Harnack-type argument shows that the supremum on the same ball grows at most linearly. Then, we carry out the same program in the singular, supercritical range $\frac{2N}{N+1}<p<2$, where the picture is similar but several roles are reversed. In space, the iteration via the Comparison Principle can only be started from a point lying above an explicit slope, and explicit solutions show that nothing better than a cone bound can be expected below it. The self-similar profiles are unique but only local, and positivity in the paraboloid is compatible with every exponent $β\le1$ and with no exponent in $(1,\frac1{2-p})$. In time, the dichotomy is replaced by an a priori linear bound for the infimum. Similarities and differences between the two ranges are collected at the end of the work.

papers.title: Pseudoconformal characterizations of scattering in weighted Sobolev spaces for non-scaling-invariant mass-subcritical NLS
papers.abstract: We consider mass-subcritical nonlinear Schrödinger equations with finitely many power-type nonlinearities and initial data in weighted Sobolev spaces. In the short-range regime, we prove a pseudoconformal characterization of scattering in the weighted energy space $Σ$. We also establish a fractional counterpart in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1)$, formulated in terms of the boundedness of the order-$s$ pseudoconformal operator. Our results include equations with combined nonlinearities, for which no distinguished scaling symmetry is available. As an application of the fractional theory, we prove small-data scattering in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1]$. The arguments rely on the lens transformation, harmonic-oscillator Strichartz estimates, and fractional harmonic Sobolev estimates.

papers.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.

papers.title: Tolerance complexes of chordal graphs and squarefree symbolic powers
papers.abstract: For a simplicial complex $K$ and an integer $t\ge0$, the $t$-tolerance complex $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ consists of the sets that become faces of $K$ after deleting at most $t$ of their elements. Kim and Lew conjectured that if $K$ is $d$-Leray, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(η(d+1,t+1)-1)$-Leray (the Leray conjecture), and that if $K$ is $d$-collapsible, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(η(d+1,t+1)-1)$-collapsible (the collapsibility conjecture), where $η$ is the Erdős--Gallai number. We prove the collapsibility conjecture for $d=1$ when $t\le3$ or $\dim K\le4$, and for all $t$ when $K$ is the clique complex of a subtree graph of a spider, a class of chordal graphs containing all interval and split graphs; in particular, it holds for nerves of finite families of intervals. For every $d$, we prove both conjectures when $K$ has at most $d+1$ facets, when $K$ has nonzero homology in its top dimension, and when the Stanley--Reisner ideal of $K$ is squarefree stable. The Stanley--Reisner ideal of $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is the $(t+1)$-st squarefree symbolic power of that of $K$, so the Leray conjecture becomes a regularity bound. Using this, we prove the Leray conjecture for flag complexes when $t\le3$, and for all $t$ for independence complexes of bipartite and chordal graphs, and we show that it is preserved under joins. We also construct chordal graphs $H$ for which the Leray number of $\mathcal{T}_t(\mathrm{Cl}(H))$ exceeds its Helly dimension by an arbitrarily large amount, and others for which it depends on the field. Finally, we reduce the case $t=1$ of the Leray bound for $d$-collapsible complexes to a question on intersections of links.

papers.title: Parabolic semiinfinite sheaves on affine flag varieties
papers.abstract: We study sheaves on affine flag varieties of reductive algebraic groups in parabolic semiinfinite settings, generalizing some constructions and results from the work of Gaitsgory and of Achar, Dhillon, and the first author (for the case of the Borel subgroup) and of Dhillon and Lysenko (for characteristic-$0$ coefficients and a particular case of parabolic semiinfinite condition). In particular we define perverse t-structures and Raskin equivalences in this context, and study an analogue of the Gaitsgory sheaf. In future work, these $\infty$-categories will be related to representation-theoretic $\infty$-categories associated with the Langlands dual group.

papers.title: Operational limits of reference renewal for retained quantum-service results
papers.abstract: We implement reference renewal to reconsider retained physical quantum-service results under a prespecified protocol. Twelve transitions retained six results each; ten completed renewal, eight met the prespecified endpoint, and five succeeded using retained results alone. The exact one-sided p=0.0546875 does not establish the recovery hypothesis. Incomplete references, binding failures and sequential waits expose operational limits. Offline reconstruction recovers decisions from preserved counts. Retrospective binding-plus-oracle checking accepts all 60 usable-transition results without renewal. With the exact oracle also supplying calibration scores, the study does not demonstrate incremental numerical-correctness utility of renewal.

papers.title: From Distribution of Extremes With Degradation to the Stress Redundancy Principle
papers.abstract: How a degradation source affects the statistics of the first among many identical independent stochastic particles to successfully reach a narrow target remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impact of degradation on the distributions of first-passage times and exit locations by exploiting the time-dependent fluxes associated with the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation. We also compute the escape probability by solving a mixed boundary value problem. In the large initial population $N_0$ limit, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean first passage time associated with the fastest particle, revealing how the killing field modifies the classical $1/\log(N_0)$ scaling. However, when considering the population size at the time of the first exit, we obtain a specific dependency with respect to degradation, a phenomenon that we call the stress redundancy principle. For a degradation field restricted to a narrow subregion, we use an optimal control approach to derive the optimal trajectory where the fastest escape particles will be concentrated: interestingly, we report here that the optimal trajectories avoid the degradation area depending on killing intensity. Finally, we obtain analytical expressions for the distribution of first exit points along a narrow absorbing arc in two-dimensional regular domains. In addition, for a killing subregion tangent to the target boundary, our computations reveal how geometrical parameters influence the exit distribution. In summary, a killing source can significantly affect the statistics of the fastest diffusing particles, relevant for defining cellular and molecular time scales.

papers.title: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Many image classification tasks have labels that are unchanged by rotations and reflections. Equivariant quantum neural networks incorporate such symmetries by design, but the specific benefit of symmetry is difficult to isolate. Equivariant quantum circuits are usually compared with architectures that also differ in gates, structure or size. Here, we investigate the role of invariance in a controlled setting, classifying images whose labels are invariant under the dihedral group $D_4$. We compare four eight-qubit models with identical encoding, circuit structure and number of trainable parameters, and equivalent dynamical Lie algebras, and benchmark invariant implementations against non-invariant ones in terms of generalization error, robustness to shortcut learning and resilience to a realistic noise model. On four binary tasks, including MNIST and two scientific data sets of galaxies and red blood cells, the invariant models trained on a few tens of images show better generalization than non-invariant ones. Invariance also makes the models immune to orientation shortcuts: when trained with a class-dependent corner watermark, the non-invariant models learn the watermark and often drop to chance level when it is moved. We show that the gain in accuracy of invariant models persists also under a realistic noise model.

papers.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
papers.abstract: Kühnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.

papers.title: Independent Families Under Determinacy-Like Hypotheses
papers.abstract: We generalize the notion of an independent family on $ω$ to $\mathcal{J}$-independent families on an arbitrary cardinal $κ$ and then show that under determinacy-like hypotheses that there can be no such families for reasonable $\mathcal{J}$. This is quite atypical as all other generalizations of the kinds of combinatorial families coming from the theory of cardinal characteristics follow a very different pattern, which will also be explained; in this sense independent families seem particularly special. The base theory assumed throughout is $\textsf{ZF + }$All infinite sets are Dedekind infinite.

papers.title: High-Speed Control of a Fluxonium Qubit via Picosecond Pulses from Josephson Digital Circuits
papers.abstract: We develop a control strategy for fluxonium qubits based on picosecond single-flux-quantum (SFQ) pulses generated by Josephson digital circuits. A major challenge is that SFQ protocols originally designed for transmon control become inefficient for low-frequency fluxonium. In this regime, the asymmetry of flux and charge couplings leads either to excessive leakage or excessively long gate times. We show that this limitation can be overcome by two complementary protocols. The first protocol employs high-frequency SFQ pulse packets applied through the flux channel, offering a simple, analytically transparent, and robust approach for high-fidelity single-qubit control. The second protocol combines phase-shifted flux and charge pulse sequences to enhance the resonant drive and reduce the gate duration. Multilevel simulations demonstrate single-qubit gate fidelities above $99.99\%$; the simpler protocol remains robust under moderate variations of qubit parameters and flux bias, while the combined protocol preserves high fidelity while substantially accelerating the gate. These results establish SFQ-based cryogenic control as a realistic route to fast, accurate, and scalable manipulation of fluxonium qubits.

papers.title: An Eyring-Kramers Formula for Singular Wells
papers.abstract: Understanding the persistence of learned behaviors in AI safety motivates an investigation of the dynamical counterpart to the equilibrium geometry studied in singular learning theory. We analyze this persistence through transitions between singular wells. We establish an Eyring-Kramers formula for a low temperature Langevin diffusion between two compact connected zero components of a real-analytic potential. The wells may be singular and nonisolated, and the unique minimizing gate is a nondegenerate index-one saddle, with gates understood as inclusion-minimal sets meeting every minimizing path. A boundary-gate construction shows that uniqueness of this inclusion-minimal gate is equivalent to every minimizing path passing through the saddle and one such path meeting the communication level only there. Compact semianalytic topology provides a separating function away from a fixed saddle neighborhood; analytic Morse coordinates give matching capacity bounds by first sending the temperature to zero and then shrinking that neighborhood. An anchored energy estimate and a small-ball potential-theoretic identity give uniformity for deterministic starting points. The leading constant is expressed in terms of the sublevel-volume coefficient, a Gamma factor, and the saddle Hessian.

papers.title: The Symplectic Nature of Noncentral Reducible Stratum in SU(2) Character Variety
papers.abstract: Let \(Σ_g\) be a closed oriented surface of genus \(g\geq2\). The purpose of this paper is to use an explicit example, the representation of the surface group $π_1(Σ_g)$ into $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, to investigate the deformation space of the representation variety at a type of singular points, reducible but noncentral representations, and explore the geometric structure of the corresponding stratum in the representation variety and the character variety. In particular, the reduced tangent quadratic cone determines the symplectic structure at the reducible noncentral stratum of the character variety. Such a symplectic structure fits in the ambient character variety $χ\big(π_1(Σ_g),\mathrm{SU}(2)\big)$, where the top stratum of smooth points admits the Narasimhan-Atiyah-Bott-Goldman symplectic structure.

papers.title: Shape Perturbation of the Galerkin Boundary Element Dirichlet-to-Neumann Matrix on Moving Polygons
papers.abstract: For nonlocal interface evolution problems such as the Mullins-Sekerka flow, certain parametric schemes discretize only the interface and approximate the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map by boundary elements. Their error analysis requires bounds on how this discrete operator changes as the polygon moves. In that analysis, the polygons are only Lipschitz and close to a smooth curve only in a Lipschitz norm, the perturbations are controlled only in the energy norm, and the kernels are singular on the diagonal. We study the symmetric Galerkin boundary element matrix on the polygons in a Lipschitz neighborhood of a smooth reference curve. Its first variation, tested against discrete Neumann solutions, is bounded by the energy norm of the perturbation alone. The second-order remainder of the associated mass form is bounded by the product of the energy norm and the Lipschitz norm of the perturbation, so that only one of the two factors needs a uniform bound. On the interpolating polygon, the matrix is consistent with the continuous operator without the logarithmic loss that a pointwise comparison of the kernels would suggest, and its shape derivative is consistent with that of the continuous operator. All bounds are uniform in the mesh size and depend only on the constants of the reference curve.

papers.title: Splitting module-finite extensions over singular local rings
papers.abstract: We study when a module-finite extension of a singular local ring splits as a module over the base. On a Gorenstein curve of positive residue characteristic, weak normality forces splitting for every extension of finite projective dimension. In residue characteristic two the converse holds when two is zero or a nonzerodivisor. A missing square root in the prescribed base gives an explicit nonsplit extension of generic rank four. We obtain a second curve criterion by gluing retractions on the branches and determine all evaluation ideals for coordinate crossings and for \(x^2=y^2u z_1\cdots z_s\) in odd characteristic. For cubic extensions we prove a presentation theorem with arbitrarily many relations. It applies on the blow-up of an ideal generated by a regular sequence of length three, and on the blow-up of a three-dimensional local ring with a quadric tangent cone. A family of matrices satisfying the criterion exists over every residue field in the regular-sequence case.

papers.title: Generalized Cramér-Rao Inequalities Associated with $(h,τ)$-Divergence and $(h,τ)$-Exponential Family
papers.abstract: The Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and exponential family have laid the foundation for information geometry and have been widely generalized. Using Eguchi's theory, the Fisher information metric can be derived from the KL divergence. Based on this metric, Amari and Nagaoka established an information-geometric proof of the classical Cramér-Rao (CR) inequality for finite-support models. Among the various generalizations of the KL divergence, this paper focuses on the $(h,τ)$-divergence and establishes the associated CR inequality, referred to as the $(h,τ)$-CR inequality, using information geometry. We also provide a proof of this inequality based on the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, thereby extending its applicability to models with more general support sets. Under suitable regularity conditions, equality holds in the classical CR inequality if and only if the underlying family is exponential. However, for the $(h,τ)$-CR inequality, this property does not generally extend to the $(h,τ)$-exponential family. We therefore establish an attainable CR inequality for this family. This new inequality extends the attainment result of the classical CR inequality by the sufficient statistic of the exponential family to the $(h,τ)$-exponential family.

papers.title: Smoothed Least-Absolute Conditional Multidimensional Scaling via Iteratively Reweighted Majorization
papers.abstract: Conditional multidimensional scaling combines latent coordinates with observed covariates to fit pairwise dissimilarities. We develop a smoothed l1 formulation using the shifted Charbonnier loss. We prove residualwise sharpness of the quadratic loss majorizer, monotonicity, compact containment, and stationarity of noncollapsed accumulation points. A uniform additive bound quantifies approximation to exact least-absolute conditional stress. The experiments use paired contamination, separately calibrated loss parameters, combined-configuration recovery, and direct checks of the theorem's inequalities.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
papers.abstract: This paper studies the numerical approximation of a mathematical model of coupled flow and viscoelastic deformation in a fractured porous medium including fracture contact mechanics. We consider a mixed-dimensional model, where the fracture is modeled as a co-dimension one object within the porous medium. This model couples Darcy flow in the matrix and fracture, linear viscoelasticity of the matrix and frictional contact mechanics of the fracture surfaces; the contact conditions include normal compliance and a Coulomb friction law. We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme for this problem, using conformal finite elements in space and the implicit Euler method in time. Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution is established, and stability and a priori error estimates are derived. A numerical experiment is performed in which numerical error estimates are computed and compared to the theoretical results.

papers.title: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons: Gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition
papers.abstract: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling of linear systems, such as Landau polaritons formed by a two-dimensional electron gas in a terahertz cavity, is described by the bosonic Hopfield model, and gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition (SRPT). Modulating the magnetic field alone has been predicted to enhance the cycle-averaged coupling and induce a Floquet SRPT. We develop an exact theory of periodically driven Landau polaritons. Including the electric field induced by the modulated flux (Faraday's law), the problem reduces exactly, by Kohn's theorem, to the electronic center-of-mass mode coupled to the cavity, whose Hamiltonian is a sum of squares at every instant. A theorem of Krein then guarantees stability to all orders above a computable drive frequency, the Krein frequency, for which we give a self-contained proof. Below it, the system is stable except within resonance tongues where the drive creates pairs from the vacuum, the dynamical Casimir effect. At high drive frequency the electrons experience the mean field plus a ponderomotive trap (the Fock--Darwin problem), not an enhanced coupling. A gauge theorem excludes a Floquet photon condensate for any band structure, including Kane nonparabolicity, for which we derive a generalized Thomas--Reiche--Kuhn (TRK) sum rule. The predicted transition arises from averaging the coupling in a fixed Landau-level basis, which yields an effective model that violates the TRK sum rule; under driving, gauge invariance also requires the induced Faraday field. The rule to modulate and average the minimal-coupling Hamiltonian, not the parameters of its projection, applies to any linear, minimally coupled system. Instead of an SRPT, magnetic modulation produces dynamical Casimir emission: Faraday-driven polariton--magnetoplasmon pairs at low threshold, and two-color photon pairs with up to 5--10~dB of two-mode squeezing.

papers.title: Ramification of torsion packets on curves with good-reduction Jacobians
papers.abstract: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Write $R=W(k)$ for the ring of Witt vectors over $k$, and $K$ for the field of fractions of $R$. Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus greater than one. Write $J$ for the Jacobian variety of $X$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$ of $K$. In the present paper, we prove that if $J$ has good reduction over $R$, then every point $x\in X(\overline{K})$ such that $[σx-x]$ is torsion for each $σ\in \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ is $K$-rational.

papers.title: Pareto Front Tracing in Higher Dimensions Using Numerical Integration
papers.abstract: We propose a numerical integration approach for tracing the Pareto front of unconstrained continuous multi-objective optimization problems. By stating optimality conditions for weighted sum scalarizations, we derive parametric equations for Pareto critical points, parameterized by the weights. Sensitivity analysis with respect to the weights yields a system of partial differential equations (PDEs). We prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions and derive conditions under which a solution extends to the entire weight space and yields Pareto optimal solutions. A tracing strategy for the resulting PDE system is developed that uses numerical integration along individual weight coordinates using Runge--Kutta methods. We provide an error analysis considering inexact initial solutions, perturbations of the right-hand sides, and numerical integration errors. We investigate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the tracing strategy on convex quadratic problems and WFG examples, where the latter demonstrate the applicability to problems with Pareto fronts consisting of convex and non-convex parts. Comparisons with repeated weighted sum scalarizations and a predictor--corrector method illustrate the computational benefits of the proposed strategy.

papers.title: Asymptotic Robustness of HDG Schemes for the Convection-Diffusion Equation
papers.abstract: The convection-diffusion problem has been studied extensively as an important model for convection-dominated problems. The problem becomes more challenging when the convecting velocity is no longer Lipschitz and merely has Sobolev regularity. In this paper, we use Boyer's extension of the DiPerna--Lions theory for the transport equation to study the vanishing diffusion limit of discretizations of the convection-diffusion equation with Sobolev velocity. In the case of flux-adapted boundary conditions, we prove that a continuous Galerkin discretization converges strongly to the renormalized solution of the transport equation as the diffusion coefficient and mesh size go to zero, without requiring any relationship between them. We refer to this unconditional strong convergence as asymptotic robustness. In the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions, we use the renormalization theory and barrier arguments to prove that a piecewise constant hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin scheme is asymptotically robust, while the continuous Galerkin scheme may fail to converge. Our results indicate that the asymptotic robustness of schemes for the convection-diffusion problem depends on the realization of the boundary conditions as opposed to internal layers.

papers.title: Characterizing Fixed-Treewidth Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: We give the first inductive characterization of planar graphs of treewidth $k$ for each $k \geq 3$. Our definition generalizes the well-known inductive definition of planar $3$-trees and the recent definition of so-called planar quasi-$4$-trees [Förster, 2024]. As a key step, which may be of independent interest, we show that every planar triangulation $G$ of treewidth $k$ admits a tree decomposition of width $k$ where each adhesion set induces a cycle in $G$. As an application of planar quasi-$4$-trees, we show that planar graphs of treewidth at most $4$ have vertex arboricity at most $2$. That is, the vertex-set of every planar graph of treewidth at most $4$ can be partitioned into two sets that each induce a forest.

papers.title: Bounding and Approximating Kostka Numbers
papers.abstract: Kostka numbers, the coefficients of Schur polynomials, count semistandard Young tableaux of prescribed shape and weight. We give a deterministic algorithm for approximating Kostka numbers within a simply exponential factor in the number of variables and the size of the partition. Our approach combines Gurvits capacity bounds for log-concave polynomials with an algorithm for approximating the Gurvits capacity of a Schur polynomial. For a Schur polynomial in $n$ variables indexed by $λ$, we show that the logarithm of the capacity associated with any nonzero coefficient can be approximated to additive error $ε$ in time polynomial in $n$, $|λ|$, and $\log(1/ε)$. The analysis establishes an explicit bounded optimization region and efficient approximate first-order oracles, and handles boundary weights through a factorization into smaller Schur polynomials.

papers.title: Poisson boundaries of lattices in locally compact groups
papers.abstract: For a random walk on a general locally compact group we provide a discretization procedure transforming the walk to one on a lattice of the group, preserving the Poisson boundary and some finiteness of moments.

papers.title: A New Computational Model for the Spin-Free Sum-of-Squares Energy Bounds of Electronic Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: Optimizing spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bounds for electronic Hamiltonians leads to semidefinite programs whose expanded size grows rapidly with the orbital dimension. We derive an exact reformulation of an established spin-free SOS model as a convex quadratic problem over a single symmetric matrix constrained between zero and the identity. Explicit recovery maps connect feasible quadratic-program iterates to certificates in the original SOS formulation, and identify the Frank--Wolfe gap with the separation between recovered primal and dual objectives. We implement the quadratic action through GPU-accelerated Coulomb contractions and solve the reformulated problem using a cached implementation of fully corrective Frank--Wolfe, referred to here as the dimension-reduced simplicial method (DRSM) that caches operator products and optimizes convex-combination weights in a small corrective quadratic program. Numerical experiments cover 65 FCIDUMP models, molecular geometries, and regular hydrogen rings, including original-coordinate recovery checks on nine instances and comparisons with FISTA and a boundary-point SDP solver. On eight H100 GPUs, a cold-start calculation for C$_{720}$ with 10,080 spatial orbitals reaches a freshly recomputed Frank--Wolfe gap of $8.82\times10^{-9}$ hartree in 5.02 hours. Full-space hydrogen-ring calculations reach 10,000 orbitals, with cyclic reduction providing further computational savings. These results show how exact reformulation, data structure exploitation and reuse of Coulomb actions make optimization of the selected large-scale SOS relaxation practical.

papers.title: Reconstructing Numerical Semigroups from Circulant Spectral Dimensions
papers.abstract: The polynomial algebra generated by the spectral moments of a family of circulant graphs consists of all eventually polynomial sequences in the graph order; as an unfiltered algebra, it therefore carries little information about the jumps. We show that its natural power-sum weight filtration retains substantially finer arithmetic data. For a finite jump set $S$ with $\gcd(S)=1$ and $M=\max S$, the relevant invariant is the numerical semigroup $Σ_S=\langle M,M-s,M+s:s\in S\rangle$, which arises from the lengths of closed walks winding around the cycle. We prove that the eventual global filtered dimension is $MD+\lfloor D/2\rfloor+1-M(M+1)-g(Σ_S)$. Restricting graph orders to $n\equiv a\pmod q$, for $q\mid M$, replaces the genus term by the number of gaps of $Σ_S$ in the class $-a\pmod q$; the class $a=0$ gives the genus of the quotient semigroup $Σ_S/q$. These formulas yield an inverse reconstruction theorem: the unrestricted dimensions determine $M$, and the dimensions in all classes modulo $M$ at one common stable degree determine the Apéry set and hence $Σ_S$. We give effective thresholds, exact examples, and a finite-rank algorithm valid in every degree. Reconstruction of the semigroup need not identify the original jump set.

papers.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
papers.abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

papers.title: Rectifiable measures in Ahlfors regular spaces: endpoint constructions
papers.abstract: A theorem of Balka and Keleti implies that on any complete separable metric space $\mathbb{X}$, every locally finite Borel measure $μ$ of packing dimension strictly less than $m$ is "Euclidean-like" insofar as there exist Lipschitz maps $f_i:E_i\subset\mathbb{R}^m\rightarrow\mathbb{X}$ such that $μ(\mathbb{X}\setminus\bigcup_1^\infty f_i(E_i))=0$. An ongoing challenge in geometric measure theory is to understand when this property, called $m$-rectifiability, holds for measures of packing dimension $m$. Towards this goal, we prove that every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q\geq m$ supports $m$-rectifiable doubling measures of packing dimension $m$. The proof of existence of such measures is new even when $\mathbb{X}=\mathbb{R}^n$ and $n>m$. More generally, on every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q>m-1$, we construct $m$-rectifiable, purely $(m-1)$-unrectifiable measures with any prescribed exact Hausdorff and packing dimensions $0\leq s_H\leq s_P\leq q$ with $m-1\leq s_P\leq m$, which are doubling when $s_H>0$. This verifies a conjecture of Badger and Schul. The design of the measures relies on metric cubes with variable scaling, in which the ratio of consecutive side lengths tends to infinity but jumps only on a sparse set of generations, together with Badger and Schul's square packing construction of Lipschitz maps.

papers.title: Examples of homological mirror symmetry via Zariski descent
papers.abstract: This paper considers a general setting in which the Fukaya category of an exact symplectic manifold may be decomposed as a fiber product of Fukaya categories of smaller pieces. We establish a property of Fukaya categories that is mirror to Zariski descent of coherent sheaves. This fits into a natural strategy to prove homological mirror symmetry by a local-to-global analysis. The examples we consider in detail are open Riemann surfaces and exact log Calabi-Yau surfaces, and we provide proofs of homological mirror symmetry in these cases.

papers.title: Electrical Stark Tuning and In Situ Field Sensing of $V_{2}$ Silicon Vacancies in a 4H-SiC a-Plane Lateral pin-Diode
papers.abstract: Silicon carbide has emerged as a highly promising platform for scalable quantum technologies, with the silicon vacancy serving as a robust spin qubit and quantum sensor. However, conventional c-plane 4H-SiC restricts the experimental scheme and resonant optical excitation to the sample's geometry. The usage of a-plane substrates enables more versatile resonant optical access to the color center through the wafer surface. Here, we demonstrate the electrical control and optical addressability of $V_{2}$ (cubic lattice site) silicon vacancies within the intrinsic region of lateral pin-diodes fabricated on a-plane 4H-SiC wafers using a scalable complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) process. Despite extensive semiconductor processing, the integrated color centers exhibit good optical quality, evidenced by narrow optical transition linewidths below 80 MHz at zero bias. These embedded quantum sensors are utilized for in situ measurement of local electric fields at cryogenic temperatures via the Stark effect. Comparisons with macroscopic technology computer-aided design simulations reveal the value of these integrated quantum sensors to help understand cryogenic device behavior, for example in predicting highly localized field crowding. Furthermore, to address the spectral indistinguishability required for quantum networks, we precisely tune the zero-phonon line (ZPL) of individual emitters via the reverse-bias Stark effect. This successfully compensates for the spectral variations of distinct emitters. Following the relaxation of transient charge fluctuations, the Stark-tuned emitters exhibit spectral stability over measurement periods exceeding four hours. Our results establish a-plane 4H-SiC as a robust platform for future interference experiments and quantum photonic integrated circuits.

papers.title: Noetherian connected braided Hopf algebras are affine
papers.abstract: The well-known Wu--Zhang question asks whether every Noetherian Hopf algebra over a field is affine (finitely generated as an algebra). In this paper, we extend this fundamental problem to the braided setting within the monoidal category ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ of left Yetter--Drinfel'd modules over a Hopf algebra $H$. By developing term-rewriting methods based on reduction orderings and prime-word factorizations in free prebraided algebras, we establish explicit expansions for YD-triangular comultiplications. We prove that if $(\mathbb{K}\langle X \rangle, ε)$ is an augmented free algebra in ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ and $I \subseteq \ker ε$ is an ideal invariant under a YD-triangular comultiplication, then every $I$-reducible letter---and consequently every non-empty word in $\langle X \rangle$---can be expressed modulo $I$ as a linear combination of products of $I$-irreducible letters strictly smaller with respect to the reduction order. As a primary consequence, we prove that any right Noetherian connected prebraided Hopf algebra $B$ in ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ is affine, generated by the image of a finite set $X_{I}$ of $I$-irreducible letters. As an application, we show that the braided component $B = A^{\mathrm{co}\,π}$ of a right Noetherian Radford biproduct $A = B \sharp H$ is affine whenever $A_{(0)} \subseteq \jmath(H)$, reducing the affineness of $A$ entirely to that of $H$.

papers.title: Whittaker supermodules for the Takiff superalgebra \mathfrak{osp}(1|2)
papers.abstract: In this article, we classify all simple Whittaker supermodules over the Takiff Lie superalgebra \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)\otimes\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), associated with Whittaker characters defined on the even part of its positive nilpotent subalgebra.

papers.title: Anosov representations from cyclic Higgs bundles
papers.abstract: For every complex simple Lie group G (not of type $E_8$) we construct the minimal Slodowy slice, which is a half-dimensional slice in the character variety of a closed surface group into G, containing the composition of Fuchsian representations with the minimal representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in G and invariant under the mapping class group action. This slice is defined via cyclic Higgs bundles, and we show that when G is not of type $E_8$, the corresponding representations are Anosov, so in particular discrete and faithful, and dominate some Fuchsian representation. For each of these Higgs bundles, we consider the equivariant harmonic map to the symmetric space, and we show it is an embedding and a quasi-isometric embedding with regard to the induced metric. From the cyclicity of these Higgs bundles we are also able to construct an auxiliary harmonic map to a pseudoriemannian symmetric space $G/G^σ$ which is also an embedding. Our techniques also apply to harmonic Higgs bundles over the unit disk satisfying a certain completeness condition. These techniques also apply to two other families of cyclic Higgs bundles.

papers.title: Negative-Dimensional Simplicial Complexes via the Grothendieck Group of the Join Monoid
papers.abstract: We introduce a framework that extends classical combinatorial and topological notions of simplicial complexes to a setting that includes simplicial complexes of negative dimension. This is achieved by considering the Grothendieck group of the commutative monoid of finite simplicial complexes under the join operation, which provides formal inverses and allows negative-dimensional objects to be defined. Within this group we adapt standard invariants such as $f$- and $h$-vectors, their corresponding polynomials, and the Euler characteristic. The same construction naturally endows the Grothendieck group with an Alexandroff topology. We show that this space is universal for finite topological spaces, and consequently the associated ordered simplicial complex is universal within its class.

papers.title: Flagged Grothendieck enumerators and ribbon decomposition determinants
papers.abstract: We establish Hamel--Goulden-type ribbon decomposition determinantal formulas for a new class of symmetric functions called flagged Grothendieck enumerators. In particular, these functions generalize both canonical refined stable Grothendieck polynomials and their duals. The proof uses Talaska's formula via flows on planar lattice graphs with systems of paths and cycles.

papers.title: Composite local observables of sine-Gordon via stochastic analysis
papers.abstract: We develop a rigorous framework for the description of general local composite observables in Euclidean quantum field theories. The approach is nonperturbative and combines renormalisation group ideas with techniques of stochastic analysis. Via renormalisation dictated by sufficiently precise approximate solution theory of corresponding flow equations, we construct various local observables of the sine-Gordon model on the full space up to $β^2<6π$, including highly singular ones such as vertex fields $\exp(iαφ(y))$ in the optimal Wick regime $|\operatorname{Re}(α)|<4π/β$ and derivatives of arbitrarily high order, i.e. $\partial^μφ(y)$ for any multiindex $μ\in \mathbb{N}^2_0$. Applications of the approach include a direct proof of smoothness of observable-inserted correlation functions, and verification that the constructed objects satisfy a version of the prefactorization algebra axioms adapted to our setting.

papers.title: Irrationality and Noether--Lefschetz loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is twofold. First, we construct examples of families of surfaces where the locus of points in the base with constant degree of irrationality is not constructible. Second, we explore the notion of gonality loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces, which are characterized by the existence of a smooth curve with fixed gonality. Among various results, we prove that polarized gonality loci are always unions of Noether--Lefschetz divisors.

papers.title: Intermediate Growth and Rigidity in Primitive Circulant Spectral Algebras
papers.abstract: At prime graph orders, the complete nontrivial and primitive Fourier spectra of a circulant coincide. We show that this agreement conceals a strong algebraic separation when the graph order varies. For any nonempty finite jump set $S$, let $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ be the algebra of arithmetic functions obtained by evaluating symmetric power sums on the primitive spectrum, filtered by power-sum weight. Removing the common Euler-totient term gives a reduced, locally finite algebra $B_S$, and we prove a filtration-preserving isomorphism $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}\cong B_S[T_2]$. Thus $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ is non-Noetherian and has Krull dimension one. Its filtered dimensions satisfy $\exp(c_S\sqrt{D/\log D})\leq ρ_S^{\mathrm{prim}}(D) \leq\exp(C_S\sqrt D)$ for large $D$, and its associated-graded Hilbert series is nonrational. Despite agreement on every prime order, the primitive and full spectral evaluation algebras intersect only in $\mathbb{Q}$. More strongly, no nonconstant primitive spectral function is eventually quasirational on residue classes. We give an exact finite-matrix rank formula and determine the quotient obtained by restricting to integers with large prime factors.

papers.title: Universal Invariants for $\gcd(n^k-1,n!-1)>1$
papers.abstract: For integers $k\geq2$ and $λ_1,λ_2\in\{-1,+1\}$, let $S_k^{λ_1,λ_2}:=\{n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0,1\}:\gcd(n^k+λ_1,n!+λ_2)>1\}$. This family arose from a MathOverflow problem concerning the existence of integers $n$ satisfying $\gcd(n^2+1,n!+1)>1$ and from the subsequent question of whether arbitrarily many, but finitely many, solutions can be obtained by varying the exponent and the signs. We concentrate on the case $λ_1=λ_2=-1$ and introduce the notion of a universal invariant for an odd prime $p$, namely an integer $n\geq2$ such that $\gcd(n^{p\cdot m}-1,n!-1)>1$ for every integer $m\geq1$. We prove that this condition is equivalent to $\gcd(n^p-1,n!-1)>1$, characterize the possible prime divisors in terms of roots of unity over finite fields, and recall an explicit construction due to Jonathan Love that yields a universal invariant for every odd prime $p\geq5$, with the cubic case treated separately. As an application, we prove that $|S_k^{-1,-1}|\geqω_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ for every integer $k\geq2$, where $ω_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ denotes the number of distinct odd prime divisors of $k$. Hence, the cardinalities of these sets are unbounded as $k$ varies. This lower bound is deliberately coarse and constructive, as it is obtained by considering only universal invariants; stronger general lower bounds are obtained by different constructions. We also discuss minimal universal invariants, their persistent common divisors, the special structure of the cubic case, and a heuristic due to Will Sawin suggesting that there may be infinitely many cubic universal invariants, although the known examples are exceptionally sparse. Whether $S_k^{-1,-1}$ is finite or infinite for any fixed exponent $k\geq3$ remains an open problem.

papers.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--Păun, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact Kähler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.

papers.title: From Worst-Case to Smoothed Complexity in Continuous Optimization
papers.abstract: Worst-case complexity bounds often fail to reflect the practical performance of optimization algorithms, while average-case complexity heavily relies on the distribution of the input. In this work, we develop a smoothed-analysis framework for classical continuous optimization algorithms by studying their behaviour on random perturbations of arbitrary functions. Our main contribution is to apply methods suited for non-degenerate functions to perturbations of degenerate functions, thereby recovering the faster best-known rates for the non-degenerate class. We derive smoothed complexity guarantees for several standard methods, including (Accelerated) Gradient Descent, Conjugate Gradient, and Newton-type methods, under various settings including nonconvex ones, and show that these bounds can substantially improve upon their worst-case guarantees, bringing them closer to the practical behaviour of the respective methods.

papers.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling. Further, we investigate the properties of orthogonally bipolar polytopes, their characterization, and their application to tilings: in dimension three, the cutouts of $P$ by the orthogonal projections of $B$ onto its faces tile $P$ by orthogonally bipolar polytopes exactly when every such projection lies in the relative interior of its face. Finally, we propose an interpretation of the topic in political science.

papers.title: Geodesically Semiconvex Approximations in the Wasserstein Space and Applications to Flow Interchange
papers.abstract: We study the approximation of functionals by geodesically semiconvex functionals in the Wasserstein space, with applications to dissipation estimates along the Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme. For the potential and interaction energies, the approximation problem reduces to approximate the underlying potentials in Euclidean space. For the internal energies, we construct approximations by decomposing truncated functionals into differences of geodesically convex functionals and applying Moreau-Yosida regularization to the second component. Under suitable assumptions, we establish strong quantitative convergence of the gradient of the first variation in weighted \(L^2\) space. These approximations may enable us to obtain dissipation estimates along the JKO scheme for functionals that are not geodesically semiconvex. We illustrate this approach by deriving an \(L^{m+1}\) bound for the JKO scheme of fast diffusion equation, and by establishing internal energy dissipation for the JKO scheme of Fokker-Planck equation.

papers.title: Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and its topological floor
papers.abstract: The zero-point energy of an $LC$ circuit measures the polarization fluctuation of an insulator coupled to it. In a crystal this fluctuation is the bulk quantum weight $K_{\rm bulk}$, which the Chern number $C$ bounds below by $|C|$. We show that a finite Chern flake adds an edge term that survives as the flake grows. The low-frequency transitions of its chiral edge have squared dipole matrix elements that sum to an edge weight $K_{\rm edge}\ge |C|$ per unit area, a floor that follows from the positive absorption of both circular polarizations and the known cancellation of circular dichroism between edge and bulk. At weak coupling, which a growing flake eventually leaves, a circuit slower than the edge modes reads $K_{\rm bulk}+K_{\rm edge}$, averaged over two field directions, and a faster one approaches $K_{\rm bulk}$, so the reading depends on whether the flake is made large or the circuit slow first. In exact free-fermion calculations on lattice flakes with $|C|=1$ and 2 the summed circular dichroism of the edge sector extrapolates to $|C|$ in magnitude, so that the floor is $|C|$. Above the floor, each edge channel adds a number fixed by the boundary shape and its edge velocities, which square and rectangular lattice flakes with one channel follow to within 0.003, while the circular dichroism counts only the net chirality. The avoided crossing of the circuit with the edge mode gives the edge weight in units of the Hall conductance quantum, up to a geometric factor of the capacitor.

papers.title: A Symmetrization for Almost Symmetric Numerical Semigroups
papers.abstract: We characterize almost symmetric numerical semigroups in terms of their associated Young diagrams, showing that almost symmetry is equivalent to a simple numerical identity relating the genus, the type, and the number of small elements, and also to a combinatorial condition on the hook lengths of the diagram. We then introduce a symmetrization procedure that associates with each almost symmetric numerical semigroup a symmetric numerical set. This yields a map from the set of almost symmetric numerical semigroups to the set of symmetric numerical sets. We also present experimental data on the image of this map and on the proportion of its elements that are numerical semigroups. The results show, in particular, that the map is far from injective and that its image contains many numerical sets that are not semigroups.

papers.title: The Isoperimetric Flow and Synthetic Scalar Curvature for Causal Variational Principles
papers.abstract: An isoperimetric flow is introduced in the setting of causal variational principles. Describing the whole space by the support of a minimizing measure, we define an area functional on subsets by a surface layer integral. Mean curvature is defined via the first variation of this area functional. Using the method of minimizing movement, the isoperimetric flow is constructed as a Lipschitz curve of measures with prescribed volume change. As illustrating examples, we introduce and analyze ``smeared variants'' of the mean curvature flow in Euclidean space and on a Riemannian manifold. In these examples, it is shown that our area functional coincides with the usual area up to specified curvature corrections. As an application of our general results, by analyzing the volume and area of small isoperimetric balls, we introduce notions of local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature.

papers.title: On the geometry of Gaussian Mean Shift Detection
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of detecting a shift in the mean of a standard Gaussian random vector, where the direction of the shift belongs to an arbitrary subset $T$ of the Euclidean unit sphere. We introduce a correlation functional $κ(T)$ and establish a general lower bound on the detection radius in terms of this functional. We identify regularity conditions under which this lower bound is optimal up to an absolute constant. As an application, we recover some well-known results in the literature such as the detection radius for $s$-sparse unit vectors.

papers.title: Scattering Resonances of Plane-Embedded Cavities: A Finite Element DtN Approach
papers.abstract: While scattering resonances of plane-embedded cavities have wide-ranging engineering applications, numerical results for such configurations remain virtually unexplored. We present an effective finite element approach for computing these resonances. The unbounded domain is truncated using a Dirichlet-to-Neumann(DtN) boundary operator, recasting the problem as the eigenvalue problem of a holomorphic Fredholm operator function. Discretization is carried out using Lagrange finite elements with a truncated DtN expansion, and convergence is rigorously proven using Karma's approximation theory. The resulting non-linear matrix eigenvalue system is computed using a multi-step parallel spectral indicator method. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical predictions and provide benchmark solutions for future investigations.

papers.title: Regularity via subequations
papers.abstract: Is there a unified theory of a priori estimates for purely second-order constant coefficient elliptic PDE? A strong indication that such a theory exists is provided by the foundational a priori estimates of Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck (1984) and Trudinger (1995) that treated many equations, yet left out many others. This article develops such a unified theory based on Harvey--Lawson's theory of subequations, the aforementioned a priori estimates, and some new ingredients. Serendipitously, this also solves a problem posed by Nirenberg (2007). In addition to unifying all previously known such estimates, we find a vast number of new a priori estimates (e.g., spanning real, complex, quaternionic, $G_2$, among other natural equations, and even differential inclusions that generalize PDEs).

papers.title: The zero-sum constant $\mathsf{s}_p^*$ and inverse problem
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime. We denote by $\mathsf{s}_{p}^{*}$ the smallest integer $l$ such that, out of any given $l$ integers coprime with $p$, one can select $p$ integers satisfying that the sum of the $p$ integers is a multiple of $p$, but not a multiple of $p^{2}$. It was conjectured that $\mathsf{s}_p^*=2p+1$. In this paper we prove this conjecture and solve the corresponding inverse problem. More precisely, we characterize all sequences of $2p$ integers coprime to $p$ in which every $p$-term subsequence with sum a multiple of $p$ also has sum a multiple of $p^2$.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Operator Maps in Optimal Liquidation
papers.abstract: We analyze the solution map of a optimal execution problem in which price dynamics are subject to a general transient impact kernel. Given the structure of the optimal trading strategy derived by Abi Jaber and Neuman in \cite{https://doi.org/10.1111/mafi.12465}, we show that the strategy is locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the underlying model parameters governing temporary and transient price impact as well as the fundamental price process. Continuity of this map justifies the application of neural-net based approximations which take model parameters as inputs. We propose a method generating samples of the transient price impact kernel for the purposes of creating training data, and a method of projecting the kernel to a finite dimensional representation appropriate for input to a neural net, and a dimensional reduction based on the relationship between inventory and trade signal. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the trained neural net and use it to quantify the potential financial costs associated with misspecifying the transient impact kernel.

papers.title: On Federated Averaging with Partial Participation under a General Variance Condition
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the convergence of Federated Averaging (FedAvg) with partial participation under a general variance condition. In each communication round, the server samples $S$ of the $n$ clients uniformly at random without replacement. The stochastic gradients are assumed to satisfy the so-called ABC condition, which allows their variance to grow with the local objective gaps. For smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish a finite-time stationarity bound in terms of the heterogeneity measure $σ_f^\star:=f^\star-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i^\star$ and the client sampling factor $I_S:=(n-S)/(n-1)$. Here, $f^\star$ and $f_i^\star$ denote the infima of the global average objective and client $i$'s local objective, respectively. The bound exhibits a linear speedup in the number of sampled clients $S$ and recovers the full-participation result when $S=n$. Under diminishing stepsizes, we further prove that the gradient norm converges to zero both in expectation and almost surely. Notably, compared with existing analyses of FedAvg with partial participation, our results require no additional data heterogeneity assumption such as bounded gradient dissimilarity (BGD), and the sampling-induced term in our bound is not amplified by the number of local updates at the leading order. The importance of removing the BGD assumption is illustrated by an example that is smooth and lower bounded but violates BGD, yet is covered by our analysis.

papers.title: Generic singularity formation in two-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
papers.abstract: On bounded domains, the mass-conserving parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system admits smooth equilibria at every mass. Nevertheless, we prove that on a disk, an open dense set of positive initial densities leads to finite-time blow-up or infinite-time grow-up whenever the effective mass is at least the critical value $4π$. This threshold is sharp: below $4π$, every solution exists globally, remains uniformly bounded, and converges to a smooth equilibrium. At the critical mass, all solutions are global, while infinite-time grow-up accompanied by boundary concentration is generic. We extend the result to other bounded planar domains and closed surfaces, obtaining sharp mass thresholds for the round sphere and the flat square torus.

papers.title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
papers.abstract: This work summarizes some updates to the ropelength problem, concerning the shortest possible contour length of a unit-thickness knot, that were derived with the assistance of ChatGPT-5.6 Luna. The first of two main results is that the universal lower bound for a knot with crossing number C has been improved from $L\geq1.105C^{3/4}$ to $L\geq2.0996C^{3/4}$, achieved by further separating local and global terms in an optimization integral. The second main result is a bound relating ropelength to stick number (s), such that $L\geqπ(s-1)$. This implies stronger lower bounds for the ropelengths of at least 41 torus knots, and a specific class of pretzel knots. Other results include an improved packing-based lower bound for T(Q,Q) links and an optimized standard parameterization for torus knots. There were many problems for which the LLM was unable to render assistance, for example in reducing the numerical coefficients or scalings of known universal upper bounds.

papers.title: Global existence and sharp decay rates of weak solutions for the 2D inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress tensor diffusion
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the global existence and optimal decay rates of weak solutions to a two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress diffusion. For $\frac{1}{2}<β<1$, by virtue of energy estimates and compactness arguments, we establish the existence of global weak solutions with $(u,τ)\in H^{1}\times (H^{1}\cap L^{\infty})$. Moreover, based on the Littlewood-Paley decomposition theory and the improved Fourier splitting method, we derive the optimal decay rates. In particular, by constructing a suitable low-frequency energy functional and exploiting the dissipation mechanism of the coupled system, we obtain the optimal $L^\infty$ decay rate for the stress tensor.

papers.title: Counting Rational Points on Cayley's Cubic Surface
papers.abstract: We study rational points of bounded maximum-coordinate height on the split four-nodal Cayley cubic surface over \(\mathbb Q\), with its nine lines removed. Writing \(U\) for this open subset and \(N_U(B)\) for its counting function, we establish \[ N_U(B)\sim c_{\mathrm{Peyre}}B(\log B)^6. \] The argument starts from the universal-torsor parametrization and combines two counting methods over complementary ranges of the auxiliary variables. The two-dimensional lattice count is controlled by averages of reciprocal shortest-vector lengths and character-moment bounds, while Poisson summation treats the complementary parameter range. The main contribution is the uniform control needed to combine these methods when the size parameters of the auxiliary variables vary independently: the estimates retain every coprimality condition, the original height weight, and the full set of auxiliary tuples contributing to the geometric error. Divisibility estimates without an additional power of the height parameter control the sieve tail and justify removing the sieve after taking the height limit. We track the derivative losses and boundary contributions throughout the summation, and identify the common continuous main term with Peyre's constant by computing the effective-cone volume and the real and finite local densities.

papers.title: The Čech-Stone compactification of the reals and coz-included sublocales
papers.abstract: A new notion of a coz-included sublocale is introduced. It is a necessary condition for a sublocale to be a dense $C$-embedding, and together with the property of being well-embedded, is sufficient. However, although it is clearly a strengthening of coz-ontoness (or z-embeddings), it is incomparable with $C^*$-embeddings as is demonstrated by the Čech-Stone compactification of the real numbers. Motivated by non-trivial spatial examples, this new notion and other weaker variants, such as casi coz-included and relative zero sublocales, are explored and characterized in the point-free setting. As a consequence, new characterizations of several classes of frames, such as perfectly normal and $Oz$ frames, among others, are provided. Besides the lattice theoretic interpretations, there are some interesting topological ramifications.

papers.title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure
papers.abstract: Let $γ$ be a Gaussian measure on the sequence space $\ell_2$ whose mean is zero and whose correlation operator $C_γ$ is a diagonal operator on $\ell_2$. Exact values of the $q$-average linear $n$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q<\infty$ are obtained. We also obtain asymptotic orders of the average linear $n$-width in $\ell_\infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$, and of the probabilistic linear $(n,δ)$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q\le 2$, and for $2<q\le \infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$.

papers.title: Scattering of water waves in presence of a partially immersed obstacle
papers.abstract: We study linear water waves in two dimensions in a fluid of infinite depth containing a fixed, partially immersed obstacle. Under natural geometric assumptions on the wetted boundary, we construct the harmonic lifting and prove that the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator is an unbounded, self-adjoint and non-negative operator on a $L^2$ space. This yields global well-posedness and conservation of energy. We establish the absence of trapped modes and, by a compact perturbation argument, a limiting absorption principle at every positive spectral parameter. Consequently, for all finite energy initial data, the physical local energy tends to zero as $|t|\to\infty$, including in neighborhoods of the obstacle and the contact points. Quantitative resolvent estimates and fractional regularity in the spectral parameter yield algebraic local energy decay for Sobolev initial data in weighted $L^2$ spaces.

papers.title: Classical phase unwrapping enables large-time-step unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization
papers.abstract: For computing molecular energies on early fault-tolerant hardware, unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization (UQKSD) avoids both the deep circuits of quantum phase estimation and the Pauli-term sampling of variational methods by extracting the energies from a projected real-time propagator. At a small time step $τ$, nearly linearly dependent Krylov vectors make the overlap matrix ill-conditioned. Our tests at fixed total evolution time show that additional Krylov vectors then add no accuracy, while the thresholded energy becomes increasingly sensitive to the choice of cutoff. A larger time step improves the conditioning and reduces the Krylov dimension $M$ needed for a target accuracy, but the energies are then known only modulo $2π/τ$. We present Classical Unwrapping for Resolving Eigenvalues (CURE-QKSD), a classical post-processing method that leaves the UQKSD circuits and generalized eigenvalue problem unchanged and recovers the missing multiples of $2π/τ$ from phase-consistency landscapes of one or, when needed, two UQKSD runs. In noiseless tests on six molecules with 12--20 qubits, all 28 targeted energies are recovered in their aliased regimes with final errors of at most $1.1\times10^{-7}$~Ha. Under Gaussian noise with $σ=10^{-4}$, the median error of the ground or first excited state reaches chemical accuracy at large aliased time steps with $M=20$--$65$, whereas uncorrected principal-branch energies are off by $0.7$--$115$~Ha. CURE-QKSD therefore makes aliased time steps usable for UQKSD calculations with smaller, better-conditioned Krylov bases.

papers.title: $\varphi$-symmetric Sasakian Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We study Sasakian Lie algebras with trivial centre for which the adjoint operator $\mathrm{ad}_ξ$ associated to the Reeb vector field $ξ$ has two-dimensional image. Their structure is governed by a Kähler-exact Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}_1$ and a vector $H_0\in\mathfrak{h}_1$, and the cases $H_0=0$ and $H_0\neq0$ are of a different nature. For $H_0=0$ we prove that the Sasakian structure is $\varphi$-symmetric if and only if $\mathfrak{h}_1$ is locally symmetric. For $H_0\neq0$ and $\mathfrak{h}_1$ solvable, we prove that it is $\varphi$-symmetric if and only if $\mathfrak{h}_1$ is locally symmetric and a natural two-form $ρ_0$ on $\mathfrak{h}_1$ determined by $H_0$ is parallel. The latter condition is equivalent to the vanishing of the mixed root spaces attached to the distinguished root selected by $H_0$ in the associated normal $j$-algebra. As a consequence, every Sasakian Lie algebra in this class of dimension at most seven is $\varphi$-symmetric, which extends a result of Loiudice and Lotta in dimension five. This bound is sharp: in dimension nine we exhibit a Sasakian structure which is not $\varphi$-symmetric, even though its Kähler base is locally symmetric.

papers.title: Monotone Rearrangement for Flattening Weights $F_2$
